info.title: Ambivo CRM API
info.description:
Lead, Contact, Account, Opportunity, and Product management for the Ambivo CRM platform.

## Authentication
All endpoints require a Bearer JWT token in the `Authorization` header.
Obtain a token via the Ambivo authentication flow.

## Response Pattern
All JSON responses follow this convention:
- **Success**: `{ "result": 1, "data": {...} }`
- **Error**: `{ "result": 2, "error_code": "SLUG", "error": { "message": "..." }, "status_code": 200, "request_path": "..." }`

Errors are sent with HTTP 200. Check `result` to tell success from failure.
A response documented here as `400` arrives as HTTP 200 with `result: 2`.
`error_code` is the message upper-cased with spaces turned into underscores.
Some refusals send a bare `{ "result": 2 }` with no message.

## CRUD Action Pattern
Most entity endpoints use a single `POST` endpoint with an `action` field in the request body
to perform create, read, update, and delete operations.
New field values go in `payload`. The record id goes at the top level, named for the entity:
```json
{ "action": "add", "payload": { ... } }
{ "action": "update", "lead_id": "...", "payload": { ... } }
{ "action": "delete", "contact_id": "..." }
{ "action": "get", "account_id": "..." }
```

## Pagination
List endpoints support pagination via query parameters:
- `page_size` — number of records per page (default 30)
- `page_num` — page number (1-indexed)
- `match_filter_dict` — JSON-encoded filter object
- `sort_dict` — JSON-encoded sort object (e.g. `{"created_ts": -1}`)

In list responses, `data.total_count` is the number of rows on this page.
The full match count is the top-level `gross_count`. It is sent on page 1 only.
Search endpoints page with a `last_id` cursor.

## Timestamps
All timestamp fields are **epoch seconds** (integer). A value of `0` means "not set".

## Multi-Currency Money Block

Every Opportunity, Order, OrderLine, Invoice, InvoiceLine, and Product carries a 5-field
money block snapshotted at create time: `currency`, `fx_rate`, `fx_rate_date`,
`base_<amount-field>`, `fx_pending`. For single-currency tenants
(`record.currency == tenant.currency`), `fx_rate=1.0` and `base_*` mirrors equal native —
zero behavior change. For multi-currency tenants, the `base_*` mirror is in the tenant's
functional currency for consolidated reporting.

### 🛑 Aggregation rule for ALL future development

Any new MongoDB aggregation, chart, dashboard, or report that sums/averages a monetary
field on Opp / Order / OrderLine / Invoice / InvoiceLine **must** use the `$ifNull`
coalesce pattern. Plain `$<field>` references will silently mix currencies the moment
a tenant has any foreign-currency record.

```python
# Opportunity:
{"$sum": {"$ifNull": ["$base_value_of_sale", "$value_of_sale", 0]}}
{"$sum": {"$ifNull": ["$base_estimated_value_of_sale", "$estimated_value_of_sale", 0]}}

# Order / Invoice header:
{"$sum": {"$ifNull": ["$base_total_amount", "$total_amount", 0]}}
{"$sum": {"$ifNull": ["$base_balance", "$balance", 0]}}

# OrderLine / InvoiceLine (after $unwind):
{"$sum": {"$ifNull": ["$order_line_list.base_amount", "$order_line_list.amount", 0]}}
```

The pattern works identically for `$avg`, `$min`, `$max`. Three-arg `$ifNull` ensures
legacy records (no `base_*` field) and `fx_pending=true` records (`base_*=null`) both
fall through to the native field — no records silently drop from totals.

**Anti-patterns** (will break multi-currency consolidation):
- `{"$sum": "$value_of_sale"}`
- `{"$sum": {"$ifNull": ["$value_of_sale", 0]}}`
- `{"$sum": "$base_value_of_sale"}` (drops legacy/fx_pending records)

For full design + invariants see `docs/core-models/data-models.md` and
`docs/core-models/opportunity-api.md`. Regression-tested by
`scripts/audit_single_currency_no_drift.py` — run after any change that touches
monetary aggregation.

### ⚠️ FX rate convention — direct quote (Wise-style)

The system's only convention for `fx_rate`:

> **Rate is "units of TO per 1 unit of FROM."**
> Direction: `from = record.currency` (transaction), `to = tenant.currency` (base).
> Math: `base_amount = native_amount × fx_rate`.

This matches Wise, ECB, OpenExchangeRates, Fixer, Currencylayer, and most major FX APIs.
Concrete: for a `EUR` record on a `USD` tenant when 1 EUR ≈ 1.18 USD, the cached rate
(and the manual override-table key `"EUR->USD"`) holds `1.18`, and a 1000 EUR Opp saves
as `base_value_of_sale = 1000 × 1.18 = 1180.00` USD.

**This is the OPPOSITE of NetSuite's classic indirect-quote convention** (where rate is
"units of FROM per 1 unit of TO" and you'd divide). If a future engineer ever hooks up
an FX provider that uses NetSuite's convention, they **MUST invert the rate before
calling `FxService.cache_rate`** — otherwise a 1000 EUR Opp on a USD tenant would be
saved as `base_value_of_sale = 1000 / 1.18 ≈ 847` USD (half the right answer; the error
compounds as `rate²`).

```python
# WRONG — cached an indirect quote ("1 USD = 0.847 EUR"):
fx.cache_rate("EUR", "USD", 0.847)

# RIGHT — convert to direct quote first:
fx.cache_rate("EUR", "USD", 1 / 0.847)   # → 1.180 = "1 EUR = 1.180 USD"
```

The same applies to manual overrides set by tenant admins via `tenant.fx_rate_overrides`.
UI copy on the tenant settings page should make this explicit: *"Enter how many [TO]
you get for 1 [FROM]."*

## Site-Code Partition (Multi-Office Support)

Every Lead, Contact, Account, Opportunity, Order, Invoice, and Task carries a scalar
`site_code` field that partitions the record by office / business unit within a single
tenant. The field is **immutable at create** — once stamped, it never changes through
the normal update API.

### Three layers

| Layer | Field | Job |
|---|---|---|
| Registry | `tenant.site_list[].code` | Admin-controlled list of valid site codes |
| Input | `role.open_assignment_group_code` (OAG) | Drives auto-default at create; derives viewer's site set at read time |
| Partition | `<record>.site_code` | The immutable per-record tag |

Each `tenant.site_list[]` entry has exactly one `code` plus `is_active` (boolean) and
`default_owner_userid` (string). Multiple roles MAY carry the same OAG code, and a user
MAY hold multiple roles → up to N distinct codes via their role assignments.

### Create-time stamping (4-tier precedence)

`site_code` is resolved by `UserService._resolve_site_code_for_new_record` in every
`manage_*` create path (gated by `if action == "add":` — updates never touch the field):

1. **Explicit `payload.site_code`** — always wins.
2. **Lineage inheritance** from parent records. Lead→(none); Contact→(source_lead → account);
   Account→(none); Opportunity→(contact → account); Order→(opportunity → contact → account);
   Invoice→(order → opportunity → contact → account); Task→(subject entity per `subject_type`).
3. **Auto-default** to the creator's sole OAG code, but only when **all three** hold:
   (a) creator has exactly one non-empty OAG code, (b) tenant has exactly one active
   registered site, (c) the two codes are equal. A singleton mismatch (codes differ)
   logs a warning and falls through to tier 4.
4. **Empty string** — the "all-for-one" default. Visible to everyone in the tenant.

Whatever resolves passes through `validate_site_code` per `tenant.site_code_enforcement`:
- `off` (default): code accepted as-is, no validation
- `warn`: unknown code logs a warning but write proceeds
- `required`: unknown code raises `InvalidDataException` (HTTP 400, `error_code=SITE_CODE_NOT_REGISTERED`)

Empty `site_code` is always permitted regardless of mode — only non-empty unknown codes trip enforcement.

### Read-time visibility

Records are matched when `site_code ∈ viewer's site set` OR `site_code` is null/empty
(back-compat — "all-for-one"). Viewers with no OAG-bearing roles see everything (admin /
cross-cutting interpretation — no site constraint applied). Analytics callers that pass
`tenant_scope=True` bypass site partition entirely.

Today the partition is **auto-enforced** in:
- The lead/contact "open" peer-visibility tabs (`UserProspectByStatusHandler`).
- The task list path (`UserService.get_user_tasks`), with a guard preserving the legacy
  "no peer visibility for OAG-less viewers" semantic (tasks are personal — surfacing
  every "assigned" task to an unscoped viewer would over-share).

For Opportunity / Order / Invoice / Account list endpoints, the partition is **user-driven** —
pass `match_filter_dict.site_code = "X"` in the list query to filter to one office.

### Filtering by site_code

Any list endpoint that accepts `match_filter_dict` accepts `site_code` as a key:

```json
GET /user/opportunities/manage?match_filter_dict={"site_code": "HB"}
GET /user/orders/manage?match_filter_dict={"site_code": "OA"}
GET /user/invoices/manage?match_filter_dict={"site_code": "antksh"}
GET /entity/data?entity_type=account&match_filter_dict={"site_code": "endvr"}
```

To list records that have NO site_code (the all-for-one bucket), pass an empty string:
```json
{"site_code": ""}
```

To list records across multiple offices a user belongs to, use `$in`:
```json
{"site_code": {"$in": ["HB", "OA"]}}
```

tags.name: Leads
tags.description: Lead management — capture, qualify, convert, and track sales leads

tags.name: Contacts
tags.description: Contact management — people associated with accounts and opportunities

tags.name: Accounts
tags.description: Account management — companies, vendors, partners, and other organizations

tags.name: Opportunities
tags.description: Opportunity management — sales pipeline tracking and deal management

tags.name: Orders
tags.description: Sales order management — fulfillment stages and order lifecycle

tags.name: Invoices
tags.description: Invoice management — billing stages and invoice lifecycle

tags.name: InstalledBase
tags.description: Installed Base — durable, termed instances a tenant sells or buys (licence, subscription, equipment warranty, service/maintenance contract). Tracks the term, lifecycle, contract value, install location and renewal chain. A nightly sweep drives renewal reminders and the active→expiring→renewed/ expired lifecycle. `direction` (sold|purchased) serves both sell-side (customer, A/R, churn risk) and buy-side (vendor, A/P, service-lapse risk).

tags.name: PurchaseOrders
tags.description: Purchase Orders — buy-side procurement (the tenant purchases from a vendor, typically to renew a purchased installed-base licence/AMC/warranty). Line items + money/FX like a sales Order, with a single-state approval gate and settlement to a Bill. Optional entity — only for tenants who route renewals through procurement.

tags.name: Documents
tags.description:
Document generation — render branded PDFs (quotes, invoices, proposals) from CRM
records (order / invoice / opportunity) using HTML/Jinja templates, manage
per-tenant templates (which override the read-only Ambivo starters), and send
generated quotes/proposals into the native e-sign pipeline. Responses use the
`write_success` / `write_error_response` convention (`result: 1` with merged keys,
or the `CanonicalError` envelope), not the CRM `msg_list` shape.

tags.name: Products
tags.description: Product catalog — items, services, and categories

tags.name: User Access Code
tags.description:
Payment access code (PIN) management. Users set a 4-6 digit numeric PIN that serves
as a second verification layer before sensitive financial operations (e.g. Wise payments)
in Ambivo Books. The PIN is bcrypt-hashed and stored on the User document in MongoDB.
Lockout occurs after 5 failed attempts (15-minute cooldown).

tags.name: Password Verification
tags.description:
Authenticated password verification endpoint. Allows a logged-in user to confirm
their current password (e.g. before sensitive account changes). Rate limited to
5 requests per hour per user via Redis-based rate limiter.

tags.name: User Management
tags.description:
User registration, login, email confirmation, password management, and session handling.
Covers the full user lifecycle: self-registration, admin user creation, email/password login,
OAuth login (Google/Microsoft), OTP login (SMS), MFA verification, JWT token resolution,
and internal token authentication for cross-module use.

tags.name: Notifications
tags.description:
Holistic notification management — send, list, read, and delete user notifications.
The POST endpoint enables multi-channel notification delivery (in-app, push, email, SMS)
in a single API call. External systems authenticate with a user Bearer token to trigger
automation-style notifications.

tags.name: Calendar
tags.description:
Calendar management — list calendars, create/update/delete events (including recurring),
query free slots, sync Google and Microsoft calendars, and manage appointment payments/refunds.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description:
Task management — create, assign, track, and complete tasks.
Tasks can be linked to entities (leads, contacts, accounts, opportunities) via subject/subject_type.
Supports priorities, status workflow, comments, attachments, and calendar event integration.

tags.name: Task Sequences
tags.description:
Task sequence management — define ordered sequences of task templates.
Each sequence contains a list of task templates with step ordering, actions,
and due date offsets. Used to automate multi-step workflows.

tags.name: Task Templates
tags.description:
Standalone task template management — CRUD for reusable task blueprints stored
in the `user_task_template` collection. Templates define the "shape" of a task
(name, action, automation flags, calendar-event creation intent, defaults) so
the same definition can be reused across sequences, playbooks, and ad-hoc task
creation.

### Route surface
| Route | Methods | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/user_task_template` | GET / POST / PUT / DELETE | List or fetch single via `?template_id=`; POST single object OR array for bulk; PUT requires `template_id` in body; DELETE requires `template_id` query param. |
| `/user_task_template/search` | GET | Regex search over `name` + `description`; pass `q` or `search_query`. |
| `/user_task_template/bulk` | POST | Bulk create — body MUST be a JSON array. |
| `/user_task_template/{template_id}` | GET / PUT / DELETE | REST-style operations on a single template by its 24-hex ObjectId. |

### Permissions
Each method enforces `@privilege_required(module='task_template', ...)` with
the matching CRUD letter (`R` for GET, `C` for POST, `U` for PUT, `D` for
DELETE). All operations are tenant-scoped — cross-tenant access returns
"not found" even if the id is valid in another tenant.

### Relationship to Task Sequences
Task Sequences embed their own `task_template_list` inline (see the
`TaskTemplateEntry` schema). The standalone templates managed by this group
are a separate collection — use them for shared libraries of task blueprints
that sequences, playbooks, or manual flows can reference.

tags.name: Playbooks
tags.description:
Playbook management — define, automate, and track entity-driven follow-up sequences.
A playbook is a configurable list of activities (checklists + automated workflows) organized
by entity stage. When an entity's status matches a trigger status, the PlaybookExecutorService
enrolls it and fires automated activities (SMS, email, notifications, calendar events) via the
AI Workflow System. Supports delayed scheduling, skip-if-replied guards, calendar event creation
on the entity owner's calendar, and two-pass template interpolation for personalized messages.

tags.name: Playbook Execution Logs
tags.description:
Playbook execution log management — track, query, and manage records of playbook step executions.
Each log entry records what activity was executed, for which entity, the delivery status,
workflow execution ID, calendar event ID, and the owner who performed or received the action.

tags.name: Entity Status Values
tags.description:
Unified endpoint for retrieving valid status/stage values for any entity type.
Returns the allowed values for lead status, contact status, account status,
opportunity stage, order stage, invoice stage, task status, bill stage, and payment status.

For `opportunity / order / invoice / lead / contact / account / task` the response merges
tenant-defined **custom** status/stage values (managed via `/tenant/entity-custom-stages`)
with the seeded list. Custom values do NOT inherit built-in business logic
(e.g. `closed_won` -> order creation, lead `disqualified` blocks conversion);
they're "open" and trigger no automation unless a workflow targets them.

Supports both JWT and internal service-to-service authentication.

tags.name: Entity Custom Stages
tags.description:
Tenant-defined custom status/stage values that augment the seeded enums for
Opportunity / Order / Invoice / Lead / Contact / Account / Task. Stored in a
single collection (`entity_custom_stages`) striped by
`(tenant_id, entity_type, key)`.

**Augment-only contract** — seeded values keep all built-in business logic
(closed_won creates an order, contact `customer` is auto-set when an opp wins,
lead `disqualified` blocks conversion to contact, etc.). Custom values are
"open" by definition: pickers and kanbans surface them, but no automation
fires off them. To act on a custom value, build a workflow in
`ai_workflow_system`.

Reads via `GET /entity/status-values?entity_type=...` automatically merge
seeded + tenant active customs. Write operations (add/update/delete) require
tenant-admin permission; reads require any authenticated user.

tags.name: SMS
tags.description:
Direct SMS sending endpoints — queue or send an SMS message via Telnyx.

These endpoints send SMS messages directly. They are distinct from
`/user/notifications/manage` (which includes SMS as one optional channel
in a multi-channel notification) and `/admin/sms/verifications` (OTP login).

### Which endpoint to use

| Endpoint | Auth | Use Case |
|----------|------|----------|
| `POST /messages/send_sms` | User JWT | Simple fire-and-forget SMS queuing. Specify both `from_number` and `to_number` explicitly. No conversation room or tracking. |
| `POST /phone/user/send_sms` | User JWT | Softphone user sending SMS from their assigned SIP number. Creates a client conversation room for bidirectional messaging. Supports attachments. Rate limited (2 req / 90 s). |
| `POST /admin/send_sms` | Superadmin JWT | System-level SMS on behalf of any tenant. Checks blocked-number list. Source defaults to tenant dialer phone. Max 304 characters. |
| `POST /bot/send_sms` | User JWT (bot owner) | Send SMS from a bot's assigned phone number. The calling user must own a bot with a phone number. |

### SMS Provider
All endpoints ultimately send via **Telnyx** messaging API.

tags.name: Phone
tags.description:
Phone-number utility endpoints. Today this group exposes a single
validation/lookup endpoint that combines an offline libphonenumber
parse with an optional live Telnyx number_lookup. Future routes that
operate on raw phone numbers (rather than CDRs, SIP, or SMS) belong
here. SMS-sending endpoints live under the `SMS` tag; CDR / SIP /
tenant-number routes are exposed elsewhere in the API and are not
currently documented here.

tags.name: Research Pipeline
tags.description:
Heavyweight multi-stage research orchestration that produces structured
deliverables (JSON report + optional PDF + optional HTML slide deck +
optional knowledge-base ingestion). Runs asynchronously in a Celery
worker; typical wall-clock is 3–15 minutes for a full 5-stage run.

Use this when you need a shareable artifact — briefing deck, branded
PDF, sales dossier. For chat-turn answers under 2 minutes, use
Knowledge Synthesis (`/kh/chat/async`) instead; both share the same
underlying agents but differ in orchestration and output shape.

### Pipeline stages

1. **Strategic research** — web search across configured providers to
   discover sources relevant to the topic.
2. **Scraping** — Jina Reader / Firecrawl pulls full content from
   top-ranked URLs (up to `max_sources`).
3. **Synthesis** — an LLM reads the scraped content and produces the
   structured report (title, executive summary, headings, key points,
   sources with relevance).
4. **Professional report generation** — emits the canonical JSON report
   and optionally a branded PDF via reportlab.
5. **Presentation (optional)** — generates an HTML slide deck when
   `presentation_enabled: true`.
6. **Knowledge-base ingestion (optional)** — writes the generated
   artifacts back into a tenant Qdrant collection when
   `knowledge_base_enabled: true`.

### Artifacts

Every run emits a JSON report. PDF, HTML slides, KB collections, and
scraped source dumps are produced per request configuration. All
artifacts are uploaded to S3 and surfaced with presigned URLs in the
workflow's `artifacts` dict (`json_reports`, `pdf_reports`,
`html_presentations`, `scraped_files`, `knowledge_base_collections`).

### Citations and generation date

Every report includes a `metadata.generated_at` ISO timestamp and, when
`include_citations: true` (the default), a `sources` array listing every
URL actually scraped during the run. The PDF's "Data Sources &
Attribution" appendix renders the same list as clickable links plus a
prominent "Report generated on <date>" header. Set `include_citations:
false` to produce an executive-summary-only output without the source
attribution — the generation timestamp still remains in metadata and on
the PDF cover.

The sources list is **force-merged from the scraper's actual output**
— the LLM cannot cherry-pick which sources to credit, and sources that
the LLM invents but weren't actually scraped are dropped (anti-
hallucination guard). The count in `metadata.sources_processed`
reflects the ground truth from the scraping stage.

### Async lifecycle

1. `POST /kh/research` — returns `{workflow_id, status: "created",
   estimated_completion_minutes}` in <1 s.
2. `GET /kh/research/{workflow_id}` — poll until `status == "completed"`
   or `"failed"`. Typical poll cadence: every 10–30 s.
3. `GET /kh/research/{workflow_id}/artifacts` — fetch the artifact
   bundle with presigned S3 URLs.
4. `DELETE /kh/research/{workflow_id}` — cancel a running workflow.

### Caching

Identical topics (same normalized topic + max_sources + output_format)
return cached workflows within 7 days by default. Set `force_refresh:
true` to bypass the cache.

tags.name: Knowledge Synthesis
tags.description:
Multi-source research synthesis over the vectordbapi.ambivo.com gateway.
Submits a natural-language query, orchestrates web search + content scraping +
knowledge base lookups across multiple providers in parallel, and returns a
synthesized prose answer grounded in real sources.

Used by CRM for on-demand lead/account/opportunity research ("brief me on this
prospect before the call"), competitive-landscape lookups, and inline
context enrichment. The agent-level wrapper is documented at
`docs/agents/research_agent.md` in the ambivo_api repo; this spec documents
the direct HTTP surface so non-agent callers (batch jobs, mobile clients,
server-side integrations) can use it.

### Three call shapes — pick by client constraint

| Shape | Endpoint | Max wall-clock | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sync** | `POST /kh/chat` with `streaming:"false"` | ~120 s (gateway cutoff) | Simple HTTP clients, fast queries |
| **SSE streaming** | `POST /kh/chat` with `streaming:"true"` | Unlimited (20 s heartbeat) | Chat UIs rendering progress |
| **Async (submit + poll)** | `POST /kh/chat/async` + `GET /kh/chat/async/{job_id}` | Unlimited (Celery, 1 h job TTL) | Server-to-server, long queries, mobile |

All three share the same underlying agents (`WebSearchAgent`, `WebScraperAgent`,
`KnowledgeBaseAgent`, `KnowledgeSynthesisAgent`). The async path is the default
recommendation for CRM clients because (a) the 120 s gateway cutoff can bite
under heavy traffic, (b) mobile clients lose SSE connections on backgrounding,
and (c) polling gives the UI a natural "check progress" affordance.

### Knowledge Synthesis vs Research Pipeline

A separate heavier workflow — the **Research Pipeline** (`/pgv/research`) —
produces structured deliverables (title + summary + sections + scored sources,
plus S3 PDF/HTML artifacts) and takes 3–15 minutes. Use synthesis for chat-turn
context; use research pipeline when you want a shareable artifact. Both use the
same underlying agents — the difference is orchestration and output shape.

Empirically on the same topic ("recent advances in quantum error correction"):
- Synthesis: 137 s, 1,714 chars prose
- Research pipeline: 185.7 s, 3,147 chars structured report + 2 scored sources + S3 artifacts

### Job state machine (async path)

```
pending → running → (done | failed | cancelled)
```

`cancelled` can be set externally via `POST /kh/chat/async/{job_id}/cancel` at
any time. The Celery worker re-reads state before its final write and respects
an externally-set `cancelled` status so a client cancel during a long run is
honored rather than stomped by the completing task.

### Auth and ownership

All endpoints require the standard Bearer JWT. The async cancel/list endpoints
additionally enforce per-job ownership server-side: the authenticated
`user_id` + `tenant_id` must match the job's owner. Cross-tenant cancellation
returns `403` even with a valid JWT.

tags.name: Email
tags.description:
Email mailbox management — connect OAuth mailboxes (Google, Microsoft), browse folders,
search/read/send/reply/forward messages, and manage message flags.

### Mailbox Authentication
Most endpoints accept credentials via one of three methods:
- `authorized_mailbox`: Email address of an OAuth-connected mailbox (recommended)
- `email_connection_id`: ID of a running stateful IMAP connection
- `email_creds_dict`: Raw credentials (legacy, for non-OAuth setups)

When `authorized_mailbox` is used, operations are proxied through the email microservice.

### IMAP Search Criteria
The `search_criteria` parameter uses standard IMAP SEARCH syntax:
- `ALL` — all messages
- `UNSEEN` — unread messages
- `FROM "user@example.com"` — messages from a sender
- `SUBJECT "keyword"` — messages with subject keyword
- `SINCE "01-Jan-2026"` — messages since a date
- `BEFORE "01-Feb-2026"` — messages before a date
- Combine: `FROM "user@example.com" SINCE "01-Jan-2026"`

tags.name: Daily Plan
tags.description:
Daily Agent Productivity Plan — an LLM-synthesized, prioritized "what should I work on today"
report for sales/CS agents. The generation runs **asynchronously** in Celery; the endpoint
enqueues the job and returns immediately with a `job_id`. Clients poll
`GET /user/daily_plan/status` for `completed` and a presigned S3 `pdf_url`
(HTML report — styled deep-links into CRM tasks/leads/contacts/accounts).

### When it runs
- **7:00 local, every day** — Celery beat calls `POST /admin/daily_plan/morning_sweep`
  hourly; each run picks the enabled users whose local time is 7:00-7:59 and who
  have no plan yet today (`daily_plan_trigger: "morning"`).
- **On login** — fallback for someone with no plan inside the 4h window
  (`daily_plan_trigger: "login_autogen"`).
- **On request** — `POST /user/daily_plan/generate`.

All three gather the same context in the API; Celery only writes the plan.

### When a plan is ready
- **Push** (type `N009`) with `pdf_url` — every completed plan.
- **Bell + Connecteam + email**, once per user per day (the first completed plan), via
  `/admin/notification/holistic`: title "Your plan for <date>", body = the report link
  and nothing else. Push is off in this call. Guarded by
  `user_notifications.daily_plan_notified_ts`.

### Data sources (records the user currently owns)
- **Recent activity** (`recent_activity`, last 5 days, max 25) — leads (not converted)
  and contacts where the prospect did something, read from the record's typed
  activity log (`comments[].type`): guest card / intake PDF (`pdf_response_store`),
  web form (`system` "Via Widget …"), form again (`weblead_resubmit`), `voicemail`,
  `missed_call`, inbound `sms`, `new_record_created`, `assignment`. Campaign sends
  and other automation are ignored. Each record carries its newest 3 events and
  whether the agent wrote a note after the latest one.
- **Renewals** (`renewals`, max 15) — leases the user sold (primary sales agent) that
  end in 60-75 days, i.e. are in their renewal decision window today. Orders in
  `invoiced` or `paid`. Same window as the Sales Performance renewals tile.
- **Opportunities** with `expected_close_date` in the next 14 days (or already past-due)
  in active stages: `draft`, `discovery`, `prospecting`, `developing`, `negotiation_review`
- **Tasks** overdue (last 30 days; older ones reported as `counts.older_overdue_tasks`)
  / today / tomorrow, incomplete
- **Calendar events** for today (user's default calendar — silent-fail if not connected)
- **Inbound emails** (last 24h, PEEK mode — never marks as read) from the user's
  primary authorized mailbox, matched by sender email against lead/contact/account
  records; silent-fail if no mailbox is connected. Runs without a session use a
  5-minute token limited to the mailbox module.
- **Playbook stage enrichment** — for records enrolled in an active playbook,
  `playbook_stage_info` carries the playbook name, current step, and next activity.

### Plan items
Each `top_priorities` item carries `channel` (`call|text|email|none`) and
`draft_message` (at most 2 sentences, built only from facts in the context).
Categories: `prospect_activity`, `renewal`, `overdue_task`, `follow_up`, `task_today`,
`meeting_prep`, `opportunity_close`, `new_assignment`, `task_tomorrow`,
`contact_outreach`, `lead_outreach`.

### LLM pipeline
Synth → quality-assess → optional refine (threshold 0.7, max 2 iterations).
Quality score and iteration count are surfaced in the status response for observability.
Plan uses pre-rendered human-readable dates (`due_local`, `days_overdue`, `updated_local`)
so rationales never hallucinate dates from epochs.

### Feature flags (BOTH required — defaults `False`)
- `Tenant.daily_plan_enabled` — tenant-level master toggle
- `User.daily_plan_enabled` — per-user opt-in

Both flags are toggled via the **existing generic update endpoints** —
no dedicated Daily Plan config endpoints. Use the recipes below.

**Enable the tenant master toggle** (tenant-admin-only, via
`POST /user/update/tenant`; field passes the blocklist-based updater):
```bash
curl -X POST https://ingress.ambivo.com/user/update/tenant \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AMBIVO_ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"payload": {"daily_plan_enabled": true}}'
```

**Enable a per-user opt-in** (tenant-admin-only, via
`POST /user/admin/user/update`; the field is on that endpoint's
whitelist):
```bash
curl -X POST https://ingress.ambivo.com/user/admin/user/update \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AMBIVO_ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "userid": "<target-userid>",
    "action": "update",
    "payload": {"daily_plan_enabled": true}
  }'
```

Superadmins can also set the tenant flag via
`POST /admin/update/tenant`. Self-serve user toggle (user flipping
their own flag) is not yet supported — always goes through admin.

### Dedup
If a `processing` job was started within the last 5 minutes for today,
`POST /user/daily_plan/generate` returns the existing `job_id` instead of enqueuing a new run.

### Batch fan-out
`POST /admin/daily_plan/batch` is **tenant-admin-only**. The API enqueues ONE dispatcher
task; Celery owns the per-user fan-out. Calendar is skipped in batch mode (Celery has
no user OAuth tokens).

tags.name: Entity Data
tags.description:
Unified `/entity/data` endpoint — query, export, aggregate, and inspect chart
configuration for any standard entity (lead, contact, account, opportunity,
order, invoice, product, task, …). The full multi-action surface is documented
in `docs/entity_data.md` in the ambivo_api repo. The OpenAPI entries here cover
the **chart_config** and **aggregate** actions, including the time-period
dimension (week/month/quarter/year) and per-entity time-series presets.

tags.name: Entity Lists
tags.description:
Saved CRM record lists backed by the `user_entity_list` collection. A list
may be **static** (membership = an explicit `entity_ids_list` snapshot) or
**dynamic** (membership recomputed at read time from a stored
`match_filter_dict`). Supported `entity_type` values:
`lead | contact | account | opportunity | property`.

Static lists are fixed once created — adding new matching records does not
change membership. Dynamic lists ("smart lists" / segments) re-run the
query every GET, so newly matching records appear automatically and
records that no longer match drop out.

Filter-based creation is capped at **10,000** members per list. Resolution
respects the caller's tenant scope, module access, and access-dict
ownership controls — identical to other list endpoints — via the shared
`GenUtilsService.get_access_q_dict` resolver.

tags.name: Sharing
tags.description:
Record-level sharing via pre-defined **teams**. Apply a Team's member list
(from the existing `security_qa.Team` entity) to a CRM record's
`access_dict` in one call so every team member gains access, and remove
it when no longer needed.

### Supported entity types
`lead`, `contact`, `account`, `opportunity`, `order`, `invoice`, `task`
(maps to the `user_tasks` collection). Products, calendars, task
sequences, files, and custom objects are **not** supported — those
schemas' `access_dict` fields must be updated directly.

### How it works
Each Team stores a `userid_dict_list` where every member has a
`record_access_list` (e.g. `["c","r","u","d","a"]`). When a team is
applied, `Team.to_access_dict()` produces a normalized
`{userid: ["C","R","U","D"]}` map (uppercase; `"a"` is dropped — it is
not a recognized record-level privilege). That map is merged into (or
replaces) the record's `access_dict`, and the team id is recorded on the
record's `applied_team_ids` array for audit.

### Team role presets
Members' `record_access_list` usually comes from a role preset
(`TEAM_ROLES.record_access_list_presets`):

| Role | Raw list | After `to_access_dict()` |
|---|---|---|
| `administrator` | `["c","r","u","d","a"]` | `["C","R","U","D"]` |
| `approver` | `["c","r","u","a"]` | `["C","R","U"]` |
| `contributor` | `["r","u"]` | `["R","U"]` |

Team admins still get full record CRUD — the `"a"` code is a
team-scoped privilege (who can edit the team itself), not a record
privilege, so it's filtered out during conversion.

### Wildcard keys on `access_dict`
Beyond per-userid entries, `access_dict` recognizes:
- `"all": "*"` — tenant-wide full access, bypass mode.
- `"*": "*"` (or `"*": ["U","R",…]`) — wildcard grant.
- `"<userid>": "*"` — treated as full CRUD for that user.

Apply/remove-team operations do **not** emit or consume these keys;
they only manipulate explicit per-userid entries.

### Snapshot semantics
Subsequent edits to the Team do **not** propagate to already-applied
records. A follow-up `resync` endpoint is planned for that use case.

### Permissions
Caller must have update (`U`) privilege on the target record AND be
either:
- a member of the team, OR
- a tenant admin.

`remove_team` does NOT require team membership — any record-updater can
clean up a previously-applied team.

Permission denials return `403`; all other validation failures return `400`.

### Gotchas
- **Create endpoints ignore team ids.** `POST /user/customer/account`,
  `/user/lead`, `/user/opportunity`, etc. seed `access_dict` with the
  creating user only. Any `team_id` / `applied_team_ids` in the create
  payload is silently dropped — call `POST /share/apply_team` as a
  follow-up.
- **`applied_team_ids` is best-effort, not authoritative.** Direct
  Mongo writes (or future endpoints that manipulate `access_dict`
  without going through `ShareService`) will cause drift between the
  audit list and the actual access map.
- **Merge is keyed at userid.** In `mode=merge`, a team member's
  privileges replace (not union with) any pre-existing entry for the
  same userid.
- **Tenant-admin bypass is permissive.** Any tenant admin can apply
  any team in the tenant to any record, even if they're not a member.
  Audit reviewers should not assume membership from an applied team.
- **Record owner is always retained.** `record.userid` (the owner) is
  resolved separately in `generate_query_for_access()` and is never
  touched by apply/remove, even in `mode=replace`.

tags.name: CTA
tags.description:
Call-To-Action (CTA) records bind a Widget (or a raw URL template) to
context-sensitive mappings so a single definition can produce per-record
personalized URLs.

### Widget-type CTAs (mail-merge for web forms)

A Widget is embeddable HTML/JavaScript — typically a form (survey,
feedback, appointment request, quote, renewal intent, unsubscribe) hosted
on the tenant's website. A `cta_type="widget"` CTA ties that form to a
CRM entity through a `mapping_dict` that says which form field should be
pre-filled from which entity attribute, e.g.

```
cta.url          = "https://tenant-site.com/feedback"
cta.entity_type  = "lead"
cta.mapping_dict = {
  "email": "lead.email",
  "name":  "lead.fullName",
  "phone": "lead.phone"
}
```

When `generate_dynamic_link` runs for a specific prospect (say, Jane
Doe), the server builds a URL whose query string carries Jane's values,
each **base64-encoded**:

```
https://tenant-site.com/feedback?email=amFuZUBleGFtcGxlLmNvbQ%3D%3D&name=SmFuZSBEb2U%3D
```

That URL is delivered to Jane via SMS / email / push (usually by the
automation/workflow engine). When Jane clicks it, the widget's
JavaScript on the hosting page reads the query string, base64-decodes
each value, and pre-populates the form fields — so the form looks
personalized just for her. Only the query string changes per recipient;
the form HTML is the same for everyone.

Base64 is used for three reasons: (a) the raw PII (email / phone) is not
visible in SMS previews, (b) special characters (`&`, `=`, non-ASCII,
emoji) survive transport cleanly after `urlencode()`, and (c) casual URL
tampering breaks the decode, leading to empty fields rather than garbled
inputs landing in the CRM.

### Endpoint

`POST /cta/manage` dispatches on `req_body["action"]` (default `"add"`).
The `"generate_dynamic_link"` action renders the URL described above,
deriving the template from the CTA record when `cta_id` is passed (for
`cta_type="widget"` the template is built from `cta.url` +
`cta.mapping_dict`; otherwise `cta.url` is used verbatim) or from an
explicit `cta_link` override. An opt-in `shorten=true` flag additionally
persists a `link-redirect` CTA and returns `short_link`
(`https://amb.cx/<code>`) so the URL fits in an SMS.

tags.name: Usage & Billing
tags.description:
Tenant usage reporting and shadow-billing telemetry — record/storage
metrics, quota limits, GenAI tokens, and the newer eSign / PDL enrichment
dimensions. Includes an opt-in self-contained HTML report uploaded to a
temporary public link.

tags.name: GenAI
tags.description:
One completion through Core. Services (the workflow system, vectordb-api)
call this instead of holding provider keys, so the tenant's AI setting,
quota and billing apply in one place.

tags.name: Stripe
tags.description:
Ambivo **platform** Stripe resources (the ambivo billing account, NOT
Stripe Connect / connected accounts). Read-only catalog endpoints here are
authenticated by the shared internal secret so internal and third-party
services can fetch the product/price catalog without a user JWT.

**Stripe management routes.** These POST routes take `{action, payload}` and
pass them to Stripe. Each needs a signed-in user (Bearer JWT).

- `/stripe/checkout_session/manage`, `/stripe/product/manage`,
  `/stripe/customer/manage`, `/stripe/payment_methods/manage`,
  `/stripe/setup_intent/manage` and `/stripe/payment_intent/manage` are for
  Ambivo superadmins only. Anyone else gets `result: 2` with
  `error_code: STRIPE_ADMIN_ONLY`.
- `/stripe/payment_method_configurations/manage` is for a tenant admin acting on
  the tenant's own Stripe Connect account (`payload.stripe_account`). A superadmin
  may act on any account. Anyone else gets `result: 2` with
  `error_code: STRIPE_ACCOUNT_NOT_YOURS`.

Both refusals are HTTP 200 and carry an `error` message.

tags.name: Commissions
tags.description:
Sales-agent commissions for orders. A **commission structure** (plan:
straight / tiered / cumulative-tiered / gross-margin) is assigned to an
**agent** via an agent-structure assignment; the calculate endpoint books
per-order-line **commission** records. Includes a commission-by-agent
**report** (JSON / CSV / PDF), CSV/XLSX **import/export** for structures and
assignments, and reconciliation of order commissions into QuickBooks vendor
bills. Structure & assignment CRUD are gated on the `commission_structure`
privilege module; booked-commission CRUD and the report on the `commission`
module. All responses use the CRM `result` (1=success, 2=failure) envelope.

tags.name: Files
tags.description:
The tenant file manager — folders (`file_folders`) and stored files
(`stored_files`), both living in one tree rooted at the virtual folder
`"-1"`.

### Entity context

A folder or file may be **filed under a CRM record** via the pair
`entity_type` + `entity_id` (e.g. `contact` + the contact's id). That is
what makes an upload appear on the record's Files tab instead of only in
the generic drive. `property` and `property_floor_plan` additionally
populate `property_id` / `fp_id`, because the property-scoped listings
filter on those columns.

### App context

Several front-end applications share this one file manager. `app_context`
records **which app a folder or file was created in**, so Asset Base does
not show the CRM drive and vice versa. It is stamped at create time and
filtered on at read time, and is independent of `entity_type` /
`entity_id` — a file can be both "an Asset Base file" and "filed under
contact X".

Values are the front-end application ids, lower `snake_case`:
`crm`, `sales`, `marketing`, `properties`, `books`, `asset_base`,
`knowledge_hub`, `app_factory`, `content_portal`, `dataviz`, `admin`,
`account`, `setup`, `authorization`, `custom`, `client_portal`,
`insurance`, `widget`, `form_widget`, `payment_widget`,
`appointment_widget`, `custom_data_widget`, `vcard_widget`.

Input is normalized before it is stored — `"Asset Base"`, `"asset-base"`
and `"ASSET_BASE"` all become `asset_base`, so they are one drive and not
three. An id not on the list above is normalized and stored rather than
rejected, so a newly released app is never blocked on a server deploy.

**Inheritance.** A folder created inside an app-scoped folder inherits its
parent's `app_context`, and a file uploaded into an app-scoped folder
inherits the folder's, whenever the request does not name one itself. A
subtree therefore cannot end up half in and half out of the app it visibly
lives in.

**Reading.** Every listing endpoint accepts `app_context` and every one of
them ignores it when it is absent — omit it and you get the pre-`app_context`
behaviour of seeing everything. Filtering for `crm` **also returns records
created before `app_context` existed**, which carry no value at all;
filtering for any other app returns that app's records only. Without that
roll-up, switching the CRM to a filtered listing would empty its drive.

### Copy

Copying is a real duplication, not a reference: every copied file gets
its **own S3 object** and its own `stored_files` record, so deleting
either side never touches the other. Presigned links, share ids, CDN
publication and vector-index state are dropped from the copy, and a copied
KB folder is created as a plain folder (its index was never built for it).

On a copy request `entity_type` + `entity_id` name the **destination
context**, not a filter — this is how a folder or file sitting in the
generic drive is copied *into* a contact, lead, account, order or
property. Send both empty to strip the association; omit both and the copy
inherits whatever the source carried. The copy still inherits the
**source's** `access_dict` — filing it under a record does not re-derive
sharing from that record.

Folder copy is bounded at **500 MB** for the whole tree (sum of all file
sizes, all levels) and the same ceiling applies per file; the request is
rejected before anything is written. All responses use the CRM `result`
(1=success, 2=failure) envelope.

tags.name: Dashboards
tags.description:
Saved CRM reporting dashboards — the boards the crm2 **Dashboards** page
renders. A dashboard is a named set of chart definitions drawn against
`/entity/data?action=aggregate`; charts are held opaquely on the board and
rendered client-side.

### What a caller sees

A single `GET /crm/dashboards` returns the union of three audiences,
resolved server-side, so no client merge is needed:

- **Platform defaults** — seeded boards (`tenant_id: "-1"`, `is_default:
  true`) every tenant inherits, one set per entity (Leads, Contacts, …).
  Read-only to normal users.
- **Tenant-shared** boards (`visibility: "shared"`) — visible to the whole
  tenant.
- **Own private** boards (`visibility: "private"`) — visible only to their
  `owner_userid`.

### Writes

`POST` creates, `PATCH` updates (body carries `dashboard_id`), `DELETE`
removes. A platform default is read-only (only a superadmin may edit one),
and a private board is mutable only by its owner — the server enforces both.

### Scope

Each board stores a `scope_dict` (`{kind, group_id?, stacked?, site_code?}`)
selecting what its charts read: the signed-in tenant, or a consented tenant
**group** (consolidated, FX-normalized) via the group reporting endpoint.

InternalSecret.name: X-AMBIVO-INTERNAL-SECRET
InternalSecret.description: Internal service-to-service secret for cross-module calls

AccountingSyncKey.name: X-Accounting-Sync-Key
AccountingSyncKey.description: Internal service-to-service secret used to authorize celery/cross-app endpoint calls (e.g. the nightly installed-base renewal sweep). Accepts the ambivo internal secret or the accounting sync key.

DashboardChart.description: One chart on a board. `mode: "group"` groups by `groupBy`; `mode: "time"` buckets `dateField` by `timeGrain`. `measure` is the aggregate field (`_count` = record count). Stored opaquely and rendered client-side.

entityType.description: lead, contact, account, opportunity, order, invoice, product, task, installed_base, purchase_order.

DashboardScope.description: What a board's charts read under — the signed-in tenant, or a consented group (consolidated).

stacked.description: Group scope: break each series down by member tenant.

entity_type.description: The entity tab this board is filed under.

is_default.description: True for the seeded per-entity defaults.

source_key.description: Stable key for a seeded/migrated board.

CrmDashboardWrite.description:
Create/update body. `tenant_id`, `is_default`, and `owner_userid` are server-controlled.
No field is required. On create, `name` defaults to `""` and `charts` to `[]`.

visibility.description: On create, any other value is saved as `shared`. On update, it returns `INVALID_VISIBILITY`.

InstalledBase.description: A durable, termed instance sold or purchased. Every row is shared with the whole team (`access_dict` is `{"*": [C,R,U,D]}`). Any staff user can read and update any row. Only the owner or a tenant admin can delete. Monetary fields carry an FX block; reports read base_* (coalesced to native when no fx_rate). NOT to be confused with a Fixed Asset.

status.description: Lifecycle status; driven by the renewal sweep.

direction.description: sold = A/R (customer, churn risk); purchased = A/P (vendor, service-lapse risk).

order_id.description: Provenance — the sales order this was provisioned from.

notice_period_days.description: Days before end_date to flip to expiring (default 90).

requires_purchase_order.description: Buy-side opt-in. When true, a purchased record's renewal sweep raises a draft PurchaseOrder in addition to the task. Default false.

linked_id.description: Reseller: links a purchased record to the sold one.

manufacturer.description: Make / brand (for equipment). Groupable in charts.

install_location.description: Free-text physical site where the instance is installed (e.g. "Dallas HQ, Rack 3"). This — not site_code — is the physical location.

reminder_offsets_days.description: Days-before-expiry reminder thresholds (default [90,60,30,15]). Explicit [] disables reminders.

site_code.description: Org-partition tag (tenant.site_list[].code) for access scoping — NOT the physical install location (use install_location for that).

tags.description: Free-text tags; lowercased into a searchable search_tag_list on write.

PurchaseOrder.description: Buy-side procurement order (the tenant purchases from a vendor). Money and lifecycle mirror a sales Order; settles to a Bill. Access is access_dict only.

stage.description: `received` is the goods-receipt milestone (three-way match); entering it stamps received_date and provisions purchased installed_base records for asset-tracked lines.

bill_id.description: Settles to this Bill (A/P); stamped by /user/purchase_order/create_bill.

po_line_list.description: Line items: [{line_id, product_id, description, line_detail_dict:{qty,unit_price}, amount}].

received_date.description: Epoch goods were received; stamped on entry to stage=received.

approval_status.description: Rollup. With a multi-step chain: pending until every step approves; rejected on any step rejection.

approver_userids.description: Intended approvers (single-state gate). Set by the server; a save that changes it is refused.

approval_steps.description: Optional multi-approver chain (empty = single-state gate). Ordered sign-off steps, e.g. Finance → IT → Legal. approve() advances step by step; the PO is fully approved only once every step approves. Built by the server from the tenant approval chain when the PO is submitted. Read-only: a save that changes it is refused with PURCHASE_ORDER_APPROVAL_CHAIN_NOT_SETTABLE.

seq.description: 1-based order; auto-filled from position if omitted.

approver_userids.description: Any one of these (or a tenant admin) may act on this step.

current_approval_seq.description: seq of the step awaiting action (0 = none / chain complete).

is_bill_interfaced.description: True once settled to a Bill.

bill_interface_ts.description: Epoch the Bill was created from this PO.

tags.description: Free-text tags; lowercased into a searchable search_tag_list on write.

CommissionStructure.description: A commission plan (rate/tiers/period). Not bound to an agent by itself.

CommissionAgentStructure.description: Assignment binding an agent to a commission structure, optionally time-boxed.

gross_count.description: Total matching rows. Counted on page 1 only; 0 on later pages.

csv_text.description: Raw CSV text (header row + data), parsed server-side.

rows.description: Per-row outcome (status = created | updated | failed, with id or error).

ErrorResponse.description: Sent with HTTP 200. Some refusals send only `result: 2`, with no message.

error_code.description: The message upper-cased, with spaces turned into underscores.

error.description: Usually an object with `message`. A few handlers send a plain string code.

arguments.description: The detail passed with the error, such as "missing lead_id".

CanonicalError.description:
Canonical error envelope emitted by handlers using `write_error_response()`.
New endpoints SHOULD use this shape so clients can branch on `error_code`
deterministically. `status_code` is the HTTP-style hint set by the handler
(often 200 even on logical failures — the HTTP status is set independently).
Endpoint-specific context fields (e.g. `key`, `entity_type`, `max_length`)
may appear alongside the required keys.

error_code.description: UPPERCASE_WITH_UNDERSCORES. Stable identifier — branch on this, not on `error.message`.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Safe to display to end users.
message.example: custom stage 'demo_scheduled' already exists for opportunity

status_code.description: HTTP-style status hint set by the handler.

request_path.description: Path the request hit. Useful for client-side telemetry.

DocumentTemplate.description:
An HTML/Jinja template bound to a CRM `entity_type`, rendered to a branded PDF
via WeasyPrint. Tenant-owned templates override the Ambivo starters
(`tenant_id` = `"-1"`), which are read-only. Setting `is_default` true makes it
the template the Print button uses for its `(entity_type, doc_kind)`. Timestamps
are epoch seconds.

html_content.description: Jinja2 + HTML body (merge fields + line loops).

allow_esign.description: Whether the rendered output may be sent for e-signature (quote/proposal true; invoice false).

DocumentGenerateResult.description:
Success envelope for `POST /user/document/generate`. The fields present depend
on the request: `pdf_url` for `output=pdf`, `preview_html` for
`output=html_preview`, the `esign`/`native_esign_document_id`/`status` trio when
`esign=true`, and the `draft`/`native_esign_document_id`/`status` trio when
`persist_draft=true`.

esign.description: Present and true when the document was sent for signature.

draft.description: Present and true when a draft was staged (`persist_draft=true`).

status.description: Native e-sign status: `"pending"` after a send (esign or `/user/document/send`), `"draft"` for persist_draft.

StageValueMeta.description:
One entry in `/entity/status-values?entity_type=...` response. Used by
UI consumers to render dropdowns, kanban columns, and admin tables with
labels, colors, and seeded-vs-custom-vs-overridden badging.

key.description: The actual stored value on the entity document (e.g. `closed_won`, `demo_scheduled`).

label.description:
Display label. For pure-seeded entries this is a title-cased version of
the key; for custom entries it's the tenant-supplied label; for
overridden seeded entries (`is_overridden: true`) it's the tenant's
override label.

color.description:
Hex color string. Empty for pure-seeded entries; tenant-defined for
customs and overrides.

is_seeded.description:
`true` when the entry is a built-in seeded value. Built-in business
logic (e.g. `closed_won` creates an order, `closed_lost` cleans up
the contact) is keyed off this slot and is preserved even when the
entry is overridden -- only label/color/position can be customized.
`false` for pure tenant-defined custom stages.

is_overridden.description:
`true` when this seeded entry has a tenant override row in
`entity_custom_stages` swapping its label, color, or position.
Always `false` when `is_seeded: false` (overrides only apply to
seeded keys). Clients with localized strings for seeded entries
should prefer their own copy when `is_overridden: false` and use
the server-supplied label when `is_overridden: true`.

entity_custom_stage_id.description:
Mongo `_id` of the `entity_custom_stages` row backing this entry.
Present on pure-custom entries (`is_seeded: false`) AND on
overridden seeded entries (`is_seeded: true && is_overridden: true`).
Use this id to PATCH (edit override/custom) or DELETE
(override -> reset to seeded defaults; custom -> soft-delete the
column) via `POST /tenant/entity-custom-stages`. Absent on
pure-seeded entries with no tenant customization.

is_active.description:
`false` for soft-deleted custom values. The endpoint only returns active values
in the merged list; this field is reserved for admin-screen consumers that may
also surface inactive rows for reactivation.

position.description:
Sort order (ascending). Seeded positions come from a logical
lifecycle hint map; custom positions are tenant-supplied (default
200, after all seeded slots). For overrides, the tenant-supplied
position wins when set; when omitted on creation the server
inherits the seeded position so simple renames don't reflow the
kanban.

EntityStatusCountValue.description:
One bucket in `/entity/status-counts` — same shape as `StageValueMeta`
plus a `count` and an optional `is_orphaned` flag.

key.description: Stored status/stage value on the entity document.

is_seeded.description: True for built-in seeded values; false for tenant customs.

is_active.description:
True for active seeded + custom values. False when the bucket is
surfaced as `is_orphaned` (custom stage was soft-deleted but
records still hold the key).

position.description: Sort order. Orphaned buckets use 999 so they trail.

count.description: Number of records currently in this bucket (post access filter).

is_orphaned.description:
Optional. Present and `true` for buckets whose status definition has
been soft-deleted but records still hold the value. Admin UIs can
prompt re-creating the custom stage or migrating those records.

EntityStatusCountsPayload.description: Body of `data` for a single entity_type response from `/entity/status-counts`.

field_name.description: Document field this entity_type stores the status/stage in.

values.description: One entry per bucket, ordered by `position` ascending.

EntityCustomStage.description:
Persisted tenant-defined custom stage/status row in the
`entity_custom_stages` collection. Striped by `(tenant_id, entity_type, key)`.

entity_custom_stage_id.description: Mongo `_id` as string. Use as the address for update/delete.

tenant_id.description: Owning tenant (server-stamped from JWT — clients cannot set this).

key.description: ASCII slug used as the actual stored value on entity documents. Immutable after creation.

label.description: Display label shown in pickers + admin table.

color.description: Hex color string. Empty when unset.

position.description:
Sort key (ascending) for kanban columns and pickers. Default 200 (after all
seeded slots). Use a number BETWEEN seeded position hints to interleave
(e.g. position=25 on opportunity sits between discovery(20) and developing(30)).

field.description: Mongo field name on the entity document.

label.description: Human-readable label suitable for chart axes / legends.

type.description:
Field semantic type. Includes FK markers (`account_fk`, `user_fk`,
`contact_fk`, `opportunity_fk`, `order_fk`, `lead_fk`) so the FE can
resolve grouped IDs to display names.

default.description: Exactly one entry per entity is flagged true.

EntityDataChartConfigPreset.description:
One-click chart definition. Group-by presets carry `group_by`;
time-series presets carry `date_field` + `time_grain`.

EntityDataPicklistResponse.description:
`action=picklist`. `data` holds the rows under one key: the entity type,
or `values`. A fixed list adds `codes_enforced` for `site`.

gross_count.description: Every matching row. Counted on page 1 only.

group_by.description: Human-readable label, e.g. "Stage: completed" or "Stage: completed | Owner: 5dcd...".

group_by_field.description: Present when grouping by a single field.

group_by_fields.description: Present when grouping by multiple fields.

group_by_values.description: Raw grouped value (or map of field→value when grouping by multiple fields).

EntityDataAggregateTimeBucketPeriod.description:
Period object — keys present depend on time_grain.
- year: `{year}`
- quarter: `{year, quarter}` (1–4)
- month: `{year, month}` (1–12)
- week: `{year, week}` (ISO week 1–53)
- day: `{year, month, day}`

timezone.description: IANA timezone resolved from user.timeZone → tenant.timeZone → UTC.

field.description: Echoes the offending field name when applicable.

EntityDataAggregateReportRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /entity/data` with `action=aggregate_report`.
Combines a group-by (or time-bucket) aggregation with an optional
tabular records section, renders to HTML or PDF, and (optionally)
uploads to S3 returning a presigned URL.

**Required:** Provide either `group_by_fields` OR (`date_field` AND
`time_grain`) — the dispatch enforces this and returns
`missing_group_by_fields` / `date_field_and_time_grain_both_required`
on violation.

**Filter:** `match_filter_dict` accepts the same Mongo-style filter
as `action=aggregate`, plus `expr({{current_ts}}-N)` interpolation.
Tenant scoping is applied automatically to the records query.

match_filter_dict.description:
MongoDB-style filter applied before aggregation. Server interpolates
`{{current_ts}}` and `expr(...)` automatically. Empty filter
returns all tenant records (subject to tenant scoping).

group_by_fields.description:
Field names to group on (e.g. `["lead_status"]`). Required unless
`date_field` + `time_grain` are provided. Validated against the
entity's `chart_config.groupable_fields`.

aggregate_field.description: Numeric field to sum/avg alongside count. Defaults to count-only.

date_field.description: Date field for time-bucket mode. MUST be paired with `time_grain`.

entity_ids_list.description:
Explicit ObjectId list — alternative or addition to
`match_filter_dict`. Server merges into `match_filter_dict._id.$in`
and logs a warning if both an explicit `_id` and `entity_ids_list`
are provided (entity_ids_list wins).

upload_to_s3.description:
When `true` (default) the report is uploaded to S3 and the response
contains a presigned `url` (~3 years for HTML, ~10 years for PDF;
`inline` content-disposition for browser preview). When `false`
the response carries inline `content` (HTML string) or
`content_base64` (PDF bytes, base64-encoded).
Send a JSON boolean. Any non-empty string, even "false", counts as `true`.

include_records.description:
Include a tabular records section under the aggregate.
Send a JSON boolean. Any non-empty string, even "false", counts as `true`.

record_limit.description:
Cap on records included in the table. Server enforces a hard max
of 1000. Pass 0 to skip the records section even when
`include_records=true`. Records are ordered by `_id` desc (newest
first) before the cap is applied, so a cap returns the most
recent docs. Best-effort: per-record serialization failures are
logged + skipped, never fail the report.

EntityDataAggregateReportSummary.description: Compact summary of what got included in the report.

records_error.description:
Set only when the records section degraded (e.g. mongo I/O failure).
The aggregate-only report still rendered.

EntityDataAggregateReportSuccess.description:
Successful aggregate-report response. When `upload_to_s3=true` the
`url` is set and `content`/`content_base64` are absent. When
`upload_to_s3=false` it's the inverse.

DailyPlanDict.description:
Structured daily plan emitted by the LLM synthesis pass.
Shape is stable across iterations (synth / refine both return this schema).

summary.description: 2–3 sentence overview an agent can read in 10 seconds.
summary.example: Today has no meetings but 15 overdue renewals demand attention — start with Lourdes Soto (56 days overdue). Confirm 4/17 appointment with Heidi Pascarelli first.

top_priorities.description: Ranked action items. `entity_id` is always the canonical ObjectId for the entity type.

category.description:
Which work bucket this priority was drawn from. The synthesizer
ranks priorities by these buckets, highest urgency first — the
numbering below is the canonical priority order:

1. `overdue_task` — incomplete task whose `due_date` is before
   today (oldest first). Highest priority.
2. `follow_up` — inbound email received in the last 24h that
   matches a lead/contact/account in context; replying is treated
   as a high-signal obligation.
3. `task_today` — incomplete task due today.
4. `meeting_prep` — a calendar event today; review notes/context
   before the meeting.
5. `opportunity_close` — an opportunity closing within ~14 days,
   especially one that is past-due or low-probability.
6. `contact_outreach` — a contact in the meeting-setup /
   recent-contact stage that needs a touch.
7. `task_tomorrow` — incomplete task due tomorrow.
8. `lead_outreach` — a new, not-yet-worked lead. Lowest priority.

All eight values are exhaustive; the synthesizer never emits a
category outside this set.

entity_type.description:
The CRM entity this priority points at; `entity_id` is the
canonical ObjectId for this type. `task` pairs with the
`overdue_task`/`task_today`/`task_tomorrow` categories,
`calendar_event` with `meeting_prep`, `email` with `follow_up`,
and `opportunity` with `opportunity_close`. `calendar_event` and
`email` are not clickable CRM records — render them as plain text
rather than deep-links.

title.example: Call Lourdes Soto to start renewal conversation

rationale.description:
Grounded one-liner citing context fields. Dates come from the pre-rendered
`due_local` / `days_overdue` fields — never converted from epoch by the LLM.
rationale.example: This renewal task is 56 days overdue (due 2026-02-14), the most critically neglected item.

suggested_action.example: Call Lourdes at 19392947666 or email dra.lourdessoto@gmail.com

playbook_stage.description:
The entity's current playbook stage, derived from its
`lead_status` / `status`. Empty string (or null) when the
entity is not enrolled in a playbook.

wait_list.description: Entities to skip TODAY based on hold signals in recent comments (e.g. "call back in 2 days").

entity_type.description:
The held entity's type. The synthesizer parks leads, contacts,
and opportunities (not tasks or calendar events) on the wait
list when a recent comment contains an explicit hold signal.

reason.example: Lead asked to be contacted next week per most recent comment.

meetings_today.description: User's calendar events for today (empty in batch mode — Celery has no user OAuth).

PaginatedListResponse.description:
Paginated list response.
The data object contains an entity-specific key (e.g. `lead_contacts`, `accounts`,
`opportunities`, `products`) holding the array of records, plus `total_count`.
Lists page by `page_num`. Searches page by a `last_id` cursor.
Top-level `gross_count` holds the full match count on page 1.

total_count.description: The number of records on this page. The full count is top-level `gross_count`.

last_id.description: Search endpoints only. The id of the last record on this page. Send it as `last_id` to get the next page.

data.description:
Contains an entity-specific array key (e.g. `lead_contacts`, `accounts`, `contacts`,
`opportunities`, `products`) plus `total_count`.

gross_count.description: Every record the caller can see that matches the filter. Sent on page 1 only.

last_id.description: ID of the last record — use for cursor-based pagination

type.description: Label for the email (e.g. work, personal, other)
Label for the phone (e.g. mobile, work, home, fax)
Label for the address (e.g. billing, shipping, home, office)

ts.description: Epoch timestamp in seconds. 0 = not set.

access_dict.description:
Per-record sharing map. Keys are user ids, values are arrays of
record-level CRUD privileges (`C`, `R`, `U`, `D`).

**Special keys:** `"all": "*"` or `"*": "*"` grant tenant-wide
wildcard access; a per-user value of `"*"` is also treated as full
privilege by `generate_query_for_access()`.

**Create-time:** this field is seeded with the owner only on
create endpoints (e.g. `POST /user/lead`). Bulk sharing with a
team is always a follow-up `POST /share/apply_team` call — see
the **Sharing** tag.

applied_team_ids.description:
Audit trail of team ids applied via `POST /share/apply_team`.
Maintained only by the share endpoints; direct Mongo writes to
`access_dict` will cause drift. Treat as best-effort, not source
of truth. See the **Sharing** tag.

See "Site-Code Partition (Multi-Office Support)" in the spec intro for full semantics.

Represents a company/organization account. Collection: `accounts`. Primary key: `account_id`.

product reads this way). When this product is added to an Opp /
