email.description: At most 100 characters. A longer value gets HTTP 404 with an HTML "Blocked" page.

password.description: At most 128 characters. A longer value gets HTTP 404 with an HTML "Blocked" page.

device_id.description:
Device identifier for session tracking. Send it on every call. Without it the
server answers result 2 with a KeyError message.

tenant_id.description: Required when user exists in multiple tenants

os.description: Client OS, for example `web`, `ios` or `android`. Send it on every call, as with `device_id`.

trust_device_token.description:
Token from an earlier MFA verify that asked to remember this device. When it is
valid for this `device_id`, the server skips the MFA challenge.

LoginResponse.description:
Four possible shapes:

1. **No MFA enrolled** — returns `result: 1` with `token` + `user`.
2. **MFA enrolled (single factor)** — returns the `MfaChallengeEnvelope` shape
   (`result: 1` + `is_mfa_response: true` + challenge fields). The client must
   collect the code and POST to `/user/mfa/verify`.
3. **MFA enrolled (multiple active factors)** — returns the
   `MfaFactorSelectionEnvelope` shape with `requires_factor_selection: true`,
   a short-lived `pre_mfa_token`, and a `factor_list`. The client must POST the
   chosen `factor_id` + `pre_mfa_token` to `/user/mfa/initiate` to trigger the
   actual challenge before calling `/user/mfa/verify`. This shape has no `result` key.
4. **MFA required by tenant policy, no factor enrolled**: returns
   `is_mfa_response: true`, `requires_mfa_enrollment: true` and an `enrollment_token`.
   The client enrolls a first factor through `/user/mfa/enroll_gate`. This shape has
   no `result` key.

token.description: JWT session token (present only on direct login — no MFA pending)

is_mfa_response.description: When true, MFA is required and a challenge has been issued.

type.description: Channel of the issued challenge (single-factor branch).

challenge_destination.description:
Masked destination — last 4 digits for SMS (e.g. `"5118"`)
or masked email for email MFA (e.g. `"j***e@acme.com"`).

expires_at.description: UTC expiry time of the email-OTP challenge (email factor only).

userid.description: User ID — required when POSTing to `/user/mfa/verify`.

requires_factor_selection.description:
True when the user has more than one active factor. The client must
present the `factor_list` to the user and POST the chosen `factor_id`
(with the `pre_mfa_token`) to `/user/mfa/initiate`.

pre_mfa_token.description:
Opaque random string (5 min, single-use). It names a pending sign-in stored on
the server and carries no claims. Bound to the listed factors. Required by
`/user/mfa/initiate`.

factor_list.description: Active MFA factors the user can choose from.

requires_mfa_enrollment.description: True when tenant policy requires MFA and the user has no active factor.

enrollment_token.description: Opaque token, valid 15 minutes. Send it to `/user/mfa/enroll_gate`.

mfa_default_method.description: The channel to offer first on the enrollment screen.

device_trust.description: OTP sign-in (`/admin/sms/verifications`) only. Device token valid for 30 days.

token.description: JWT token (included in user object for some flows)

name.description: Full name (will be split into first/last)

password.description:
Auto-generated if not provided. At least 12 characters.
If the email already has an account, this password signs that user in.

phone.description: Accepted, but a JSON-body registration does not save it on the new user.

app_context.description:
Optional. Google ignores it. Microsoft treats any non-empty value as `tenant`,
which is also the default.

web_token.description: Optional. A tenant's web token; the sign-in is tied to that tenant.

prompt_consent.description: When true, forces re-consent (appends `&prompt=consent` to OAuth URL)

post_navigation.description:
URL where the API server redirects with the JWT appended as a path segment after
OAuth completes. **Must end with trailing slash** (e.g. `https://app.ambivo.com/token-login/`).
Must be on the deployment's redirect allow-list (`*.ambivo.com`, plus partner brand
domains on a white-label deployment). The JWT is appended directly:
`{post_navigation}{jwt_token}?final_navigation={url}`

final_navigation.description:
Final destination URL after token processing. Appended as a query parameter to
the `post_navigation` redirect. Without `post_navigation`, this is ignored.

login_hint.description: Email hint for Google's account picker (Google only)

url.description: Full OAuth provider URL (Google/Microsoft). Navigate the browser here.

token.description: JWT login token or temporary exchange token (`tx1_<24 hex>_<64 hex>`, 60 seconds, one use)

OtpSendRequest.description:
Send a one-time code. Send `phone_number` for SMS or `email` for email.
`channel` picks the channel; without it, `email` present means email.

channel.description:
Where the code goes. Without it, the code goes by email when `email` is
present, else by SMS. An explicit value is final.

phone_number.description:
Phone number for SMS. E.164 (e.g. +18505551234); without a leading `+` it is
read as a US number. Used for user lookup and delivery.

email.description: Email for the email channel. Used for user lookup and delivery.

tenant_id.description: Required when the email/phone matches users in multiple tenants

device_trust.description: Token from an earlier successful verify on this device.

OtpVerifyRequest.description:
Verify the code and complete login. Send the `challenge_id` from the send reply.
Without it, send the same identifier used in the send step (`phone_number` or `email`).

code.description: 6-digit code received by SMS or email

challenge_id.description:
From the send reply. When present, the challenge names the account and
`phone_number`, `email` and `tenant_id` are ignored.

phone_number.description: Same phone number used in the send step (when no `challenge_id`)

email.description: Same email used in the send step (when no `challenge_id`)

tenant_id.description: Required when the identifier matches users in multiple tenants

device_trust.description: Token from an earlier successful verify on this device.

TenantSelectionResponse.description: Returned when user exists in multiple tenants and tenant_id was not provided

tenant_id.description: Look the email up in this tenant only.

link_url.description:
Reset link to send instead of the default. `{{token}}` is replaced with the token.
The host must be on the deployment's allow-list, else `error_code: "Invalid Path"`.

confirmation_token.description: 10-character token from the password reset email. Valid for 1 hour.

new_password.description: New password. At least 12 characters and must meet the password rules.

MfaVerifyRequest.description:
Same shape verifies SMS (WorkOS-backed) and email (local) challenges — the server
routes by `MFAChallenge.type` on the stored row. Ownership is enforced server-side:
the body's `userid` must match the challenge's recorded owner.

Send `action: "resend"` to re-issue the challenge without verifying. Resend is
rejected with `MFA_RESEND_TOO_SOON` (returns `retry_after_seconds`) if invoked
less than 30 seconds after the original challenge was issued, and with
`MFA_CHALLENGE_NOT_PENDING` if the original row has been verified or superseded.

userid.description: Owner of the challenge — server hard-rejects mismatches.

challenge_code.description:
6-digit OTP from the user's SMS or email. Required for the default
(verify) action. Omitted when `action: "resend"`.

action.description: Set to 'resend' to re-issue the challenge code instead of verifying.

attempts_remaining.description:
Per-challenge remaining attempts. Present on `INVALID_MFA_CODE`. Default
cap is 5 — once reached, the row transitions to `status: "locked"` and
subsequent attempts return `MFA_CHALLENGE_EXHAUSTED`.

MfaFactor.description: One entry in the `factor_list` returned by multi-factor login.

factor_id.description: Locally-generated id (for email) or WorkOS factor id (for SMS).

challenge_destination_masked.description: e.g. `"***5118"` for SMS or `"j***e@acme.com"` for email.

MfaChallengeEnvelope.description:
Returned by `/user/mfa/initiate` and (for single-factor users) by `/user/login`.
No session JWT is created until the code is verified.

MfaEnrollRequest.description:
Four operations multiplexed on `mfa_type`:

- **`sms`**: enrolls a phone number with WorkOS and texts an activation code.
  Requires `phone_number`.
- **`sms_verify`**: submits the SMS activation code; on success the factor is active.
- **`email`** — enrolls an email factor in `pending_verify` state and emails an
  activation code. The factor is **not** counted as active until the code is
  verified. Requires the user's `confirmed_email == true`.
- **`email_verify`** — submits the activation code; on success the factor flips
  to `status: "active"` and is usable for login.

Re-calling `email` while an email factor already exists rotates the address
(old factor + open challenges are dropped). Concurrent enrollment from two
tabs is resolved by the partial unique index on `raw_data.pre_mfa_jti`.

password.description:
The account password. Required for `sms` or `email` when a factor is already
active, and for a verify that replaces a live factor.

phone_number.description: Required when mfa_type=sms. E.164 or US 10/11-digit accepted.

email.description:
Optional override for mfa_type=email. Defaults to `user.email`.
Must equal the user's confirmed primary address.

MfaEnrollResponse.description:
Shape varies by `mfa_type` of the request:
- SMS enrollment returns the WorkOS factor response.
- Email enrollment returns the pending-verify challenge envelope.
- `email_verify` returns the activation result with `purpose: "enroll"`.

warning.description:
Non-fatal post-verify hint. `FACTOR_NOT_FOUND_AT_ACTIVATION` means the
factor was rotated/deleted between issue and verify (concurrent re-enroll).
`FACTOR_ACTIVATION_FAILED` means the database update failed; the user
should be re-enrolled.

pre_mfa_token.description:
Opaque token returned by `/user/login` when `requires_factor_selection: true`. Valid 5 minutes.
Single-use — replays are rejected with `PRE_MFA_TOKEN_ALREADY_USED`.

factor_id.description:
Must be one of the `factor_id`s present in the original login `factor_list`
(the token's `factor_ids` claim is the authoritative allowlist).

MfaDeleteRequest.description:
Removes a user's own MFA factor(s). `"all"` removes both SMS and email
factors in a single call.

mfa_type.description: Any other value removes nothing and returns `message: "NO-ACTION"`.

password.description: The account password. Not asked of accounts with no password the user could know.

factor_id.description: Optional. With `mfa_type=sms`, the SMS factor to remove.

MfaAdminResetRequest.description:
Tenant-admin override: reset MFA for a locked-out user in the admin's tenant.
The default (no `mfa_type`) resets both SMS and email factors **and** purges
any open `mfa_challenge` rows so a stale code in transit cannot be redeemed
after the reset.

mfa_type.description: Optional — when set, only that factor type is reset.

MfaErrorCode.description:
Canonical error codes returned by the MFA endpoints.

| Code | Returned by | Meaning |
|------|-------------|---------|
| `INVALID_MFA_CODE` | verify | Wrong OTP; `attempts_remaining` decremented. |
| `MFA_CHALLENGE_EXHAUSTED` | verify | Per-challenge attempt cap hit; row locked. |
| `EMAIL_MFA_EXPIRED` | verify | Code past its 5-min TTL. |
| `EMAIL_MFA_NOT_PENDING` | verify | Row already verified, superseded, or locked. |
| `EMAIL_MFA_REQUIRES_CONFIRMED_EMAIL` | enroll / login | `confirmed_email` is false. |
| `EMAIL_MFA_FACTOR_NOT_ACTIVE` | login / initiate | Pending-verify factor at login. |
| `EMAIL_MFA_FACTOR_NOT_FOUND` | challenge | factor_id not in user's enrolled list. |
| `EMAIL_MFA_NO_EMAIL` | enroll | No email address available. |
| `EMAIL_MFA_SEND_FAILED` | challenge | Could not enqueue the email send. |
| `EMAIL_MFA_CHALLENGE_INSERT_FAILED` | challenge | DB write failed (rare). |
| `EMAIL_MFA_CHALLENGE_ERROR` | challenge | Unexpected internal error. |
| `EMAIL_MFA_VERIFY_ERROR` | verify | Unexpected internal error. |
| `MFA_RESEND_TOO_SOON` | resend | Within the 30-second cooldown. `retry_after_seconds` returned. |
| `MFA_CHALLENGE_NOT_FOUND` | verify / resend | Challenge id unknown or ownership mismatch (uniform response — no info leak). |
| `MFA_CHALLENGE_NOT_PENDING` | resend | Original challenge already consumed or superseded. |
| `MFA_FACTOR_NOT_FOUND` | initiate / resend | factor_id not enrolled. |
| `MFA_FACTOR_NOT_IN_LIST` | initiate | factor_id not in the original login menu. |
| `MFA_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE` | resend / initiate | Stored challenge type is neither sms nor email. |
| `MFA_NO_FACTORS` | resend | User has no enrolled factors. |
| `INVALID_PRE_MFA_TOKEN` | initiate | Token invalid, expired, or wrong purpose. |
| `PRE_MFA_TOKEN_ALREADY_USED` | initiate / challenge | Replay — partial unique index on `raw_data.pre_mfa_jti` rejected it. |
| `USER_NOT_FOUND` | initiate | Subject of the pre-MFA token doesn't exist. |
| `MISSING_FIELDS` | initiate / verify | Required body field absent. |
| `INVALID_JSON` | any | Request body is not valid JSON. |
| `PASSWORD_REQUIRED` | enroll / delete / admin reset | The body needs the account `password`. |
| `PASSWORD_INCORRECT` | enroll / delete / admin reset | Wrong password; `attempts_remaining` returned. |
| `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` | enroll / delete / admin reset | Too many wrong passwords. |
| `LOGIN_RESPONSE_FAILED` | verify | `generate_login_response` raised — internal error. |
| `GUEST_ACCESS_EXPIRED` | verify / enroll_gate | A managed guest whose access end date passed after the password step. HTTP 200, `error: {message}`, no session. |

EmailCheckRequest.description: Send `email` or `phone`. With neither, the reply is `result: 2`.

email.description: At most 200 characters. A longer value gets HTTP 404 with an HTML "Blocked" page.

phone.description:
Checked only when `email` is absent. At most 20 characters. The reply says only
whether a user has this phone.

return_associated_phone.description:
Send it on every call. Leaving it out fails the request. Only `true` (or the
string `"true"`) looks the email up among users. Any other value checks the
mail domain only and the reply is always `result: 2`.

result.description:
1 = a user has this email (with `return_associated_phone: true`) or this phone.
2 = no user found, or no user lookup was made.

email.description: The email sent, or null for a phone check.

mx_check.description: 1 when the email domain has mail servers.

email_provider_list.description: Mail providers found for the email domain.

alt_tenant_list.description: Tenants the user belongs to. Empty for a phone check.

user_phone_last_4.description: Last 4 digits of the user's phone. Only when exactly one user has the email.

sender_email.description: Sender email — if it matches an authorized mailbox, sends via that mailbox; otherwise via relay

text.description: SMS body text (defaults to notification message_body)

entity_type.description:
Linked entity type. Canonical enum: `lead`, `contact`, `account`, `opportunity`, `task`
(plus `order`, `invoice`). The server normalizes legacy aliases
(`leadcontacts`, `accountcontacts`, `deal`) to the canonical form
and emits a `route` hint in the push `data_message_dict` so
mobile clients can deep-link directly to the detail screen.
See `docs/holistic_notification_endpoint.md` for the full contract.

for_userid.description: Target user ID — defaults to the authenticated caller's userid

initial_delay.description:
Delay in seconds before delivery. If >60, notification is scheduled for deferred execution.
On `/user/notifications/manage`, a queued notification ignores `for_userid` and goes to the caller.
A queued notification also ignores `channels.email`, `channels.sms` and the push and websocket toggles.

reference_id.description: Reference ID for scheduled task deduplication

collapse_key.description: FCM collapse key for notification coalescing

notification_id.description: MongoDB ObjectId(s) of the created static notification (present when status=sent)

eta_ts.description: Estimated delivery epoch timestamp (present when status=queued)

AdminHolisticNotificationRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /admin/notification/holistic`. Mirrors
`HolisticNotificationRequest` but makes `for_userid` required (the
admin endpoint has no caller context to fall back on) and the tenant
is auto-resolved from the target user.

for_userid.description:
Target user ID — REQUIRED. The server looks up this user and
uses their `tenant_id` to scope the notification, so callers
do not need to pass `tenant_id` explicitly.

CalendarObject.description:
A connected calendar. Sensitive fields (password, access_token, refresh_token) are
stripped from list responses.

is_default.description: Whether this is the user's default calendar

access_dict.description:
Per-record sharing map `{userid: ["C","R","U","D"]}` with
optional wildcard keys `"all": "*"` / `"*": "*"`.

**Not team-shareable:** calendars are NOT listed under the
**Sharing** tag's supported entity types — `POST
/share/apply_team` will reject `entity_type: "calendar"`. Update
this field directly via the calendar settings endpoint.

time_zone.description: IANA timezone (optional — defaults to user's timezone)

recurrence.description: RFC 5545 RRULE strings for recurring events

upsert_opportunity.description: Auto-create an opportunity from this event

isOnlineMeeting.description: Create as online meeting (Microsoft Teams / Google Meet)

RecurringInstanceUpdatePayload.description: Update or cancel a single instance of a recurring event

status.description: Set to `cancelled` to cancel this instance only

original_start_time.description: ISO 8601 datetime of the original instance start

RecurringSeriesUpdatePayload.description: Update all future instances in a recurring event series

update_from_date.description: ISO 8601 — only future instances from this date are updated

delete_future_instances.description:
Delete all future instances instead of updating.
Any value counts as true, including `false`. Leave the key out to update.

calendarIds.description: Query free slots across multiple calendars

op_hours_list.description:
Per-day working hour pairs. Index 0 = Monday, 6 = Sunday.
Each element is an array of [start, end] pairs.
Example: `[[8,12],[14,17]]` means 8am-12pm and 2pm-5pm.

specific_days_dict.description:
Override working hours for specific dates.
Keys are date strings (e.g. "15-May-2024"), values are hour pair arrays.

buffer_seconds_after.description: Buffer seconds to add after each event

buffer_seconds_before.description: Buffer seconds to add before each event

use_client_time_zone.description: IANA timezone to use for slot calculation

max_daily_events_limit.description: Maximum number of events per day

interval_slot_list.description: List of available time slots as epoch timestamp pairs

authorized_mailbox.description: Email address of an OAuth-connected mailbox (recommended)

email_connection_id.description: ID of a running stateful IMAP connection

email_creds_dict.description:
Raw credentials for non-OAuth setups (legacy). Every key listed as required
must be present, even when its value is null. A missing key fails with a 500.
Server settings are replaced by a lookup on the domain's MX records when
the provider is known.

latest_text.description: Preview text of the latest message

mail_headers.description: Parsed headers: from, to, subject, date, message-id

EmailMessageDetail.description: Full email message with body, attachments, and metadata

EmailSendData.description:
The sender is always the mailbox the request authenticates with.
Send `recipient_list` or `recipient`; a request with neither has no recipient.

recipient.description: A single recipient. Used only when `recipient_list` is empty.

subject.description: Ignored on reply and forward, where the original subject is used.

sender_display_name.description: Display name shown with the mailbox address in `From`.

TaskStatus.description:
Seeded values: `unassigned`, `assigned`, `in_progress`, `rejected`, `reviewsubmit`, `reviewpass`, `completed`.
On write, a hyphenated or spaced form of a seeded value is stored in its seeded spelling, so `in-progress` becomes `in_progress`.
Service-ticket statuses (`new`, `open`, `waiting_on_customer`, `waiting_on_third_party`, `resolved`, `closed`) and the tenant's custom task statuses are also accepted and returned.
Any other value returns `VALIDATION_ERROR`.

Task.description: Represents a user task. Collection: `user_tasks`. Primary key: `user_task_id`.

action_data.description: Action-specific data (phone number, email, address, etc.)

subject.description: ObjectId of the linked entity (lead, contact, etc.)

user_task_sequence_id.description: Reference to parent task sequence (if created from sequence)

status_update_date.description: Epoch timestamp of last status change

access_dict.description:
Per-record sharing map. Keys are user ids, values are arrays of
record-level CRUD privileges (`C`, `R`, `U`, `D`).

**Special keys:** `"all": "*"` or `"*": "*"` grant tenant-wide
wildcard access; a per-user value of `"*"` is also treated as full
privilege by `generate_query_for_access()`.

**Read enforcement:** `UserTaskService` read paths (`get_task`,
`list_tasks`, `search_tasks`) honor this map — tenant admins
bypass, otherwise only the owner (`userid`) and users present in
`access_dict` with matching privilege see the task.

**Create-time:** `POST /user_tasks` does not set this field.
Only the assignee (`userid`) and tenant admins can read a new task.
If you assign a task to someone else, you cannot read it back unless you are a tenant admin.
To share a task with a team, call `POST /share/apply_team` (see the **Sharing** tag).

applied_team_ids.description:
Audit trail of team ids applied via `POST /share/apply_team`.
Maintained only by the share endpoints; direct Mongo writes to
`access_dict` will cause drift. Treat as best-effort, not source
of truth. See the **Sharing** tag.

site_code.description:
Office / business-unit partition tag. Scalar, immutable-at-create.
Tasks inherit from the subject entity (lead/contact/account/opportunity)
referenced by `subject` + `subject_type` when no explicit value is passed.
Peer visibility on `get_user_tasks` uses site_code-based partitioning,
but preserves the legacy guard: viewers with no OAG codes see no peer
tasks (only `created_by_userid` + access-shared).
See "Site-Code Partition (Multi-Office Support)" in the spec intro for full semantics.

userid.description: Assign to this user (defaults to current user)

due_date_offset_minutes.description: Minutes after sequence start when this task is due

TaskSequence.description:
Represents a task sequence — an ordered list of task templates.
Collection: `user_task_sequence`. Primary key: `user_task_sequence_id`.

access_dict.description:
Per-record sharing map `{userid: ["C","R","U","D"]}` with
optional wildcard keys `"all": "*"` / `"*": "*"`.

**Not team-shareable:** task sequences are NOT listed under the
**Sharing** tag's supported entity types — `POST
/share/apply_team` will reject `entity_type: "task_sequence"`.
Manage access by writing directly to this field.

UserTaskTemplate.description:
Standalone task template record from the `user_task_template` collection.
Persisted fields mirror the service's create/update logic; additional
tenant-defined fields are allowed via `additionalProperties`.

tenant_id.description: Auto-filled by the server from the caller's tenant.

due_date_offset_minutes.description: Minutes after enrollment when the task is due (used when the template is expanded into a task).

create_cal_event.description: If true, a calendar event is created when this template is realized into a task.

updated_ts.description: Written by the server on every create/update.

UserTaskTemplateCreateRequest.description:
Body accepted by `POST /user_task_template`. May be a single template
object OR an array of templates (bulk create). Use
`POST /user_task_template/bulk` for the array-only variant.

UserTaskTemplateUpdateRequest.description:
Body for `PUT /user_task_template`. Must include `template_id` (or `id`).
All other fields are treated as partial-update `$set` patches.

export_settings.description: Present only when the request carried `action=export`.

result.description: `1` if every item succeeded; `2` if any failed (partial success still returns per-item detail).

results.description: Per-item outcome, index-aligned with the request array.

oneOf.description: On failure, the original item payload is echoed here.

message.description:
Human-readable error. Known values include:
- `Template name is required` (on create)
- `template_id is required for update`
- `template_id is required for deletion`
- `Task template not found`
- `Task template not found or not authorized to update`
- `Task template not found or not authorized to delete`
- `Invalid JSON in request body`
- `Search query is required`
- `Request body must be an array of template objects` (bulk)

SmsPayload.description: SMS message payload used by softphone, admin, and bot SMS endpoints.

src.description:
Sender phone number (E.164). Optional — defaults vary by endpoint:
- `/phone/user/send_sms` — user's SIP phone number
- `/admin/send_sms` — tenant's dialer phone
- `/bot/send_sms` — ignored, auto-set to bot's phone

text.example: Hello, this is a reminder about your appointment tomorrow.

CtaAddRequest.description:
Default action when `action` is omitted — create a CTA record.
`widget_id` and `name` are required unless `cta_type` is `link-redirect`.

name.description: CTA name, cut to 200 characters. Required unless `cta_type` is `link-redirect`.

url.description: Target URL. For `cta_type="widget"`, the base hosting URL.

mapping_dict.description:
For `cta_type="widget"`: maps query-param name → dotted entity path
(e.g. `{"email": "lead.email"}`). Used by
`generate_dynamic_link` to derive a `{{...}}` template.

cta_prefix.description: Optional vanity prefix for a `link-redirect` short URL.

CtaGenerateDynamicLinkRequest.description:
Render a personalized URL from either an explicit template (`cta_link`)
or an existing CTA record (`cta_id`). Optionally create a short URL.

cta_id.description:
Existing CTA ObjectId. If supplied without `cta_link`, the server
derives the template from this CTA's `url` + `mapping_dict`
(for `cta_type="widget"`) or uses `cta.url` verbatim.

cta_link.description:
Explicit URL template with `{{placeholder}}` slots. Overrides
`cta_id` if both are supplied.

encoding_mode.description:
`x_state` puts all query fields into one base64 JSON parameter.
`per_field` base64-encodes each query value on its own.

state_param_name.description: Name of the single query parameter in `x_state` mode.

entity_type.description: Sets `X_type` in the `x_state` JSON when the CTA record has no `entity_type`.

entity_id.description:
Sets `X_id` in the `x_state` JSON. `X_id` in the body or in `instance_payload`
also works. Without it, the id is read from `instance_payload[<entity_type>]._id`.

instance_payload.description:
Nested dict of values used to fill the template. Keys are
referenced via dotted paths (e.g. `{{lead.email}}` resolves against
`instance_payload["lead"]["email"]`). Merged with the tenant's
interpolate value dict, so `{{tenant.*}}` placeholders resolve too.

shorten.description:
When `true`, persist (or reuse) a `link-redirect` CTA pointing at
the rendered long URL and return `short_link` + `short_cta_id` in
the response. Dedupes on `(tenant_id, final_url)`. Send a JSON
boolean. Any non-empty string, including `"false"`, counts as `true`.

url_link.description:
Rendered URL. In `x_state` mode the query is one base64 JSON parameter.
In `per_field` mode each query value is base64-encoded.

short_cta_id.description: ObjectId of the `link-redirect` CTA. Present only when `shorten=true`.

created.description: `1` when a new CTA was created, `0` when an existing short-link CTA was reused.

from_number.description:
Sender phone number (E.164). Optional. When it is blank, the tenant's
`dialer_phone` is used. If the tenant has no `dialer_phone`, the message is dropped.

response.description:
`message_queued` on success. With `result: 2` it is `MISSING_TO_NUMBER`,
`MISSING_TEXT`, or the text of an unexpected error.

phone_number.description:
Phone number to validate. Preferred form is E.164 (`+14155551234`,
`+442079460958`). National-format input (e.g. `650-631-1281`) is
accepted as long as `country_iso` is also provided so libphonenumber
can pick a region.

country_iso.description:
Optional ISO-3166 alpha-2 country hint. Required when `phone_number`
is in national format (no leading `+`). Case-insensitive.

live.description:
When `true` (default), also run a paid Telnyx `number_lookup` to fetch
live carrier, caller-name, and portability data. Set `false` to skip
the paid call and return only the offline libphonenumber result. The
live call is also auto-skipped if libphonenumber says the number is
not even "possible". Only `false` or the string `"false"` skips the
lookup; `0` or `"no"` still runs it.

result.description:
`1` = the input parsed successfully (`valid` may still be false if
the number is parseable but not actually assignable). `2` = parse
failure or input was rejected before parsing — see `reason`.

valid.description: Result of `phonenumbers.is_valid_number` on the parsed value.

possible.description: Result of `phonenumbers.is_possible_number` on the parsed value. Less strict than `valid`.

national_format.description: Number in the destination country's national format (e.g. `(415) 555-1234`).

country_iso.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 country code derived from the parsed number.

country_code.description: Numeric country calling code (e.g. `1` for US/Canada, `44` for UK).

number_type.description:
Best-effort number-type classification from libphonenumber. Some
countries do not distinguish mobile vs fixed-line, in which case
`FIXED_LINE_OR_MOBILE` or `UNKNOWN` is returned.

lookup.description:
Live Telnyx number_lookup payload. Only present when `live=true` was
requested, libphonenumber said the number is `possible`, and the
Telnyx call succeeded. Shape passes through Telnyx's `data` block
(carrier, caller_name, portability, etc.).

lookup_error.description:
Present when the live Telnyx call was attempted but failed. The
`result` field stays `1` because the offline parse succeeded —
callers that need live data should branch on `lookup` vs
`lookup_error`.

reason.description: Set on failure. Machine-readable error code.

attachment_id.description: MongoDB ObjectId of an attachment to include (MMS)

recipient_userid.description: User ID of the SMS recipient (created as guest if new)

tenant_id.description: Target tenant ID. Provide either `tenant_id` or `master_user_id`.

master_user_id.description: Master user ID (resolves to tenant). Provide either `tenant_id` or `master_user_id`.

BotSmsRequest.description:
Bot SMS request. The `src` field is ignored. The caller's own phone
number is used. Send `dst` and `text` at the top level.

text.example: Your appointment is confirmed for tomorrow at 2 PM.

info.description: Always `null` on success. The SMS is queued, so no provider details come back.

trigger_statuses.description: Entity statuses that auto-enroll into this playbook

exit_statuses.description: Entity statuses that auto-unenroll from this playbook

PlaybookActivity.description:
A single playbook activity. Type "checklist" = manual (user checks off).
Type "workflow" = automated via AI Workflow System.

enabled.description:
Per-activity on/off toggle. Default `true` when missing (back-compat
with legacy playbooks). Set `false` to suppress the step EVERYWHERE
it's touched by the executor: no immediate fire, no Celery scheduling,
no calendar event, and excluded from the AI-context "recommended
activities" prompt. A step that was already scheduled via Celery
before being disabled is caught by a second guard at fire time and
logged as `delivery_status=skipped` / `delivery_detail=activity_disabled`.
Strictly coerced: `true`/`"true"`/`1`/`"yes"`/`"on"` → true;
`false`/`"false"`/`0`/`""`/unknown string → false; `null`/missing → default true.

instructions.description:
Template text with {{variable}} placeholders. Pre-interpolated by executor.
Variables: {{first_name}}, {{last_name}}, {{email}}, {{phone}},
{{lead_status}}, {{sender_full_name}}, {{sender_email}}.
instructions.example: Hi {{first_name}}, this is {{sender_full_name}} with Nashville Apartment Locators.

automation_workflow_id.description: AI Workflow System workflow ID for automated activities

skip_if_replied.description: Skip if entity responded since enrollment

create_cal_event.description:
Create a Google/Microsoft Calendar event on the entity owner's calendar
when this activity fires. Strictly coerced — missing, `null`, `false`,
`"false"`, `0`, `""`, or any unknown string all suppress event creation;
only an explicit truthy value fires it.

The event's description auto-includes the lead's first-listed valid email
and/or valid phone number on a "phone: ... | email: ..." line so the agent
can contact the lead directly from the calendar event. Values are
suppressed if the entry is flagged invalid by its validation dict
(`*_validation_dict.result == 2`) or is a placeholder email
(`@invalid.ambivo.com`).

cal_event_title.description:
Event title template. Supports `{{first_name}}`, `{{last_name}}`,
`{{name}}`, `{{email}}`, `{{phone}}`. `{{email}}` and `{{phone}}` resolve
to empty string when the source is invalid (placeholder domain or
`*_validation_dict.result == 2`); consecutive whitespace left by empty
tokens is collapsed automatically so a template like
`"Re-attempt: {{first_name}} {{last_name}} {{phone}}"` reads cleanly
whether or not the lead has a valid phone on file.

cal_event_offset_minutes.description: Minutes offset from step execution time for calendar event start. 0 = starts at execution time.

cal_event_transparent.description:
Non-blocking calendar event. When `true` (default), the event does NOT
affect the owner's free/busy time — the agent can still accept other
meetings at the same slot. Maps to Google's
`transparency:"transparent"` and Microsoft's `showAs:"free"`.
Playbook events are nudges so this defaults to `true`; set to `false`
explicitly if the event really should block the agent's time (e.g.
a scheduled property tour). Strictly coerced — same rules as `enabled`.

PlaybookCreateRequest.description:
Top-level string fields keep only ASCII characters. Accented and other non-ASCII letters are removed.
Unknown top-level keys are dropped.

ResearchTemplate.description: One pre-built prompt template returned by `/kh/research/templates`

prompt_preview.description: First 300 chars of the template's system prompt

ResearchEstimateRequest.description:
Same shape as `ResearchWorkflowRequest` but sent to `/kh/research/estimate`
instead of `/kh/research`. Returns a time/cost estimate without
enqueuing a workflow.

note.example: Estimates are approximate and may vary based on source availability and content length.

ResearchBatchRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /kh/research/batch` — enqueues multiple
research workflows with shared defaults. Returns a `batch_id` that
can be polled via `GET /kh/research/batch/{batch_id}`.

callback_dict.description: Webhook fired when ALL topics complete (not per-topic)

ResearchReadyResponse.description: Quick ready check (cheaper than GET /kh/research/{id}, just returns a boolean + status)

ResearchWorkflowListResponse.description: Paginated list of research workflows for the caller.

ResearchWorkflowRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /kh/research`. Most fields are optional and
default to sensible values. `topic` is the only required field.

topic.example: recent advances in quantum error correction

user_id.description:
Client-supplied user identifier. When using the `/kh/` gateway
path this is injected from the JWT claims; when calling
research_service directly with the internal secret, supply
explicitly.

max_sources.description: Maximum number of sources to discover and scrape

quality_threshold.description: Minimum content quality score for scraped sources

max_content_length.description: Maximum chars to keep from any single scraped source

knowledge_base_enabled.description: If true, ingest the generated artifacts into a tenant Qdrant collection

ingest_pdf_reports.description: If true, also ingest the generated PDF into the knowledge base

presentation_enabled.description: If true, generate an HTML slide deck artifact

language.description: ISO 639-2 language code for the report (eng, spa, fra, deu, ...)

company_name.description: Company name shown on the PDF cover and headers

logo_url.description: Optional logo URL for the PDF cover

no_ambivo_attribution.description: If true, suppress the "Powered by Ambivo" footer on the PDF

custom_prompt.description:
Full prompt override for the synthesis and report generation stages.
Takes precedence over `additional_instructions` and `template`.

additional_instructions.description:
Supplementary instructions appended to the default prompt
(e.g. "focus on regulatory risks").

output_format.description:
`json` = structured JSON report only (fast).
`pdf` = PDF report only (slower; invokes reportlab).
`all` = both JSON and PDF.

response_schema.description: JSON schema that the LLM output must conform to (overrides dynamic section detection)

parent_workflow_id.description: Workflow ID of a prior research this one builds upon

force_refresh.description: Skip the 7-day cache and force a fresh research run

enable_confidence_scoring.description: Add confidence scores (0.0–1.0) to each section of the JSON output (extra LLM call)

include_citations.description:
When `true` (default), the JSON report's `sources` array and the
PDF's "Data Sources & Attribution" appendix are populated from the
scraper's actual output. When `false`, both are suppressed for a
strictly-executive-summary output. The generation timestamp
(`metadata.generated_at`) is always included regardless of this
flag.

citations_limit.description:
Upper bound on the number of sources listed. `0` effectively
disables the list even with `include_citations: true`. Default 50
is enough for typical multi-source research.

callback_dict.description:
Optional webhook configuration. When set, research_service POSTs
the workflow result to this URL when the pipeline completes.

ResearchWorkflowSubmitResponse.description: Response from `POST /kh/research`. Clients poll `GET /kh/research/{workflow_id}` until `status == "completed"` or `"failed"`.

message.example: Research workflow started for topic: quantum error correction

status.description:
`created` when a new workflow was enqueued. `completed` when the
topic hit the 7-day cache and the cached result was returned
(check `estimated_completion_minutes == 0`).

estimated_completion_minutes.description: Rough estimate of how long the full pipeline will take (0 if cached)

ResearchStageStatus.description: Per-stage execution record from the workflow status response.

ResearchArtifact.description: One artifact emitted by the pipeline. Each artifact is uploaded to S3 with a presigned URL.

stages.description:
Per-stage execution records keyed by stage name
(`research`, `scraping`, `synthesis`, `presentation`,
`professional_report`, `knowledge_base`).

artifacts.description:
Presigned S3 URLs for the generated artifacts, grouped by type.
Always present when `status == "completed"`.

ResearchJsonReportPayload.description:
Canonical shape of the `json_reports` artifact — the structured
research deliverable. This is what you get when you GET the
presigned URL from `artifacts.json_reports[0].url`.

title.example: Recent Advances in Quantum Error Correction: A Comprehensive Analysis

sources.description:
Force-merged from the scraper's output. When
`include_citations: false` or `citations_limit: 0`, this array
is empty but `metadata.sources_processed` still reflects the
true count.

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp — always present, always precise

sources_processed.description: Ground-truth count of sources actually scraped (independent of `citations_limit`)

SynthesisChatRequest.description: Request body for `/kh/chat` (sync and streaming) and `/kh/chat/async`.

message.description: The user query / prompt to synthesize
message.example: Summarize the state of quantum error correction from recent sources

session_id.description:
Optional client-supplied session id. Used for conversation context and
for the secondary index on the async list endpoint. If omitted, the
server generates one per request (no conversation memory).

streaming.description:
Only applies to `/kh/chat`. When `"true"`, returns `text/event-stream`.
Ignored on `/kh/chat/async` — async is never streaming.

enabled_agents.description:
Override which specialized agents the moderator should route to. If
omitted, the default set `["knowledge_base", "knowledge_synthesis",
"web_search", "web_scraper", "assistant"]` is used.

system_message.description: Optional system prompt applied to the synthesis LLM call

session_metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata forwarded to the agents for entity correlation

SynthesisAsyncSubmitResponse.description: Returned by `POST /kh/chat/async` — clients poll `poll_url` until `status` becomes `done`, `failed`, or `cancelled`.

SynthesisJobStatus.description:
Lifecycle:
* `pending` — accepted into the Celery queue, not yet picked up by a worker
* `running` — worker is actively orchestrating the synthesis
* `done` — completed successfully, `answer` field populated
* `failed` — worker raised an exception, `error` field populated
* `cancelled` — client cancelled via `/kh/chat/async/{id}/cancel` or
  internally transitioned during a long run

SynthesisJobState.description: Response shape from `GET /kh/chat/async/{job_id}`. The `answer` and related fields are present only when `status == done`. The `error` field is present for `failed` and `cancelled`.

elapsed_seconds.description: Total backend wall-clock in seconds (null until `completed_at` is set)

agent_routing.description: Agent routing metadata — enabled agents, active agents, etc. (only when `status == done`)

SynthesisJobSummary.description: Compact summary returned by `GET /kh/chat/async` list endpoint. Full `answer` is omitted — call `GET /kh/chat/async/{job_id}` for details.

message_preview.description: First 200 chars of the original query

SynthesisCancelRequest.description:
Body for `POST /kh/chat/async/{job_id}/cancel`. The gateway injects
`user_id` and `tenant_id` from the JWT claims — clients can send an
empty body (`{}`). Ownership is enforced server-side.

user_id.description: Injected from JWT by the gateway; used for ownership check

tenant_id.description: Injected from JWT by the gateway; used for ownership check

ShareEntityType.description: Entity types that support team-based sharing.

entity_id.description: Mongo `_id` (24-char hex ObjectId) of the record to share.

team_id.description: Mongo `_id` of the `Team` in the current tenant.

mode.description:
- `merge` — team members are added to the existing `access_dict`;
  pre-existing entries for other users are preserved. Team entries
  overwrite pre-existing entries for the same user.
- `replace` — `access_dict` is fully replaced by the team's access
  map. Record owner (`record.userid`) still retains access via the
  native owner branch of `generate_query_for_access()`.

access_dict.description: The record's full `access_dict` AFTER the operation.

applied_team_ids.description: All team ids currently applied to the record (deduplicated).

added_userids.description: Every member of the team, including users who already had an entry.

removed_userids.description: User ids dropped from `access_dict` by this call.

TenantAIProvidersView.description: A company's own AI setup. Never carries a key or token.

mode.description: own = AI calls use this setup now

managed_by_ambivo.description: Staff set the company up on another gateway. Writes are refused.

default_model.description: Sent as the model name when the call names none. "" = none.

key_stored.description: A gateway key is stored for the company.

can_enable.description: Key stored and the last test since the last save passed.

message.example: Run a test that works before you switch over.

gateway_detail.description: The gateway's own reason, with secrets removed.

TenantAIRoutingRule.description:
First match wins at the gateway. `when` conditions are ANDed. `when` is
required and must have at least one condition (null, `[]` and `{}` are
refused); for a rule that matches every call use `{"min_chars": 0}`.
Rule text may not carry control characters (NUL included).

when.description:
`min_chars` must not be above `max_chars`. `regex` and `owner` are
refused with GENAI_BAD_REQUEST, except a rule that is exactly equal
to one already stored at the gateway (set by Ambivo staff): Core
reads the stored rules first and passes such a rule on unchanged.
A new or changed `regex`/`owner` rule is refused.

contains.description: Case-insensitive substring of the prompt. Text or a list of 1 to 50 (counted after trimming and de-duplicating), each up to 200 characters.

TenantAIGuardrails.description:
The whole set. On PUT a field left out is cleared. Lists are trimmed
and de-duplicated before their limits are counted. No control
characters in any text (`system_prompt` may keep line breaks and tabs).

Network rules (CIDRs, countries) judge the signed-in user's IP address
for AI calls made directly in Core (the gateway honours
`X-AMBIVO-END-USER-IP`). Knowledge chat (vectordb calls Core with the
internal secret) and workflows skip them. Core sends that header only
for a request signed in with a user's JWT, and
only when the address is public (globally routable). Calls with no
signed-in user (internal-secret service calls, Celery, workflows), or
from a private address, skip these rules. A server-side caller that
forwards a user's JWT (FAPI, Books, MCP) is judged by its own egress
address.

system_prompt.description: Prepended as a system message to every chat call.

allowed_cidrs.description: IPs or CIDR ranges, v4 or v6. A scoped address (with `%`) is refused.

allowed_countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Lower case is upper-cased.

timezone.description: IANA zone for allowed_hours. Null is UTC.

TenantAISettings.description: Routing, guardrails and budget of the company's config set. Conversation memory is not exposed.

monthly_budget_usd.description: Null is no limit, or the budget read at the gateway failed.

spent_this_month_usd.description: Null when the budget read at the gateway failed; the rest of the settings still come back.

msg.description:
Human-readable error. Known values include:
- `missing: entity_type, entity_id, team_id` (400)
- `entity_type '<x>' not supported for team sharing` (400)
- `invalid entity_id` (400)
- `team_id is required` (400)
- `team not found for current tenant` (400)
- `record not found for current tenant` (400)
- `mode must be 'merge' or 'replace'` (400)
- `insufficient privileges on target record` (403)
- `caller is not a member of this team` (403)
- `internal error` (500)

CompanyProfile.description:
A letterhead: the company details printed on a document a customer
receives. Scope is `(tenant_id, books_entity_id, site_code)` and **blank
is a wildcard on both**, so one profile can cover a whole tenant, one
Books company, one site, or one company at one site.

books_entity_id.description: The Books company this applies to. Blank matches every company.

site_code.description: The site this applies to. Blank matches every site.

dba_name.description: The trading name. Printed in preference to legal_name.

logo_att_id.description: Attachment id of the logo. Read `logo_url` instead of resolving this.

logo_url.description: Resolved on read; not a stored field.

tax_id_label.description: What to call the tax id on the document — VAT, GST, EIN.

is_active.description: Deactivating retains the row, because documents already issued reference it.

CompanyProfileWrite.description: Fields accepted when creating or updating a profile. A profile needs `dba_name` or `legal_name`. `logo_att_id` cannot be set here; the avatar upload sets it.

CompanyBrand.description:
The render-ready view a document template receives.

**`company_name` is the printed headline** and is `dba_name` falling back
to `legal_name`. Templates read that one key, so setting a DBA changes what
prints with no template edit.

The render environment is strict about undefined names, and templates live
in the database while code deploys separately — so a template reading a key
this object does not carry fails the whole document. Read new keys
defensively.

address.description: address_lines joined with commas, for single-line layouts.

SitePicklistItem.description:
One physical place. A site is independent of a Books company: one company
spans many sites, which is why the company id hangs off the site.

label.description: The site name, or the code when there is no name.

code.description: The site's identifier everywhere else in the platform. A site with no code is invisible to every site mechanism and can never be mapped.

books_entity_id.description: Which Books company documents raised at this site post to. Blank means the tenant default.

EntityShortcode.description:
A public share link. The code is the capability, so every limit lives on
the link rather than on the caller.

public_url.description: The link to hand to the recipient.

max_accesses.description: The string `unlimited` when no cap was set.

is_protected.description: True when the link has an access code.

EntityShortcodeRecord.description:
A stored share link, as listed by `GET /entity/shortcode`. These are the
raw records, so the code is in `code` and there is no `url` or `public_url`.
They include the caller's own internal fields (`access_code`, `private_note`,
`recipient`). Dashboard items come from a separate store and carry fewer fields.

post.description:
Centralized CRUD for `tenant.site_list` — the registry of office/site codes. A site `code` is the shared vocabulary used by both `role.open_assignment_group_code` (which site a role belongs to) and each record's `site_code` (which site owns the record), so this is the single place a code is minted. The returned `site_list` is the source for the site dropdown on entity forms and the OAG dropdown on the role editor. Admin-only (tenant admin of the target tenant, or superadmin).

Failures return `result: 2` with an `error_code` and a `msg`, plus `site_code` where it applies. Codes: `NOT_TENANT_ADMIN`, `TENANT_NOT_FOUND`, `SITE_CODE_REQUIRED`, `DUPLICATE_SITE_CODE`, `SITE_CODE_NOT_FOUND`, `SITE_ADDRESS_NOT_FOUND`, `LOCATION_CODE_REQUIRED`, `LOCATION_CODE_EXISTS`, `LOCATION_CODE_NOT_FOUND`, `UNSUPPORTED_ACTION` and `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

action.description:
Defaults to `list` when omitted. `list` returns the current site_list; `add` appends a new site (rejects a duplicate code); `update` edits an existing site matched by `code` (the code itself is immutable — rename via deactivate + add); `deactivate` soft-disables a site (never hard-deletes, preserving history on records and roles still referencing it).

`add_location` / `deactivate_location` manage the AREAS within one site, in `site_list[].location_list[]`. A site is a physical address — a warehouse, a retail store, the cafe the workforce clocks in at. A location is an area inside it (kitchen, front counter, storage, receiving dock) and is where inventory is held; bins sit below a location and are free-form. They are nested under the site rather than being a registry of their own because a location has no meaning apart from its site — "storage" names a different room in every warehouse — so **the same `location_code` at two different sites is legal and expected**, while a duplicate within one site is refused with `LOCATION_CODE_EXISTS`. Like a site code, a location code is immutable and is deactivated rather than deleted, because stock rows and history point at it.

code.description: Site code, e.g. "HB", "OFFICE_A". Required for add/update/deactivate. Immutable once created.

location_code.description: The area within the site. Required for `add_location` and `deactivate_location`, alongside `code` (the site). Immutable once created. Unknown site returns `SITE_CODE_NOT_FOUND`; a duplicate within the same site returns `LOCATION_CODE_EXISTS`.

kind.description: Optional free-text classification of a location, e.g. `retail`, `prep`, `store`, `dock`. Descriptive only — nothing branches on it.

is_active.description: Whether the site is active. Absent is treated as active (back-compat). Inactive sites are excluded from dropdowns and code validation. Send a JSON boolean: `update` stores the value as sent, so the string "false" reads as active.

is_primary.description: Marks the tenant's primary site. Defaults to false on `add`.

books_entity_id.description: Optional Ambivo Books entity that owns this site's activity. Blank means the tenant's only or current entity.

latitude.description: Optional map pin, sent together with `longitude`. Without both, the server looks the address up on the map.

longitude.description: Optional map pin, sent together with `latitude`.

clock_in_near_site.description: When true, a phone clock-in for a shift here is refused when it is too far from the site. Needs a site position, else `SITE_ADDRESS_NOT_FOUND`.

200.description: Site registry updated; returns the full current site_list.

post.summary: Upload a file (e.g. the tenant avatar / logo)
post.description:
Generic multipart file-upload endpoint. The uploaded file is stored and bound to an owning entity via `storefile_custom_fields.entity_type` + `storefile_custom_fields.entity_id`, with its role given by `storefile_file_purpose`.

**Setting the tenant avatar / logo.** Upload the image with `storefile_file_purpose: "avatar"` and bind it to the tenant — `storefile_custom_fields.entity_type: "tenant"` and `storefile_custom_fields.entity_id: <tenant id>`. The returned `att_id` becomes the tenant's `avatar`, and the tenant's `avatar_url` is refreshed on the next `GET /user/admin/tenant` (clients typically re-fetch the tenant after a successful upload).

The same endpoint stores CRM record attachments — differing only by purpose and binding, e.g. `entity_type: "installed_base"` or `entity_type: "purchase_order"` with `entity_id` set to the record id.

Content type is `multipart/form-data`. Only form fields whose names start with `storefile` are read. `storefile_custom_fields` is one field holding a JSON string, e.g. `{"entity_type":"tenant","entity_id":"<tenant id>"}`. Bracket keys such as `storefile_custom_fields[entity_type]` are ignored. Any signed-in user can upload; the bound record must be in the caller's tenant.

storefile.description: The binary file to upload. For a tenant avatar this is the image (PNG/JPG). The filename is sanitized server-side.

storefile_file_purpose.description: Role of the uploaded file. Use `avatar` to set the tenant avatar/logo; `store_file` for a generic stored file / attachment.

storefile_custom_fields.description: Entity binding for the file, sent as one JSON string. Its keys are listed below. Bracketed multipart keys are ignored. It may also carry `folder_id` and `is_draft`.

entity_type.description: Owning entity type. `tenant` for the tenant avatar; a CRM object key (e.g. `installed_base`, `purchase_order`, `contact`) for a record attachment.

entity_id.description: Id of the owning entity. For the tenant avatar this is the tenant id.

storefile_is_draft.description: When true the file is stored as a draft (used by record attachment fields before the record is persisted). Omit for a tenant avatar. A field named plain `is_draft` is ignored.

storefile_folder_id.description: Optional file-manager folder id (defaults to `-1`). A field named plain `folder_id` is ignored.

storefile_app_context.description: The front-end application the upload came from (`crm`, `asset_base`, `books`, `knowledge_hub`, …), lower `snake_case`. Stamped on the stored file so app-scoped listings can filter on it. Omit it and the file inherits the `app_context` of the folder it lands in; at the drive root with nothing to inherit it is stored blank, which reads as the default (`crm`) context. Not applicable to `storefile_file_purpose: "avatar"` — avatars and chat attachments belong to no app's drive.

200.description: File stored. An avatar upload (`storefile_file_purpose: avatar`) returns only `result`, `att_id` and `temp_url`. Other uploads return the stored file details.

att_id.description: Avatar uploads only. The id that becomes the record's `avatar`.

temp_url.description: Avatar uploads only. A signed URL for the image.

file_details.description: The stored file record (id, url, name, and entity binding). Not returned for avatar uploads.

post.summary: Create, update, delete or copy a file-manager folder
post.description:
Action-dispatched folder management. `action` is one of `create` / `add`,
`update`, `update_many`, `delete`, `delete_many`, `copy`.

### `action: "copy"`

Recursively duplicates a folder: every descendant folder is recreated and
every file in the tree gets its **own S3 object** and `stored_files`
record. The root folder `"-1"` cannot be copied, a folder cannot be copied
into itself or into one of its own subfolders, and a tree whose files sum
to more than **500 MB** is rejected before anything is written.

`parent_folder_id` is the destination (defaults to the source's own
parent, so an omitted value copies the folder beside itself). `name`
defaults to `Copy of <source name>`, then `Copy of <source name> (2)` and
so on, so repeated copies into one parent never collide.

**Filing the copy under a record.** `entity_type` + `entity_id` on a copy
request are the *destination context*, not a filter — they are stamped on
the new root folder, on every copied subfolder and on every copied file,
so a folder from the generic drive can be copied *into* a contact, lead,
account, order, invoice or property:

| `entity_type` / `entity_id` | Result |
|---|---|
| both supplied | the whole copied tree is filed under that record |
| both empty strings | the copy is detached — plain drive, no record |
| both omitted | the copy inherits whatever the source was filed under |

The record must exist in the caller's tenant and, when it carries an
`access_dict`, must be readable by the caller; entity types the platform
does not register (custom modules, `contract_template`) are accepted
as-is. `property` and `property_floor_plan` also populate `property_id` /
`fp_id` on the copies. Supplying only one of the pair is an error.

The copy inherits the **source's** `access_dict`; filing it under a record
does not re-derive sharing from that record. A copied KB folder is created
as a plain folder, and the copy is never public even if the source was.

action.description: When omitted, the request is handled as `update`.

folder_id.description: The folder being updated / deleted / copied. Required for `update` and `copy`. Without it, those actions return `result: 1` and change nothing. `"-1"` (the virtual root) cannot be copied.

parent_folder_id.description: Destination parent. For `copy` it defaults to the source folder's own parent; `"-1"` places the copy at the drive root.

name.description: Name for the new/updated folder. On `copy`, defaults to `Copy of <source name>` (de-duplicated within the parent).

entity_type.description: Destination entity type for a `copy` (e.g. `contact`, `lead`, `account`, `order`, `invoice`, `property`). Empty string detaches the copy; omit to inherit the source's.

entity_id.description: Id of the destination record. Must be supplied together with `entity_type` and must exist in the caller's tenant.

is_custom_module_entity.description: Set when `entity_type` is a custom module, so the copies are marked as belonging to a custom-module record. Declared by the caller, never inherited from the source.

app_context.description: The application the folder belongs to (`crm`, `asset_base`, `books`, …), lower `snake_case`. On `create`/`add` it is stamped on the new folder; omit it and a subfolder inherits its parent's, while a folder created at the root is stored blank (which reads as the default `crm` context). On `copy` it re-files the whole copied tree into that app; omit it and the copy keeps the source's. See the `Files` tag description.

copyIntoContact.summary: Copy a folder into a contact's context

copyDetached.summary: Copy an entity-scoped folder out into the generic drive

200.description: Always HTTP 200; check `result` (`1` success, `2` failure) and `msg`.

folder.description: The service result. Note the nesting — the created/updated folder document is at `folder.folder`.

copied_file_count.description: Files copied across the whole tree (`copy` only).

failed_file_count.description: Files that could not be copied (`copy` only). The copy still succeeds; `msg` names the count.

entity_context.description: Echo of the destination context actually applied. Present only when the request supplied `entity_type`, `entity_id` or `app_context`. `app_context` appears in the echo only when the request named one.

msg.description: Error message when `result` is `2`, e.g. `contact <id> was not found in this account`, `entity_type and entity_id must be supplied together to file the copy under an entity`, `The root folder cannot be copied`, or the folder-size limit.

rejected.summary: Destination record does not exist in this tenant

value.msg: contact 5d2f5127a5e67f11bc523bff was not found in this account

post.summary: Get, update, delete, copy or resolve URLs for stored files
post.description:
Action-dispatched file management. `action` is one of `get`, `update`,
`update_many`, `delete`, `delete_many`, `copy`, `copy_many`, `get_url`,
`get_image_content`, `resize`.

### `action: "get_url"`

A short-lived link to the file (`file_url`, and `pdf_url` for documents). The caller may open
a file they uploaded or that was shared with them. A file uploaded onto a **custom object
record** (`storefile_custom_fields` with `entity_type`, `entity_id` and
`is_custom_module_entity: true`) also opens for anyone who may read that record: `R` on the
object and `R` on the record, as a read of the record checks. A file that is missing, in
another company, or not open to the caller answers
`{"result": 2, "error_code": "FILE_NOT_FOUND", "msg": "File not found, or you do not have access to it"}`.

### `action: "copy"` / `action: "copy_many"`

Duplicates one file (`file_id`) or several (`file_ids_list`). Each copy
gets its **own S3 object** and `stored_files` record, so deleting either
side never touches the other; presigned links, share ids, CDN publication
and index state are dropped from the copy. A file larger than **500 MB**
is refused.

`folder_id` is the destination folder and defaults to the file's own.
Naming follows the destination: copying into a *different* folder keeps
the original name, copying beside the original yields
`Copy of <name>`, then `Copy of <name> (2)`. An explicit `name` (single
`copy` only) always wins.

`entity_type` + `entity_id` behave exactly as on the folder copy — they
name the *destination record* the copy is filed under, both-empty
detaches, and omitting both inherits the source's association. See the
`Files` tag description for the shared rules.

A caller only copies what they can already reach: a tenant admin reaches
every file of the tenant, anyone else only files they own or that are
shared with them. In `copy_many` an unreachable or missing id does not
fail the request — it lands in `failed_file_ids` and the rest still copy.

file_ids_list.description: The files to copy. Required for `action: "copy_many"`.

folder_id.description: Destination folder for the copy; defaults to the source file's own folder. `"-1"` is the drive root. Must be a folder the caller can access.

name.description: Name for the copy (single `copy` only). Defaults as described above.

entity_type.description: Destination entity type. Empty string detaches the copy; omit to inherit the source's.

entity_id.description: Id of the destination record; must be supplied together with `entity_type` and exist in the caller's tenant.

is_custom_module_entity.description: Set when `entity_type` is a custom module.

app_context.description: Re-files the copy into that application (`crm`, `asset_base`, `books`, …), lower `snake_case`. Omit it and the copy keeps the source file's. See the `Files` tag description.

copyFileIntoContact.summary: Copy one file into a contact's context

copyManyIntoFolder.summary: Copy several files into another folder, filed under a lead

200.description: Always HTTP 200; check `result` (`1` success, `2` failure) and `msg`.

result.description: `1` when at least one file was copied, `2` otherwise.

file.description: The new file document — `copy` only (for `copy_many` read `files`).

files.description: Every file document created by this request.

failed_file_ids.description: Ids that could not be copied — missing, not accessible to the caller, or failed mid-copy (see server logs).

entity_context.description: Echo of the destination context actually applied. Present only when the request supplied `entity_type`, `entity_id` or `app_context`. `app_context` appears in the echo only when the request named one.

msg.description: Error or partial-failure message, e.g. `file_id is required to copy a file`, `destination folder not found, or you do not have access to it`, `contact <id> was not found in this account`, `1 of 2 files could not be copied` (`copy_many`).

copiedOne.summary: One file copied into a contact

partial.summary: copy_many where one id was not reachable

value.msg: 1 of 2 files could not be copied

get.summary: List the folders and files inside one folder
get.description:
The file manager's directory listing: subfolders and files of a single
folder returned as **one interleaved, paginated collection**, so a page
is a page of the directory rather than a page of each.

Each entry carries a `type` of `folder` or `file` and, per type, the flat
fields listed under the response schema. File entries are enriched with a
freshly signed `url` / `file_url`; folder entries with their immediate
`file_count` / `folder_count`.

### Grouping and ordering

With `folders_first: true` (the default) folders occupy the head of the
listing and files follow, each group ordered by `sort_by` / `sort_order`.
Set it to `false` to sort folders and files together as one sequence —
note that folders have no size, so under `sort_by: "size"` they sort as
zero.

### Scoping

Beyond `folder_id`, a listing can be narrowed by:

- `app_context` — the application the records were created in. See the
  `Files` tag description; `crm` also matches the records that predate
  the field.
- `entity_type` + `entity_id`: only `property` and `property_floor_plan`
  narrow the listing. They are translated to `property_id` / `fp_id`.
  Any other type is ignored, and the whole folder comes back. To filter
  by another record, put `entity_type` and `entity_id` in `match_filter_dict`.
- `match_filter_dict` — a JSON object of additional field conditions.
  Keys that are not real fields of the file/folder record are **silently
  dropped**, and a condition is applied only to the side that actually
  has that field.

Results are always access-filtered: a tenant admin sees the whole
tenant's drive, anyone else sees what they own or what is shared with
them.

parameters.name: folder_id
parameters.description: Folder to list. `"-1"` is the virtual drive root.

parameters.name: app_context
parameters.description: Restrict the listing to one application (`crm`, `asset_base`, `books`, `knowledge_hub`, …), lower `snake_case`. Values are normalized, so `"Asset Base"` and `asset_base` are the same drive. Omit it to list every application's records, which is what callers that predate `app_context` do. `crm` additionally returns records created before the field existed.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Items per page, clamped to 1–500.

parameters.name: page_num
parameters.description: 1-based page number.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: Anything else falls back to `name`. Folders have no size, so under `size` they are ordered by name.

parameters.name: folders_first
parameters.description: `true` groups all folders ahead of all files; `false` sorts the two together as one sequence.

parameters.name: search_text
parameters.description: Free-text match against the folder / file records.

parameters.name: entity_type
parameters.description: Only `property` and `property_floor_plan` are used. They are translated to `property_id` / `fp_id`. Other types (e.g. `contact`) are ignored, so use `match_filter_dict` to filter by them.

parameters.name: entity_id
parameters.description: Id of the property or floor plan named by `entity_type`.

parameters.name: property_id
parameters.description: Restrict to a property's files. Validated against the caller's tenant; an unknown id fails the request.

parameters.name: fp_id
parameters.description: Restrict to a property floor plan's files.

parameters.name: room_id
parameters.description: Restrict to a chat room's files.

parameters.name: match_filter_dict
parameters.description: Extra conditions as a JSON object (may be sent as a JSON string). Only keys that are genuine fields of the record are honoured — an unrecognised key is dropped rather than reported. `tenant_id` and `folder_id` are ignored here; use `folder_id` above. An `app_context` placed in here is normalized exactly like the parameter.

items.description: The page, folders and files interleaved. Read `type` to tell them apart.

folder_id.description: On a folder entry, the folder's own id; on a file entry, the folder containing it.

post.description:
Perform create, read, update, delete, and other operations on leads
by setting the `action` field in the request body.

**Route aliases:** `/user/lead` and `/user/lead/manage_contacts`

**Supported actions:**
- `add` — Create a new lead. `payload` holds the lead fields and must carry `email_list` or
  `phone_list`; a plain `email` field is ignored and the add is refused with no message.
- `update` — Update one lead. `lead_id` goes at the TOP LEVEL of the body, next to `action`;
  `payload` holds only the fields to change.
- `update_many` — Updates one lead, the same as `update`. It takes one top-level `lead_id`.
- `delete` — Delete one lead. `lead_id` at the top level.
  Only a tenant admin, the lead's owner, or a manager whose team holds the owner may delete it.
  Anyone else gets `{"result": 2, "data": {"error_code": "ACCESS_DENIED", ...}}` and nothing is
  touched: the lead, its tasks and its attachments stay. A missing lead answers `LEAD_NOT_FOUND`.
- `delete_many` — Delete several. `lead_ids_list` (array of ids) at the top level.
  The reply is result 1 even when no lead was deleted. Check `data.lead_ids_deleted_list`.
- `get` — One lead with `lead_id` at the top level, or a page of leads without it. Either way the
  leads come back in `data.lead_contacts` (a list), with `total_count`.
- `export` — Export leads matching filter criteria. `match_filter_dict`, `sort_dict` and
  `export_settings` go at the top level.
- `find_duplicates` — Find leads that share an email or phone. Send top-level `email_list`
  and `phone_list` as arrays of plain strings.
- `merge_records` — Merge duplicate leads into one. `payload` carries `entity_ids_list` (the leads to
  merge) and `reference_id` (the lead that is kept).
- `get_vcard` — Export lead as vCard.
- `get_entity_ids` — Get the leads named in top-level `entity_ids`. They come back in `data.values`.

**`lead_id` is read from the top level** (`{"action": "update", "lead_id": "...", "payload": {...}}`).
`update` and `delete` also accept a top-level `id`. `get` reads only `lead_id`.
An id inside `payload` is not read: the call fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` "missing lead_id".

**`lead_source` must be a known value**, or it is saved as `Unknown` with no error: one of Google,
Facebook, Youtube, Reddit, Snapchat, Craigslist, Yelp, Linkedin, Incoming-Call, SMS, Referral, Bing,
Yahoo, Nextdoor, Unknown, TikTok, Instagram, Billboard Ad, or one of the tenant's marketing sources.
**`lead_status`** is one of open, assigned, attempted, contacted, meeting-setup, disqualified, incorrect,
or one of the tenant's custom lead statuses.

**A lead linked to a sign-in account.** A lead with `registered_userid` belongs to a user
(`user.linked_lead_id` points back). Its email is the first `email_list` entry and
its phone the first `phone_list` number. An `update` that changes either saves the lead, but
never writes the new address or number onto the user: the user is asked to confirm it, as
`POST /user/contact/change` would. A code goes to the NEW address (by email) or number (by
text, read as E.164 the way sign-in reads it), and a notice to the old address or the
account's email. The person keeps signing in with the old one until they send
`POST /user/contact/change` `{"action": "confirm", "code": ..., "password": ...}` while signed
in. The same address asked for again while its code still works sends nothing new.

The `update` answer's `data` then carries one of these markers per field:

| Key | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `user_email_pending_confirmation` | `true` | the code was sent to the new email |
| `user_email_not_synced` | `EMAIL_EMPTY`, `EMAIL_INVALID`, `EMAIL_IN_USE`, `CONFIRMATION_UNAVAILABLE`, `CONFIRMATION_RATE_LIMITED` | nothing was started; the user keeps the old email |
| `user_phone_pending_confirmation` | `true` | the code was sent to the new number |
| `user_phone_not_synced` | `PHONE_EMPTY`, `PHONE_INVALID`, `PHONE_IN_USE`, `CONFIRMATION_UNAVAILABLE`, `CONFIRMATION_RATE_LIMITED` | nothing was started; the user keeps the old phone |

`EMAIL_INVALID` covers placeholders (`FAKE_...`, `...@invalid.ambivo.com`, a generated
`guest_..._..._...@ambivo.com`). `EMAIL_IN_USE` is any other active account's primary or
verified alternate email (a guest elsewhere counts only in its own tenant). `PHONE_IN_USE` is a
number verified on another active account of the company. `CONFIRMATION_UNAVAILABLE`: the
person cannot confirm (a placeholder email or no usable sign-in, or no password and no other
proven contact). No marker means nothing changed for the user. `merge_records` starts the same
confirmation for the kept lead but carries no marker.

`registered_userid` is never a client's: `update` (and imports) skip it in the payload.

lead_id.description: The lead, for `get` (one lead), `update`, `update_many` and `delete`. Top level, never inside `payload`.

lead_ids_list.description: The leads to delete, for `delete_many`. Top level.

email_list.description: For `find_duplicates`. Plain email strings. Top level.

phone_list.description: For `find_duplicates`. Plain phone strings. Top level.

entity_ids.description: For `get_entity_ids`. The lead ids to return. Top level.

payload.description:
Action-specific payload:
- **add**: lead fields, with `email_list` or `phone_list` (see Lead schema).
  Send `email_list`; a plain `email` field gets a bare `result: 2`.
- **update / update_many**: only the fields to change
- **merge_records**: `{ "entity_ids_list": ["<id1>", "<id2>"], "reference_id": "<id kept>" }`

Send `lead_source` exactly as listed, matching case. Any other value is saved as `Unknown`.

get_success.summary: Lead retrieved (one lead, by top-level lead_id; still a list)

get.description:
Retrieve leads with multiple view modes controlled by the `action`
query parameter:

- **`get`** (default) — Paginated flat list with filtering and sorting
- **`get_kanban`** — Leads grouped by **`lead_status`** for Kanban board
  rendering. Each status bucket contains its own `leads` array, `total`
  count, `has_more` flag, and `last_id` cursor. Supports cursor-based
  "load more" within a single column via `stage` + `last_id`.
- **`export`** — Export with `export_settings`

**Route aliases:** `/user/lead` and `/user/lead/manage_contacts`.

**Kanban notes:**
- Columns come from `LeadContacts.status_value_list`; any custom
  statuses present in the tenant's data are appended to `stage_order`.
- Access scope matches the list view: tenant admins see all tenant
  leads; non-admins see owner + shared + team (access-dict) leads.
- Uses MongoDB `$facet` for a single-round-trip multi-column load;
  cursor pagination per column via `last_id` (not page numbers).

parameters.name: action
parameters.description:
View mode:
- `get` — Standard paginated list (default)
- `get_kanban` — Kanban board grouped by `lead_status`
- `export` — Export with `export_settings`

parameters.description: Number of records per page

parameters.name: page_num
parameters.description: Page number (1-indexed)

parameters.name: match_filter_dict

JSON-encoded filter object. Examples:
- `{"lead_status": "new"}`
- `{"lead_source": "website", "lead_status": "qualified"}`
- `{"tags": {"$in": ["enterprise"]}}`

parameters.description: JSON-encoded sort object. Example: `{"created_ts": -1}` for newest first.

**Kanban only.** JSON array of `lead_status` values to include.

**Kanban only.** Load more leads for this `lead_status` column.
Used with `last_id` for cursor pagination within that column.

**Kanban only.** The `_id` of the last lead from the previous page
within `stage`. Records with `_id` less than this value are returned.

parameters.description:
Read by `action=get_kanban` only. The list ignores it.
A guest's `tenant_scope` is ignored.

Delete leads by passing IDs as query parameters. Accepts multiple parameter names
for flexibility: `lead_ids`, `lead_ids_list`, or the generic `ids_list`.

Values from query strings arrive as strings — the server parses them with `ast.literal_eval()`.

parameters.description:
JSON-encoded array of lead IDs to delete.
Example: `["682a3f1ccfe7072567e038cb", "682a3f1ccfe7072567e038cc"]`

Also accepts `lead_ids` or `lead_ids_list` as the parameter name.

post.summary: Convert a lead to a contact
