Convert a lead into a contact record. The lead's data is copied to a new
contact, or to the existing contact with the same email. The lead is marked
`converted_to_contact: true`. A lead in `disqualified` or `incorrect` status is refused.

lead_id.description: ID of the lead to convert

to_userid.description: Owner of the new contact. Defaults to the lead's owner.

product_ids_list.description: Products to attach to the contact's opportunity.

200.description: Conversion result. The reply has no `data` key.

converted_contact_dict.description: The contact record. Its id is in `id`.

post.summary: Bulk-convert up to 100 leads to contacts
post.description:
Convert multiple qualified leads to contacts in a single request. Per-lead
failures do not abort the batch — each lead's outcome (success or specific
error) is returned as an element of the `response` array. Hard cap of
**100 ids per request**.

The id list may be supplied under `lead_ids_list` (preferred), `lead_ids`,
or `ids_list`. Alternatively, supply `from_entity_list_id` to load the
ids from a saved `user_entity_list` (scoped to the caller's tenant+userid,
`entity_type: "lead"`).

Optional `to_userid` reassigns ownership of every resulting contact. It
is validated once up-front; if the target user lacks contact read
privilege the entire request is rejected before any conversion runs.

to_userid.description:
Optional userid that should own every resulting contact.
Must belong to the same tenant and have contact read privilege.

product_ids_list.description: Product/property ids applied to every converted lead's opportunity.

from_entity_list_id.description:
`_id` of a `user_entity_list` document (tenant+userid scoped,
`entity_type: "lead"`). When present, its `entity_ids_list` is
used as the lead id list.

200.description:
Request completed. Inspect `response[*].success` for per-lead outcomes.
`result` is `1` whenever the request itself executed successfully,
even if some individual leads failed.

converted_contact_dict.description: Present when `success=true`. The resulting contact document.

error.description:
Present when `success=false`. One of `LEAD_NOT_FOUND`,
`LEAD_DISQUALIFIED`, or `<ExceptionName>: <args>` for
other service errors.

400.description:
Whole-request validation error. Possible `error` / `error_code` values:
- `missing lead_ids_list` — no id list supplied
- `BULK_CONVERT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — more than 100 ids submitted
- `INVALID_TO_OWNER` — `to_userid` not found in tenant
- `TO_OWNER_DOES_NOT_HAVE_CONTACT_PRIVILEGE` — `to_userid` lacks contact read privilege
- `TENANT_MISSING` — session has no tenant context

post.description:
Import leads from a JSON array. Each row is added as a new lead.

post.description:

To find duplicate leads, use `POST /user/lead` with `action: find_duplicates`.

post.description:
Perform create, read, update, delete, and other operations on opportunities
by setting the `action` field in the request body.

**Route aliases:** `/user/opportunity` and `/user/opportunities/manage`

**Supported actions:**
- `add` — Create a new opportunity. Payload contains opportunity fields.
- `update` — Update one opportunity. `opportunity_id` goes at the top level.
- `delete` — Delete one opportunity. `opportunity_id` at the top level.
  Only a tenant admin or the opportunity's owner may delete it. Anyone else gets `ACCESS_DENIED`
  and nothing is touched (tasks, orders, attachments and Books entries stay). A missing one answers
  `OPPORTUNITY_NOT_FOUND`.
- `get` — One opportunity with top-level `opportunity_id`, or a page without it. Rows come back
  in `data.opportunities`, with `total_count` and `last_id`.
- `get_entity_ids` — Get the opportunities named in top-level `entity_ids`. They come back in `data.values`.

`opportunity_id` is read from the top level. A top-level `id` is also accepted. An id inside `payload` is not read.
To delete several opportunities, use `DELETE /user/opportunity`.

**Note:** Export is available via GET only: `GET /user/opportunities/manage?action=export`

**Company and site.** On `add`, the company (`books_entity_id`) comes from
the payload, or else from the company of the opportunity's site. When the
company sent differs from the site's company, the opportunity is still
saved as sent. This can be an intercompany transfer. The response then
has `data.warnings`, a list with this message: "Site {site_code} belongs
to another company. This was saved with the company you chose. Check
that is intended, for example an intercompany transfer."

On `update`, `books_entity_id` is never changed. A `site_code` that is
absent or unchanged does nothing. A new `site_code` must be a site set
up for the tenant. Its company must be the company already on the
opportunity. A blank company on either side means the default company.
Otherwise the update is refused with `result: 2`, and `error.message`
holds one of these messages. `error_code` is the same text upper-cased with underscores.
- "Site {site_code} is not set up for this workspace."
- "Site {site_code} belongs to a different company. The company on this
  opportunity cannot change. Create a new opportunity at site {site_code}."

opportunity_id.description: The opportunity, for `get`, `update` and `delete`. Top level.

entity_ids.description: For `get_entity_ids`. The opportunity ids to return. Top level.

payload.description: Field values for `add` and `update` (see Opportunity schema).

- **`get`** (default) — Paginated flat list with filtering and sorting
- **`get_kanban`** — Records grouped by pipeline stage for Kanban board rendering.
  Each stage bucket contains its own `opportunities` array, `total` count, and
  `has_more` flag. Supports cursor-based "load more" within a single stage via
  `stage` + `last_id`.
- **`export`** — Full dataset for CSV/JSON export

Both `/user/opportunity` and `/user/opportunities/manage` resolve to the same handler.

**Kanban implementation notes:**
- Uses MongoDB `$facet` aggregation for efficient multi-stage loading
- Supports cursor-based pagination per stage with `last_id` (not page numbers)
- Returns stage counts even when only loading a subset of records
- Access scope matches the list view: tenant admins see all tenant
  opportunities; non-admins see owner + shared + team (access-dict)
  opportunities

  contract_pending, closed_won, closed_lost

get.summary: List the letterheads this tenant prints under
get.description:
A **company profile** is the letterhead a document prints under: DBA and
legal name, logo, address, tax id, remit-to and invoice footer.

Scope is `(tenant_id, books_entity_id, site_code)`, and **blank is a
wildcard on both** — so one profile can cover the whole tenant, a single
Books company, a single site, or one company at one site. Resolution
picks the most specific match; see `/user/company_profile/resolve`.

`brand.company_name` is the printed headline and is `dba_name` falling
back to `legal_name`. Existing document templates already read that one
key, so a tenant that sets a DBA starts printing it with no template edit.

**Tenant admin only.** These are the details printed on documents a

get.description:
Answers the resolution without rendering anything — useful for showing a
user which branding a document is about to carry.

Both parameters are optional and either may be blank, because blank is a
wildcard in the profile's own scope.

**`brand: null` is not an error.** It means no profile applies and the
document will print under the tenant's own name and avatar. `source` says
which of the two happened, so a caller is told rather than having to infer
it from an absence.

**Tenant admin only.** The row is **retained and flagged inactive**, not

post.summary: Email an invoice to its customer
post.description:
Renders the invoice under its resolved letterhead (see
`/user/company_profile/resolve`) and queues it for delivery.

**The reply says `queued`, never `delivered`.** Sending goes onto an event
queue that a periodic callback drains later, and every real failure there
— all recipients filtered, a lapsed OAuth mailbox, no transport — is
logged rather than returned. A synchronous "delivered" would be a
fabrication.

Documents are mailed as a **link**, not an attachment: the underlying send
event carries `cc_list` but takes no attachments.

Send history is recorded on the invoice's `meta`, deliberately **not** on
`email_list` — that field's first entry is what the QuickBooks export
builds `BillEmail` from, so writing a send record there would displace the
address QBO reads.

email_to.description: A single address or a list; the service normalises both. Entries without "@" are dropped. When none is left, the invoice goes to the customer contact.

template_id.description: A specific document template. Omit to use the tenant's default.

200.description: Rendered, and queued unless `queued` says otherwise

queued.description: False means the invoice rendered but could not be queued. True means accepted for sending, not delivered.

400.description:
`MISSING_ARGUMENT`, `INVOICE_ID_NOT_FOUND`, `INVOICE_NO_RECIPIENT`,
`DOCUMENT_TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND` (seed or author a template — not a render
failure), `DOCUMENT_RENDER_FAILED`, or `INVOICE_SEND_FAILED`.

get.summary: The tenant's sites, for a Site dropdown
get.description:
A **site** is a physical place; a Books **company** is a legal boundary.
They are independent axes and one company spans many sites, which is why a
site carries `books_entity_id` rather than the other way round.

A site with no `code` is invisible to every site mechanism and can never be
mapped — the auto-seeded "Main Office" has none.
Primary site first, then by label. `INTERNAL_ERROR` on an unexpected
failure.

Reads the place registry. Active bins only unless `include_inactive` is true. At most 500 rows. Refusals: `SITE_CODE_REQUIRED`, `LOCATION_CODE_REQUIRED`, `SITE_CODE_NOT_FOUND`, `LOCATION_CODE_NOT_FOUND`.

Inventory posts to Books through a handshake: **Core computes the journal
entry and Books validates and records it.** This lists the movements that
did not land, with the reason each one is stuck, so a failed posting is
visible rather than silently absent from the ledger.

Paged with `page_num` and `page_size`, and filtered with
`match_filter_dict`. The full contract is in the inventory spec.

post.summary: Generate (print) a document, or send it for e-signature
post.description:
Render a branded PDF (quote / invoice / proposal) from a CRM record using a
`DocumentTemplate`, OR — with `esign: true` — render and send it into the native
e-sign pipeline.

The template is resolved from the tenant's own templates plus the Ambivo
starters (`tenant_id` = `"-1"`), preferring the tenant's default for the
`(entity_type, doc_kind)`. Provide an explicit `template_id` to override.

- `output: "pdf"` (default) returns a presigned `pdf_url` (S3).
- `output: "html_preview"` returns rendered `preview_html`.
- `esign: true` (quote/proposal only — templates with `allow_esign`) renders the
  document and calls native e-sign `create_and_send_document`. Signers come from
  `signers`, or are auto-derived from the record's primary contact
  (`contact_id` → first email). Invoices/receipts are rejected with
  `ESIGN_NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_TEMPLATE`.
- `persist_draft: true` (quote/proposal only) renders the document and stages a
  **draft** native e-sign document **without sending it** (native e-sign
  `create_document`), returning `native_esign_document_id` and `status: "draft"`.
  This is the first leg of the generate → preview → send flow: stage here, then
  dispatch with `POST /user/document/send`. Signers are **optional** here — a draft
  may be staged signer-less and the signers attached at send time (`send` enforces
  that ≥1 signer exists before dispatch).

Error codes (via `CanonicalError`): `INVALID_ENTITY_TYPE`,
`DOCUMENT_TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND`, `DOCUMENT_TEMPLATE_ENTITY_MISMATCH`,
`DOCUMENT_RENDER_FAILED`, `ORDER_ID_NOT_FOUND`, `INVOICE_ID_NOT_FOUND`,
`ESIGN_NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_TEMPLATE`, `MISSING_SIGNERS`, `ESIGN_SEND_FAILED`,
`MISSING_ARGUMENT`, `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. With `esign` or `persist_draft`, also
`ESIGN_DISABLED` (e-sign is off for the tenant) and `ESIGN_REQUIRES_PRO` (tenant
is not on the Pro or Enterprise plan).

doc_kind.description: Used to pick the default template when `template_id` is omitted.

template_id.description: Explicit template; omit to use the tenant default for (entity_type, doc_kind).

esign.description: Render and send the quote/proposal into native e-sign. Send a JSON boolean. Any non-empty string, including `"false"`, counts as true.

persist_draft.description: Render and stage a draft e-sign document without sending (generate → preview → send). Returns native_esign_document_id and status: draft. Send a JSON boolean; any non-empty string counts as true.

signers.description: Required when `esign=true` (unless derivable from the record's contact); optional when `persist_draft=true` (attach at send time). Entries without `email` are dropped. If none remain, the record's primary contact becomes the signer.

custom_message.description: Optional cover message shown to signers.

signature_fields.description: Optional positioned fields; omitted = free-form signing.

workflow_action.description: Optional native e-sign action to run on completion.

stage_draft.summary: Stage a signer-less draft (generate → preview → send)

post.summary: Send an already-generated document for signature
post.description:
Dispatch a document into the native e-sign pipeline. This is the final leg of
the generate → preview → send flow and complements `POST /user/document/generate`
(which can render and, with `persist_draft: true`, stage a draft).

Two modes:

- **By reference (preferred).** Pass `native_esign_document_id` — the draft staged
  by `generate` with `persist_draft: true`. The draft must still be in `draft`
  status (sending a draft already sent returns `ESIGN_SEND_FAILED`). Optional
  last-minute overrides (`signers`, `custom_message`, `signature_fields`,
  `workflow_action`, `expires_days`) are applied to the draft before it goes out.
  If the draft was staged signer-less, `signers` must be supplied here, else
  `MISSING_SIGNERS` is returned.
- **One-shot fallback.** Omit `native_esign_document_id` and pass
  `entity_type`/`entity_id` (+ optional `template_id`/`doc_kind`/`signers`). The
  document is rendered fresh and created + sent in a single call (equivalent to
  `generate` with `esign: true`).

Signers come from `signers`, or — in one-shot mode — are auto-derived from the
record's primary contact. Tenant scoping is enforced on the referenced document;
a doc from another tenant returns `ESIGN_DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND`.

Error codes (via `CanonicalError`): `ESIGN_DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND`,
`ESIGN_SEND_FAILED`, `ESIGN_NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_TEMPLATE`, `MISSING_SIGNERS`,
`INVALID_ENTITY_TYPE`, `MISSING_ARGUMENT`, `DOCUMENT_TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND`,
`DOCUMENT_TEMPLATE_ENTITY_MISMATCH`, `DOCUMENT_RENDER_FAILED`,
`ORDER_ID_NOT_FOUND`, `INVOICE_ID_NOT_FOUND`, `ESIGN_DISABLED` (e-sign is off
for the tenant), `ESIGN_REQUIRES_PRO` (tenant is not on the Pro or Enterprise plan).

entity_type.description: Required for the one-shot path (no native_esign_document_id).

custom_message.description: Optional cover message shown to signers.

signature_fields.description: Optional positioned fields; omitted = free-form signing.

workflow_action.description: Optional native e-sign action to run on completion.

expires_days.description: By-reference override: days until the invitation expires.

post.description:
Perform create, read, update, and delete operations on products
by setting the `action` field in the request body.

**Supported actions:**
- `add` — Create a new product. Payload contains product fields. Duplicate
  product names in a tenant are rejected with `error_code =
  PRODUCT_NAME_ALREADY_EXISTS` (the specific reason is also echoed in
  `error.reason`). Optional `price_dict_list` inside `payload` creates
  price tiers in one round-trip (each entry is assigned a fresh UUID `id`
  server-side; client-supplied `id` values are ignored). `price_dict_list` may also go at the top level.
- `update` — Update one product. `product_id` goes at the top level. A `product_id` inside `payload` is dropped.
- `delete` — Delete a single product. Top-level `product_id` required
  (NOT inside `payload`). Tenant-admin only. Other callers get `deleted: false`.
  A product with any stock movement is never deleted: the answer is `result: 2`,
  `error_code: PRODUCT_HAS_STOCK_HISTORY`. Set `is_active: false` to retire it.
- `delete_many` — Bulk delete products. Top-level `ids_list` required
  (NOT inside `payload`). Response includes one boolean per id indicating
  whether that specific record was deleted. Tenant-admin only — non-admin
  callers get `deleted=false` for every id. Products with stock movements are kept;
  `data.not_deleted` maps each of their ids to `PRODUCT_HAS_STOCK_HISTORY`.
- `get` — One product with top-level `product_id`, or a page without it. Rows come back
  in `data.products`, a list, with `total_count`. Page with `last_id`.

ids_list.description: Top-level array of product ids for `delete_many`.

payload.description:
Action-specific payload:
- **add/update**: Product field values (see Product schema)
- **get/update/delete**: use TOP-LEVEL `product_id` (not inside payload)
- **delete_many**: use TOP-LEVEL `ids_list` (not inside payload)

post.description:
Move one or more opportunities to a new pipeline stage. This is the backend
for Kanban board drag-and-drop.

- Tenant admins can change any opportunity's stage.
- Non-admin users can only change their own opportunities.
- If stage is `closed_won` or `closed_lost`, a `close_date` should be provided
  unless one already exists on the opportunity.
- `closed_won` needs `product_id` or `property_id`. Without one, the call returns
  `result: 2` with `error_code` `OPPORTUNITY_STAGE_CHANGE_ERROR`.
- Ids that are not found or not yours are skipped. `response` lists what changed.

**Valid stages:** `draft`, `prospecting`, `discovery`, `developing`,
`negotiation_review`, `contract_pending`, `closed_won`, `closed_lost`,
plus the tenant's custom opportunity stages.

opportunity_ids_list.description: Array of opportunity IDs to update

get.summary: Read a saved list, or enumerate all lists for an entity type
get.description:
Two modes:

- **Enumerate** (`list_id` omitted or `-1`): returns all `user_entity_list`
  documents for the caller (`userid` match or `userid: ""`) filtered by
  `entity_type` (default `lead`). Membership IDs are not resolved into
  full records here.
- **Read members** (`list_id` set): returns the records belonging to the
  list. For static lists this is the stored `entity_ids_list`. For
  dynamic lists (`dynamic: true` on the doc) the stored `source_filter`
  is re-run via `GenUtilsService.get_access_q_dict` each call, so the
  response reflects the current state of the underlying collection.
  The optional `match_filter_dict` query-string parameter is applied as
  an additional overlay filter on top of the list's base membership.

`property` lists page with `page_num` and `page_size`. Other types page with `last_id`.
`data.total_count` is the number of records on this page.

parameters.name: list_id
parameters.description:
`_id` of a `user_entity_list` document. Omit or pass `-1` to list
all of the caller's lists for the given `entity_type`.

parameters.name: last_id
parameters.description: ObjectId cursor (sort is `_id` desc).

parameters.name: match_filter_dict
parameters.description:
JSON dict (passed as a string in the query) applied as an extra
filter on top of the list's membership. Same shape as other CRM
list endpoints.

data.description:
Records when `list_id` is set. Shape varies by entity
type — `lead_contacts`, `contacts`, `accounts`,
`opportunities`, `properties`, plus `total_count` and
`last_id`.

entity_list.description: Catalog of lists when `list_id` is omitted/-1.

post.summary: Create or copy a saved entity list
post.description:
Create a list of records for any supported `entity_type`. Every POST
inserts a new list. Names need not be unique, so re-posting a name
makes a second list. To change a list, use PUT.

**Copy mode.** Send `copy_from_list_id`, with optional `name` and
`description`, to copy a seeded list or one of your own. The copy keeps
the entity type, the dynamic flag and the filter or members. With no
`name`, the copy is named "<source name> (copy)". Copy errors:
`COPY_FROM_LIST_ID_REQUIRED`, `INVALID_LIST_ID`, `LIST_NOT_FOUND`,
`LIST_CANNOT_BE_COPIED`, `LIST_DUPLICATE_FAILED`.

**Three input modes** — exactly one must be supplied:

1. **Static / explicit IDs** — pass `entity_ids_list` directly.
2. **Static snapshot from a query** — pass `match_filter_dict`. The
   server resolves it now (using the same access-controlled query
   pipeline as other list endpoints) and stores the resulting `_id`s as
   a frozen snapshot. The original filter is also stored in
   `source_filter` for audit. Capped at **10,000** matches.
3. **Dynamic / smart list** — pass `match_filter_dict` along with
   `dynamic: true`. The server stores `source_filter` and a
   **placeholder empty** `entity_ids_list`; membership is recomputed
   every time the list is read.

Snapshot creation respects tenant scope, module access, and ownership
access-dict controls — same as a regular `/user/lead` (or sibling) list
request.

copy_from_list_id.description: The list to copy. See copy mode above.

match_filter_dict.description:
Mongo-style filter applied to the entity collection.
Resolved server-side. Mutually exclusive with
`entity_ids_list`.

dynamic.description:
When `true`, store the filter as a smart list and recompute
membership at read time. Requires `match_filter_dict`.

snapshot_from_filter.summary: Static snapshot built from a filter

dynamic_smart_list.summary: Dynamic / smart list — recomputes at read time

dynamic.description: Echoed back when a filter was supplied.

resolved_count.description:
Number of `_id`s materialized at POST time. Always `0`
for dynamic lists (membership is computed at read time).

error_code.description:
Set on validation failures. Possible values:
`INVALID_PAYLOAD` (request body was not a JSON object),
`NAME_REQUIRED` (`name` missing or blank after trim),
`UNSUPPORTED_ENTITY_TYPE` (entity_type not in
`lead | contact | account | opportunity | property`),
`PROVIDE_IDS_OR_FILTER` (neither `entity_ids_list` nor
`match_filter_dict` was supplied),
`PROVIDE_IDS_OR_FILTER_NOT_BOTH` (both supplied),
`DYNAMIC_REQUIRES_FILTER` (`dynamic: true` without
`match_filter_dict`),
`ENTITY_LIST_FILTER_OVER_LIMIT` (snapshot filter
resolved more than 10,000 records — narrow the filter),
`ENTITY_LIST_FILTER_NO_MATCH` (snapshot filter matched
zero records),
`ENTITY_LIST_FILTER_RESOLVE_FAILED` (unexpected backend
error while resolving the filter — see server logs).

put.summary: Update a saved entity list (rename, change description, mutate IDs)
put.description:
Mutate an existing list. The body is `{entity_list_id, payload}`.
Supported payload keys:

- `name` / `description` — rename / re-describe.
- `entity_ids_list` — replace membership wholesale (subject to
  ObjectId validation; invalid IDs are silently dropped). Pass `[]` to
  empty the list.
- `add_entity_ids` (list) — `$push` IDs onto membership.
- `remove_entity_ids` (list) — `$pull` IDs from membership.
- `match_filter_dict` — a new filter replaces `source_filter`. On a static list
  it is also resolved to ids now. A filter equal to the stored one changes nothing.
  An empty filter never clears one.

`dynamic` is never changed. To convert between static and dynamic, POST a new list.
On a dynamic list, member changes are refused. Seeded lists cannot be changed.

The reply has `result` and `updated` (1 when the list changed, 0 when it did not).
On a refusal, `result` is 2 and `error_code` is one of `INVALID_PAYLOAD`,
`INVALID_LIST_ID`, `LIST_NOT_FOUND`, `SEEDED_LIST_READ_ONLY`, `INVALID_FILTER`,
`INVALID_ENTITY_IDS`, `DYNAMIC_LIST_MEMBERS_READ_ONLY`, `PROVIDE_IDS_OR_FILTER_NOT_BOTH`,
`ENTITY_LIST_FILTER_NO_MATCH`, `ENTITY_LIST_FILTER_RESOLVE_FAILED` or `LIST_UPDATE_FAILED`.

delete.description:
Delete by id. Accepts either `entity_list_ids` (preferred) or
`list_ids`. Lists owned by a different user (or seeded as system
lists) are silently skipped.

post.summary: Set or update payment access code
post.description:
Set or update the user's payment access code (numeric PIN).
The code must be 4-6 digits. It is bcrypt-hashed (salt rounds: 10) and stored
on the User document. Setting a new code resets the failed-attempt counter and
clears any active lockout.

Used by Ambivo Books to gate sensitive financial operations such as Wise vendor payments.

access_code.description: 4-6 digit numeric PIN. Send it as a JSON string; a number fails with an AttributeError message.

get.description:
Returns whether the authenticated user has a payment access code set
and whether the account is currently locked out due to failed attempts.

is_locked.description: Whether the account is currently locked (too many failed attempts)

locked_until.description: Unix epoch timestamp when the lockout expires. Null if not locked.

post.description:
Verify the user's payment access code. On success, resets the failed-attempt
counter and returns a UUID verification token. The caller (Ambivo Books) stores
this token in Redis with a 5-minute TTL and requires it as a single-use gate
before processing a payment.

**Lockout rules:**
- 5 failed attempts → 15-minute lockout
- Successful verification resets the attempt counter to 0
- During lockout, all verification attempts are rejected immediately with
  `ACCESS_CODE_LOCKED. Try again in N seconds.`

verification_token.description:
Single-use token for the downstream payment endpoint.
Only returned on successful verification (result=1).

value.msg: ACCESS_CODE_LOCKED. Too many failed attempts. Try again in 15 minutes.

delete.summary: Reset a user's access code (superadmin only)
delete.description:
Clears the target user's access code hash, attempt counter, lockout timestamp,
and set-at timestamp. The user will need to set a new access code before their
next payment.

**Authorization:** Requires the caller to be a superadmin or pseudo-superadmin.
Tenant admins get `ADMIN_REQUIRED`. The target user must belong to the
caller's tenant.

parameters.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the user whose access code should be reset

post.description:
Allows an authenticated user to verify their current password. Returns `true`
or `false` indicating whether the supplied password matches the stored hash.

**Use cases:**
- Re-authentication before sensitive operations (password change, account deletion)
- Identity confirmation in security-critical workflows

**Rate limiting:**
- Maximum **5 requests per hour** per user (Redis-based)
- Returns `429 Too Many Requests` when exceeded

**Security:**
- Requires a valid session token (cookie-based authentication)
- Password is checked via bcrypt hash comparison

password.description: The user's current password to verify

401.description: Not authenticated — invalid or expired session token

429.description: Rate limit exceeded (5 requests per hour)

error.message: Too many password verification attempts. Please try again later.

post.description:
Creates a new user account. If the email domain matches an existing tenant,
the user joins that tenant (subject to `allow_user_self_registration` and domain
restrictions). If the domain is new and non-public, a new tenant is auto-created.

After registration, a 4-digit email confirmation code is sent.
The response includes a JWT token with `email_confirmation_needed=true`.

**Existing email:** if the email already has an account and `password` is sent,
the call signs that user in. The reply is a login response with
`pwd_was_generated: false` and no `email_confirmation_needed`. Without a
password, an existing email is refused.

The tenant comes from the email domain. A `tenant_id` in the body is ignored.

**Rate limiting:** 5 requests per IP per 60s, 5 per email per 300s.

**Anti-spam:** Gibberish name detection, OS/UA mismatch checks, spam IP blocking.

Authenticates a user with email and password. The response shape depends on
whether the user has MFA enrolled and how many factors are active:

1. **No MFA enrolled** — returns `result: 1` plus `token` and `user`.
2. **Single active factor** (SMS or email) — the server issues a challenge
   in-band and returns `is_mfa_response: true` with `provider_challenge_id`,
   a masked `challenge_destination`, and (for email) `expires_at`. The client
   collects the OTP and POSTs to `/user/mfa/verify`.
3. **Multiple active factors** — the server returns
   `requires_factor_selection: true` with a short-lived `pre_mfa_token` and a
   `factor_list`. The client picks a factor and POSTs to `/user/mfa/initiate`
   to actually issue the challenge for the chosen channel.
4. **MFA required, none enrolled**: when tenant policy requires MFA and the user
   has no active factor, the server returns `requires_mfa_enrollment: true` with an
   `enrollment_token`. The client enrolls a first factor at `/user/mfa/enroll_gate`.

Shapes 3 and 4 have no `result` key. Check `is_mfa_response` first.

Send the credentials as a JSON body. Query-string arguments get HTTP 400
`INVALID_REQUEST_FORMAT`. A missing `email` or `password` gets HTTP 400
`MISSING_EMAIL` or `MISSING_PASSWORD`.

Email factors that are still in `pending_verify` state are **excluded** from
the login gate so a half-enrolled user is not locked out. No session JWT is
created until the OTP is verified.

If the user's email is unconfirmed, automatically re-sends the confirmation
email and returns an error.

**Rate limiting:** 10 per IP per 60s, 5 per email per 120s.
**Account lockout:** 5 failed attempts → 24h block per IP/user combo.

See also: [`docs/email_mfa.md`](https://github.com/ambivo-corp/ambivo_api/blob/main/docs/email_mfa.md)
and [`docs/workos_mfa_sms.md`](https://github.com/ambivo-corp/ambivo_api/blob/main/docs/workos_mfa_sms.md).

post.description:
Validates the 4-digit confirmation code sent to the user's email during registration.
On success, the user is automatically logged in (`pre_authorized=true`) and a JWT token is returned.

Also marks the tenant as verified if this is the first user to confirm in that tenant.

Send the fields form-encoded or in the query string. A JSON body is not read.

Returns a Google OAuth consent URL. The frontend navigates the browser to this URL.
After the user consents, Google redirects to ambivo_api's callback, which processes the
OAuth tokens, creates/finds the user, generates a JWT, and issues a 302 redirect to
`post_navigation/<jwt_token>?final_navigation=<url>`.

**For Microsoft:** Use `/user/register/Microsoft` with the same request format.

### Integration Playbook

1. **Backend** calls this endpoint with `post_navigation` and `final_navigation`
2. **Frontend** navigates to the returned `url` (full page navigation)
3. User consents on Google
4. Google redirects to ambivo_api callback
5. ambivo_api 302-redirects to `{post_navigation}{jwt_token}?final_navigation={url}`
6. Your SPA catches the redirect, extracts the JWT from the URL path
7. Your backend calls `POST /user/get_from_token` to validate the JWT
8. On success, store the session and redirect to the dashboard

### Critical: `post_navigation` Must End With Trailing Slash

ambivo_api appends the JWT directly to `post_navigation`. Without a trailing slash:
- Wrong: `https://app.com/token-logineyJhbGci...` (no separator)
- Correct: `https://app.com/token-login/eyJhbGci...` (with `/`)

**Domain restriction:** `post_navigation` must be on the deployment's redirect
allow-list. That is `*.ambivo.com` plus the partner's own brand domains on a
white-label deployment.

`app_context` and `device_id` are not read by this endpoint.

**No authentication required.**

Same as `/user/register/Google` but for Microsoft accounts.

post.summary: Resolve a JWT token into a full login session
post.description:
Converts a valid JWT token into a full login response (user details, session token, tenant info).
Used by frontends after OAuth redirects, email confirmation, and mobile OAuth flows.

Also supports **temporary exchange tokens**. The server issues one in place of a session
JWT longer than 900 characters, for OAuth and SAML redirect URLs. Format:
`tx1_<24 hex>_<64 hex>`. It is valid for 60 seconds and works once.

**No authentication required** — this endpoint IS the authentication step.

### Content-Type

Accepts both `application/json` and `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.
A missing `token` returns HTTP 400 with `error_code: MISSING_TOKEN`.

### OAuth Integration

This is Step 7 in the OAuth playbook (see `/user/register/Google`).
After the OAuth redirect lands on your `/token-login/<jwt>` page, call this
endpoint to validate the JWT and get the full user session.

post.summary: Send or verify a sign-in code (OTP login)
post.description:
Two-phase passwordless login (contract v2). Use `action: "send_verification_code"` to send
a code, then `action: "verify_code"` to verify it and receive a JWT login session.
A missing `action` means `send_verification_code`.

### Channel

`channel` picks where the code goes: `sms` or `email`. Without `channel`, the code goes
by email when `email` is present, and by SMS otherwise. An explicit `channel` is final:
`channel: "email"` with only a phone number is refused.

- **`sms`**: `phone_number` finds the account and receives the text. A number without
  a leading `+` is read as a US number.
- **`email`**: `email` finds the account and receives the code.

The send reply carries `channel`, `destination_masked` and `challenge_id`. Send the
`challenge_id` back with the code. The challenge then names the account, and any
`email`, `phone_number` or `tenant_id` in the verify body is ignored.

### Multi-Tenant Users

If multiple users share the same email or phone across tenants (e.g. member in one,
guest in another), the response returns `result: 3` with a `tenant_list`. The client
must re-send with a `tenant_id` to disambiguate. The code is NOT sent until a single
user is resolved.

### Device trust

A successful verify returns `device_trust`, an opaque token valid for 30 days. Send it
back as `device_trust` on later sends and verifies from the same device.

### Token Lifetime

OTP login tokens are valid for **6 months** (ambivo_api sets `is_mobile=True` for OTP
logins, which triggers the long-lived token path). This is longer than email/password
login tokens, which follow the tenant's `session_duration` setting.

**Rate limiting:** 10 requests per 90 seconds per IP. Sends are also limited per
phone or email and per account (`OTP_RATE_LIMITED`).

**Codes:** 6 digits. SMS codes expire after **10 minutes**, email codes after
**5 minutes**. Each challenge allows 5 attempts.

### Errors

Failures return `result: 2` with an `error_code` and an English `message`. Codes:
`PHONE_INVALID`, `PHONE_NOT_FOUND`, `PHONE_COUNTRY_NOT_SUPPORTED`, `EMAIL_NOT_FOUND`,
`PHONE_ON_MANY_ACCOUNTS`, `EMAIL_ON_MANY_ACCOUNTS`, `OTP_RATE_LIMITED`,
`ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE`, `OTP_SEND_FAILED`, `TENANT_NOT_FOUND`, `OTP_NO_OPEN_CHALLENGE`,
`OTP_CODE_EXPIRED`, `OTP_TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS`, `OTP_CODE_INCORRECT`, `OTP_VERIFY_FAILED`,
`OTP_PASSWORD_REQUIRED` (the account needs a password and a second factor) and
`EMAIL_MFA_REQUIRES_CONFIRMED_EMAIL`.

Public endpoint to check if an email address is registered and retrieve the user's
associated tenants. Used by the frontend before login to determine if tenant

The user lookup runs only when `return_associated_phone` is `true`. A check by `phone`
returns only whether a user has that phone, with an empty `alt_tenant_list`.

post.summary: Verify or resend an MFA challenge code
post.description:
Verifies the OTP issued during MFA-protected login. The handler routes
internally by `MFAChallenge.type`, so the same request shape works for
SMS (WorkOS-backed) and email (locally generated) challenges.

**Ownership enforcement.** The body's `userid` must match the recorded
owner of the challenge. Mismatches return a uniform `INVALID_MFA_CODE`
response with no info-leak about whether the challenge id existed.

**Attempt cap.** Each challenge has a per-row counter (default 5). Wrong
codes increment the counter atomically; once exhausted the row transitions
to `status: "locked"` and subsequent attempts return `MFA_CHALLENGE_EXHAUSTED`.

**Resend.** Send `action: "resend"` to re-issue the challenge without
verifying. Resend uses a 30-second cooldown keyed on the original challenge's
`created_date` to defeat mail-bombing; if invoked too soon the response
carries `retry_after_seconds`.

**Rate limiting:** 5 per IP per 60s, 5 per email per 300s.

resend.summary: Resend the OTP via the same channel

200.description:
On success returns the standard login envelope (`LoginResponse`) with
`result: 1`, `token`, and `user`. On a wrong / expired / exhausted
attempt returns `MfaVerifyFailureResponse`. On a successful resend
returns the standard `MfaChallengeEnvelope` shape.

exhausted.summary: Per-challenge attempt cap hit; row is now locked

post.summary: Trigger a chosen MFA factor (multi-factor login)
post.description:
Multi-factor dispatcher. Called by clients after `/user/login` returns
`requires_factor_selection: true`. Decodes the `pre_mfa_token`, looks up
the user, validates that the requested `factor_id` is in the token's
`factor_ids` allowlist (the curated menu offered by `/user/login`), then
issues a challenge on the chosen channel.

**Single-use tokens.** The `pre_mfa_token` carries a `jti` claim that is
stamped onto the issued challenge under a partial unique index
(`raw_data_pre_mfa_jti_unique`). Concurrent calls with the same token —
even racing each other — produce at most one challenge. Subsequent
presentations return `PRE_MFA_TOKEN_ALREADY_USED`.

**Channel-specific guards.** For email factors the handler additionally
verifies that the factor's `status == "active"` and that the user's
primary email is confirmed.

**Rate limiting:** 5 per IP per 60s, 5 per email per 120s.

post.summary: Enroll an MFA factor, or activate an emailed enrollment code
post.description:
Triple-duty endpoint multiplexed on `mfa_type`:

- **`sms`**: registers a phone number with WorkOS and texts an activation code.
  The factor stays `pending_verify` until `mfa_type: "sms_verify"` succeeds. The reply
  carries `factor_id`, `provider_challenge_id` and `requires_verification: true`.
  A second request within the cooldown returns `MFA_RESEND_TOO_SOON`.
- **`sms_verify`**: submits the SMS activation code with `provider_challenge_id`.
  On success the SMS factor becomes active and replaces any earlier SMS factor.
- **`email`** — generates a 6-digit OTP, emails it to the user's primary
  (confirmed) address, and stores a `pending_verify` factor. The factor is
  **not** counted as active for login until the code is verified via
  `mfa_type: "email_verify"`. Re-calling with `mfa_type: "email"` rotates
  the factor (old factor + any open challenges are dropped).
- **`email_verify`** — submits the activation code; on success the factor
  flips to `status: "active"`. The response may include a `warning` hint
  if the underlying factor was rotated between issue and activation.

Email enrollment is rejected with `EMAIL_MFA_REQUIRES_CONFIRMED_EMAIL` if
the user's primary email is not confirmed.

**Password check:** send the account `password` in the body when the account already
has an active factor and `mfa_type` is `sms` or `email`. Also send it for `sms_verify`
or `email_verify` when the new factor replaces a live one. Without it the reply is
`result: 2` with `PASSWORD_REQUIRED`. A wrong password returns `PASSWORD_INCORRECT`
with `attempts_remaining`. Too many wrong passwords return `ACCOUNT_LOCKED`.
Accounts with no password the user could know are not asked.

delete.summary: Unenroll one or all MFA factors for the authenticated user
delete.description:
Removes the caller's own MFA factor(s). For SMS this also deletes the WorkOS
factor; for email it invalidates any open challenges so a stale OTP cannot
be redeemed after deletion.

- `mfa_type: "sms"` — remove SMS factor only.
- `mfa_type: "email"` — remove email factor only.
- `mfa_type: "all"` — remove both, in a single call.

`mfa_type` is required. Any other value returns `{result: 1, message: "NO-ACTION"}`
and removes nothing.

**Password check:** send the account `password` in the body on every call. Without it
the reply is `result: 2` with `PASSWORD_REQUIRED`. A wrong password returns
`PASSWORD_INCORRECT`. Accounts with no password the user could know are not asked.

Tenant-admin-only endpoint to reset MFA for a user in the admin's tenant
who has lost access (e.g. lost their phone). The default behavior resets
**both** SMS and email factors **and** purges any open `mfa_challenge`
rows for that user — so a stale code in transit cannot be redeemed after
the reset.

Optionally pass `mfa_type` to target only one factor type.

The target user does not need to be authenticated — the operation is
gated by the caller's tenant-admin role and a check that the target user
belongs to the same tenant.

**Password check:** send the admin's own `password` in the body. Without it the reply
is `result: 2` with `PASSWORD_REQUIRED`.

A caller who is not a tenant admin gets HTTP 200 with `result: 2`. A target user in
another tenant gets HTTP 200 with `result: 2` and `USER_NOT_FOUND_IN_TENANT`.

post.description:
Sends a notification across multiple channels in a single call.
Designed for external systems and automation workflows that authenticate
with a user Bearer token.

**Channels (all configurable):**
- **In-app** — always created (MongoDB `user_static_notifications` collection)
- **WebSocket** — real-time delivery (default: on)
- **Push** — Firebase Cloud Messaging to registered devices (default: on)
- **Email** — opt-in, requires `channels.email` config with recipients
- **SMS** — opt-in, requires `channels.sms` config with phone numbers

**Scheduling:**
When `initial_delay > 60` seconds, the notification is queued as a
`TenantScheduledTask` for deferred execution. The response returns
immediately with `status: "queued"` and a `tenant_scheduled_task_id`.

**Error isolation:**
Email and SMS failures are non-fatal — the response still returns
`result: 1` with the failed channel reported in `channels`.
Only in-app notification failure causes `result: 2`.

**Non-blocking:**
Email and SMS are dispatched via the event queue (fire-and-forget).
The HTTP response returns immediately after the in-app insert and
push notification complete.

`message_queued` means the message was handed to the queue. The queue can still
drop it, for example when the tenant fails the payment check or `src` equals
`dst`. The response does not report that.

the `from` and `to` numbers and do not need delivery tracking or conversation threading.

**Text limit:** Truncated to 1000 characters.

post.summary: Validate a phone number (international, with optional live Telnyx lookup)
post.description:
Combines two layers in one response:

1. **libphonenumber (offline)** — parses the input, computes E.164 / national
   format, region/country, and best-effort number type
   (mobile / fixed-line / VOIP / toll-free / unknown). No network call.
   Works for any country supported by Google's libphonenumber dataset.
2. **Telnyx number_lookup (live, paid)** — optional second leg that returns
   the current carrier, caller name (CNAM, US-only), and portability data.
   Skipped automatically when libphonenumber says the input isn't even a
   "possible" number, so garbage input doesn't trigger a paid call.

### Input shapes

- **E.164** (`+14155551234`, `+442079460958`) — preferred. No `country_iso` needed.
- **National format with country hint** — e.g. `phone_number=650-631-1281` plus
  `country_iso=US`. The endpoint canonicalizes this to E.164 in the response.
- **Bare digits without `+` and no `country_iso`** — returns
  `result=2, reason=PARSE_FAILED` because libphonenumber cannot infer a region.

### When to use

- Pre-flight check before saving a phone on a lead/contact/account.
- Mass cleanup / dedup of imported phone columns: pass `live=false` to validate
  format-and-region in bulk for free, then re-run with `live=true` only on
  numbers that already passed the offline check.
- Determining the country of an unknown inbound number (e.g. for routing).

### Cost

The live Telnyx leg is billed per call (~USD 0.005 at time of writing). For
bulk validation, set `live=false` first; only the offline parse is free.

Auth: requires a valid bearer token. There is no per-tenant entitlement —
any authenticated user can call this endpoint.

Note: this endpoint accepts both POST (JSON body) and GET (query params) for
client convenience. POST is preferred for programmatic use.

uk_e164_offline.summary: UK number, offline only (no Telnyx lookup)

200.description: Validation result. `result=1` on success (offline parse OK), `result=2` on parse failure.

get.description:
Same as `POST /phone/validate` but accepts query parameters. Provided for
convenience (e.g. `curl` smoke tests, browser address-bar checks). For
programmatic callers prefer the POST form.

Encode the leading `+` of an E.164 number as `%2B`. A raw `+` arrives as a
space and every E.164 lookup fails with `PARSE_FAILED`. The POST form has
no such issue.

parameters.description:
Phone number in E.164 format (preferred) or national format if `country_iso` is also provided.
Send the leading `+` as `%2B`, e.g. `phone_number=%2B14155551234`.
A raw `+` in the query string is read as a space, and the parse fails with `PARSE_FAILED`.

parameters.name: country_iso
parameters.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 country hint, used when `phone_number` is in national (no `+`) format.

parameters.name: live
parameters.description: When `true` (default), also run a live Telnyx number_lookup. Set `false` to skip the paid call and return offline-only results. Only the value `false` skips the lookup; `0` or `no` still runs it.

post.summary: Send SMS from user's softphone number
post.description:
Sends an SMS from the authenticated user's assigned SIP phone number.
Creates or updates a client conversation room for bidirectional SMS messaging.

**Prerequisites:**
- Tenant must have `telco_enabled = true`
- User must have `softphone_enabled = true`
- User must have a SIP phone number assigned (`sip_creds_dict.sip_phone`)

**Conversation threading:**
The endpoint creates a client room for the SMS conversation. If the recipient
phone number is unknown, the system looks up caller ID information via Telnyx
and creates a guest user. Subsequent SMS messages to/from the same number
appear in the same room.

**Rate limit:** 2 requests per 90 seconds per user.

**Errors:** These return HTTP 500 with `result: 2` and an `error_code`:
`TENANT_NOT_TELCO_ENABLED`, `USER_SOFTPHONE_NOT_ENABLED`, `USER_SIPPHONE_NOT_FOUND`,
`MISSING_DST_OR_TEXT` and `DESTINATION_NUMBER_INVALID_<number>`.

**Result 2 with no reason:** The response is `{result: 2}` with null ids when
`dst` is the tenant's dialer phone or on the tenant ignore list. The same happens
when the number's nuisance score is 5 or more, or `text` is empty.

**Recipient in another tenant:** When `dst` belongs to a user in another tenant,
nothing is sent. The response is `result: 1` with `room_id: null`.

**When to use:** CRM softphone UI — agent sends SMS to a contact/lead from
within the Ambivo phone interface. Supports attachments (MMS).

`dialer_phone`.

**Message length:** Capped at 304 characters (gross length including carrier overhead).

**When to use:** System-level or administrative SMS delivery — e.g., automated
reminders, system alerts, or support messages sent by platform operators.

get.summary: Get entity status/stage values (seeded + tenant custom)
get.description:
Returns the effective list of status/stage values for a given entity type,
or for all entity types at once when `entity_type` is omitted.

For `opportunity / order / invoice / lead / contact / account / task` the
response merges seeded values with the tenant's **active custom** values
defined in `entity_custom_stages` (manage via `POST /tenant/entity-custom-stages`).
Seeded values keep all built-in business logic; custom values are "open" and
trigger no automation unless a workflow targets them.

**Overrides**: a row in `entity_custom_stages` whose `key` matches a
seeded value acts as an OVERRIDE -- the merged entry keeps
`is_seeded: true` (built-in logic preserved) but `is_overridden: true`
and the override's label/color/position win. An
`entity_custom_stage_id` is attached so clients can PATCH/DELETE the
override directly. Soft-deleting an override row reverts the seeded
entry to its built-in label/color/position. Pure-custom entries
(key not in the seeded list) carry `is_seeded: false` and their own
`entity_custom_stage_id`.

For `bill / payment` the response returns seeded values only (custom
values not yet supported for these entity types).

Pass `include_custom=false` to get the seeded-only list (useful for
validators that need the pristine enum).

Response includes both `stages` (canonical, recommended for new
clients) and `values_meta` (alias kept for backward compatibility --
same list object). Each entry carries `key / label / color / is_seeded
/ is_overridden / is_active / position / entity_custom_stage_id?`
so UI consumers can render colored chips, ordered kanban columns, and
badged System / Override / Custom rows. The flat `values` array is
retained for legacy callers that only need the string list.

Sorting: `position` ascending, with seeded entries before custom entries
when positions collide. Seeded positions come from `SEEDED_STAGE_POSITION_HINTS`
(logical lifecycle order, not enum declaration order). Override
entries use the override's position when set; the kanban therefore
re-sorts to honor tenant customization.

**Dual authentication**: accepts either a Bearer JWT token or the
`X-AMBIVO-INTERNAL-SECRET` header for service-to-service calls. Tenant
custom-stage merging only fires for JWT-authenticated requests (the
tenant context comes from the JWT).

parameters.name: entity_type
parameters.description:
Entity type to retrieve values for. If omitted, returns values for all
supported entity types in a single response.

parameters.name: include_custom
parameters.description:
When `false`, returns seeded values only (no `entity_custom_stages` merge).
Useful for validators or migration tooling that needs the pristine enum.

values.description: Flat list of stage/status keys (seeded ∪ tenant active customs), position-sorted.

stages.description:
Canonical richer per-entry list for UI consumers. Same ordering
as `values`. New clients should consume this field; `values_meta`
is an alias of the same list kept for backward compatibility.

values_meta.description:
Alias of `stages` (same list object) kept for backward
compatibility. New clients should prefer `stages`.

field_name.description: The actual document field this stage/status maps to (e.g. `lead_status` for leads).

stages.description: Canonical merged stage list. New clients should prefer this over `values_meta`.

values_meta.description: Alias of `stages` (same list object) kept for backward compatibility.

400.description:
Invalid `entity_type`. Canonical error shape with
`error_code: UNSUPPORTED_ENTITY_TYPE` and a `supported_entity_types`
array listing valid values.

401.description: Authentication failed — no valid JWT or internal secret

get.summary: Get entity status/stage counts (seeded + tenant custom)
get.description:
Returns the number of records in each status/stage bucket, aligned to
the merged list returned by `/entity/status-values?entity_type=...`.
Zero-count seeded values AND zero-count active custom stages are always
emitted so dashboards have a stable column set (the legacy per-entity
endpoint `/user/metric/lead/count/status` only emitted zeros for seeded
leads and didn't cover other entity types at all).

### Why this exists
Until this endpoint, getting "count per status" required:
- calling `/user/metric/lead/count/status` for leads only (seeded
  statuses only — custom buckets were missing zero-count entries), and
- constructing custom Mongo aggregations for everything else.

`/entity/status-counts` unifies this across all 9 entity types supported
by the Status API (`lead, contact, account, opportunity, order,
invoice, task, bill, payment`) and includes tenant custom stages.

### Orphaned values
Records can legally hold a custom-status `key` whose definition has
since been soft-deleted (the row stays for historical fidelity). Those
bucket values surface with `is_orphaned: true, is_active: false,
is_seeded: false, position: 999` so admin UIs can prompt either
re-creating the custom stage or migrating the records.

### Access control
By default, counts respect the same per-user access filter as
`/entity/data?entity_type=...` (subordinate + role-hierarchy + shared
access). Pass `tenant_scope=true` to count across the whole tenant
(tenant admins only; auto-enabled for entities without a `userid`
field).

parameters.name: entity_type
parameters.description:
Entity type to count buckets for. Omit to return counts for every
supported type in a single response.

parameters.name: include_custom
parameters.description:
When `false`, seeded-only buckets are emitted (no `entity_custom_stages`
merge). Records holding custom keys still surface under `is_orphaned`.

parameters.name: tenant_scope
parameters.description:
`true` to count across the whole tenant (tenant admins only).
Auto-enabled when the entity has no `userid` field. Non-admins
requesting `tenant_scope=true` fall back to access-filtered counts.
Ignored for `lead` and `contact`, which always count what the caller's grid shows.

parameters.name: match_filter_dict
parameters.description:
Optional URL-encoded Mongo-style filter applied before grouping
(e.g. `{"$and":[{"timestamp":{"$gt":1700000000}}]}`). Parsed via
`ast.literal_eval` — must be a dict literal.

400.description:
Bad input. Canonical error shape with one of:
  - `UNSUPPORTED_ENTITY_TYPE`
  - `INVALID_MATCH_FILTER_DICT` — match_filter_dict not parseable as a dict

500.description:
The counts could not be computed. Canonical error shape with
`error_code: STATUS_COUNTS_FAILED`.

post.description:
Single action-based endpoint for adding, updating, soft-deleting, and
listing tenant-defined custom values for `opportunity / order / invoice
/ lead / contact / account / task / installed_base / purchase_order`. Values are stored in
`entity_custom_stages` striped by `(tenant_id, entity_type, key)`.

**Augment + override contract** — tenants can both ADD new custom
values AND OVERRIDE seeded ones (rename, recolor, reorder). Override
rows preserve the seeded slot's built-in business logic (e.g.
`closed_won` still creates an order; `closed_lost` still cleans up
the contact) -- only label/color/position change. Pure-custom values
do NOT inherit business logic; they're "open" and require a workflow
in `ai_workflow_system` to fire any action.

**Authz**: any authenticated user can `get`; `add / update / delete`
require tenant-admin permission.

### Actions
- **add** — creates a new row in `entity_custom_stages`. If `key` is
  omitted, the server slugifies `label` (ASCII-only, lowercase, max
  64 chars).

  - If the resulting `key` is NOT in the seeded list, this creates a
    pure CUSTOM stage. Default `position` is 200 (after all seeded
    slots) so customs sort to the end unless the admin sets one.
  - If the resulting `key` IS in the seeded list, this creates an
    OVERRIDE row. The merged `/entity/status-values` response will
    keep `is_seeded: true` but flip `is_overridden: true` and apply
    the row's label/color/position. Default `position` for overrides
    is the seeded position (not 200) so a simple rename does not
    reflow the kanban.

  **Reactivation on duplicate key**: if the same `(entity_type, key)`
  already exists for the tenant but is soft-deleted (`is_active=false`),
  the row is reactivated in place with the new `label / color /
  position` instead of returning `CUSTOM_STAGE_ALREADY_EXISTS`. The
  original `entity_custom_stage_id` is preserved so historical records
  (leads/opps/etc. holding that key) keep their semantic link. The
  response carries `reactivated: true` to disambiguate from a fresh
  insert.
- **update** — partial update. `entity_type` and `key` are immutable;
  attempts to change them are silently ignored. `label / color /
  position / is_active` can be changed. Applies equally to pure-custom
  and override rows.
- **delete** — soft delete (sets `is_active=false`). For a pure-custom
  row this hides the column from new pickers + kanban. For an OVERRIDE
  row this restores the seeded entry to its built-in label/color/
  position (the seeded slot itself never goes away). Historical
  records keep the stored value either way. Reactivate via `update`
  with `is_active=true`, or by re-issuing the same `add` payload --
  the add path detects the soft-deleted row and flips it back on.
- **get** — lists this tenant's custom and override rows for the given
  entity_type (sorted by position then label then key), or for ALL
  entity types when `entity_type` is omitted.

### Seed key handling
Adding a row with `key` matching a seeded value is ALLOWED and creates
an override (see the `add` action above). Prior versions of this
endpoint rejected this case with `KEY_COLLIDES_WITH_SEEDED`; that
error code is no longer issued.

### Race protection
A unique index on `(tenant_id, entity_type, key)` is created on first
request. Concurrent `add` requests for the same key — one succeeds, the
other returns `CUSTOM_STAGE_ALREADY_EXISTS` (409). If the racing row is
soft-deleted, the loser reactivates it instead of failing.

### Error response shape
All non-2xx responses follow the canonical error shape:
`{ "result": 2, "error_code": "<UPPERCASE_CODE>",
   "error": { "message": "<human readable>" }, "status_code": <int>,
   "request_path": "<path>" }`
plus any optional context fields (e.g. `key`, `entity_type`,
`entity_custom_stage_id`, `max_length`).

entity_type.description: Required for add. Not read for update/delete. Optional for get (omit to list across all entity types).

payload.description: Required for add; optional for update (partial). Ignored for delete/get.

key.description:
Optional on `add` — server slugifies `label` if omitted.
A `key` you send is slugified the same way and cut to 64 characters.
A seeded key creates an override row.

color.description: Hex color string for kanban chip + admin badge. Optional.

position.description:
Sort key (position-ascending) for kanban columns and pickers.
Default 200 (after all seeded slots). Use a number BETWEEN
seeded position hints to interleave — e.g. position=25
on opportunity sits between discovery(20) and developing(30).

is_active.description:
Soft-delete flag. Inactive values disappear from pickers and
kanban but historical records keep the value. Reactivate via
`update` with `is_active=true`.

listLeadCustoms.summary: List a tenant's custom lead statuses

updatePosition.summary: Update only the position of a custom stage

reactivated.description:
Present and `true` when `add` flipped a previously
soft-deleted row (`is_active=false`) back to `is_active=true`
instead of inserting a new row. The original
`entity_custom_stage_id` is preserved.

400.description:
Bad input. Canonical error shape with one of these `error_code` values:
  - `UNSUPPORTED_ACTION` — `action` not in {add,update,delete,get}
  - `UNSUPPORTED_ENTITY_TYPE` — entity_type not supported (response
    includes `supported_entity_types` array)
  - `MISSING_ENTITY_TYPE` — required on add
  - `MISSING_LABEL` — `payload.label` blank
  - `LABEL_TOO_LONG` — `payload.label` over 80 chars (response
    includes `max_length`)
  - `INVALID_LABEL` — slug derivation yielded empty (label has no
    ASCII letters/digits)
  - `INVALID_POSITION` — `payload.position` not parseable as integer
  - `MISSING_ENTITY_CUSTOM_STAGE_ID` — required on update/delete

Note: `KEY_COLLIDES_WITH_SEEDED` was previously returned when
`payload.key` matched a seeded value. As of the override feature,
seeded-key adds are accepted and create an override row instead.

403.description: Tenant admin required for add/update/delete

404.description:
entity_custom_stage_id not found for this tenant (update/delete).
Canonical error shape with `error_code: NOT_FOUND`.

409.description:
Custom stage with that `(entity_type, key)` already exists for this
tenant AND is currently active. (If it exists but is soft-deleted,
add reactivates it instead — returns 200 with `reactivated: true`.)
Race protection via the unique index — surfaces here when two
concurrent add requests target the same active key.

post.description:
Enqueues a Celery job that synthesizes today's prioritized daily plan for
the authenticated user. Returns **immediately** with a `job_id`; poll
`GET /user/daily_plan/status` until `status=completed`.

### Preconditions
- `Tenant.daily_plan_enabled` must be `true` (returns `DAILY_PLAN_DISABLED_AT_TENANT` otherwise)
- `User.daily_plan_enabled` must be `true` (returns `DAILY_PLAN_DISABLED_FOR_USER` otherwise)

### Dedup + cache reuse
Two short-circuits prevent accidental LLM spend:
- **Processing job (<5 min)** — if a previous call is still in flight, the response
  carries `deduplicated: true` and reuses the existing `job_id`.
- **Completed plan (<4 hours)** — if today's plan completed less than 4 hours ago,
  the endpoint returns the cached result with `cached: true, status: "completed"`
  and a populated `pdf_url`. **No Celery job is enqueued and no LLM call happens.**
  Agent's upstream pipeline rarely changes fast enough to warrant a fresh synth
  within 4h — this is the main cost-control lever. After 4h the plan is stale
  and a fresh generation runs.
- **`force=true`** (query string or body) skips the 4-hour cache and starts a fresh generation.
  It does not skip the in-flight dedup.

### Synchronous work on the API side
Before returning, the endpoint:
1. Validates flags + dedup
2. Gathers `raw_context` (Mongo leads/contacts/tasks sync in a thread executor;
   calendar fetched via user OAuth as a Tornado coroutine — silent-fails if not connected)
3. Upserts `user_notifications` doc keyed on `userid + year+month+day`
4. Enqueues `daily_plan_tasks.generate_daily_plan` on the
   `background_scheduled_jobs_D` Celery queue

Wall-clock for the API round-trip is typically 1–2s (Mongo reads + calendar fetch).
The LLM synthesis takes an additional 30–60s in the worker.

### Example
```bash
curl -X POST https://ingress.ambivo.com/user/daily_plan/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AMBIVO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{}'
```

requestBody.description: The only body field read is `force`. Send `{}` otherwise.

get.description:
Returns the current state of today's daily plan for the authenticated user.
The doc is keyed on `userid + year+month+day` in the user's timezone.

Clients should poll this every 5–10s after `POST /user/daily_plan/generate`
until `status == "completed"`, then surface `pdf_url` (a presigned URL valid
for 60 days pointing at an HTML report in `gofer-temp` S3 bucket).

Pass `include_markdown=true` to also get the rendered markdown body (useful
for in-app rendering without fetching S3). Pass `include_raw_context=true`
for debugging — returns the exact Mongo-gathered context the LLM saw.

### Caching + retrieval model
MongoDB is the source of truth for the daily plan — **there is no Redis
cache in front**. The underlying `user_notifications` doc is keyed by
`{userid, year, month, day}` and written by:

1. `_maybe_autogen_daily_plan` on login (fire-and-forget `spawn_callback`).
2. Explicit `POST /user/daily_plan/generate` calls.
3. The Celery `generate_daily_plan` task on completion.

When `SmartDailyPlanAgent` handles a chat turn, it reads this same doc
directly (no Redis). If `daily_plan_status=="completed"` and
`daily_plan_dict` is populated, the agent runs the Q&A prompt against
that context — **no re-synthesis**, no duplicate LLM synthesis cost.
A single chat turn = one small Q&A LLM call (~500 in / ~100 out tokens).
The expensive synthesis (~3-4K tokens) runs at most once per 4-hour
`COMPLETED_REUSE_WINDOW_SECONDS` window per user per day.

### Response shape optimization (future scale concern)
The stored doc contains `daily_plan_markdown` (≈30 KB of rendered HTML).
At single-user scale this is fine, but under heavy chat traffic consider
projecting only the fields the caller needs —
`{daily_plan_status, daily_plan_dict, daily_plan_generated_ts,
daily_plan_pdf_url, daily_plan_job_id, daily_plan_error,
daily_plan_quality_score}` — and skip `daily_plan_markdown` unless
`include_markdown=true`. Most Q&A turns answer from `daily_plan_dict`
alone; only synth-time prompts need the markdown. Savings ≈25 KB wire
+ deserialization per chat turn. Not implemented today — flag for when
Mongo bandwidth or chat latency surface as a bottleneck.

### Example
```bash
curl "https://ingress.ambivo.com/user/daily_plan/status?include_markdown=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AMBIVO_TOKEN"
```

parameters.name: include_raw_context

- `not_generated` — no job has been kicked off yet today
- `processing` — Celery task is running
- `completed` — plan is ready; `pdf_url` and `daily_plan_dict` are populated

Presigned S3 URL to the HTML report. Empty until `status=completed`.
Valid for ~60 days. Despite the field name, the file is actually HTML

the Celery image.

below that the worker triggers a refinement pass. A recorded `0.7` with

the assess pass hit max_tokens and returned unparseable JSON (fallback).

With `result` 0, the lookup error: `IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED` or `LOOKUP_FAILED`.

post.description:
Called hourly by Celery beat (`admin_routine_tasks.daily_plan_morning_sweep`) through
the service-auth contract (`X-AMBIVO-INTERNAL-SECRET` + `X-AMBIVO-TENANT-ID`); a
superadmin JWT also works. Any other caller gets `403 SUPERADMIN_REQUIRED`.

Picks every user with `daily_plan_enabled=true` (in a tenant with
`daily_plan_enabled=true`, not marked for deletion, `account_type=0`) whose local
hour is 7 and whose `user_notifications` doc for their local today is not already
`completed` or `processing`. Responds at once; gathering and queueing continue in
the background, each LLM job delayed 0-60s at random. Idempotent — a repeated call in the same
hour finds those users already `processing` and skips them.

post.summary: Fan out daily-plan generation across tenant users (admin-only)
post.description:
Enqueues a SINGLE Celery dispatcher task. The dispatcher (in Celery) loops
over target users and enqueues per-user `generate_daily_plan` jobs with a
small stagger (2s) to avoid hammering Anthropic.

### AuthZ
- Standard Bearer JWT, AND
- `user.is_tenant_admin(tenant)` must be true. Non-admins receive `403`.

### Target selection
- Omit `userid_list` (or send `null`) → dispatcher fans out to **ALL** users
  in the caller's tenant where `daily_plan_enabled=true`.
- Supply `userid_list` → intersected with enabled users in the tenant
  (authz boundary — cross-tenant ids are silently dropped).

### Batch mode differences vs self-serve
- Celery gathers Mongo context itself; **calendar is SKIPPED** (no user OAuth token in Celery).
- `crm_host` is threaded through the payload so deep-links still render.

### Examples
All enabled users in tenant:
```bash
curl -X POST https://goferapi.ambivo.com/admin/daily_plan/batch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AMBIVO_ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{}'
```

Specific users:
```bash
curl -X POST https://goferapi.ambivo.com/admin/daily_plan/batch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AMBIVO_ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"userid_list": ["5b23c83842e02e5b677d34dc", "5c91..."]}'
```

userid_list.description:
Optional. When omitted or null, fan out to all users in the tenant
with `daily_plan_enabled=true`. Max 500 ids per batch.

post.summary: Run a multi-source synthesis query (sync or SSE streaming)
post.description:
Submits a natural-language query for multi-source synthesis and returns
either a single prose answer (when `streaming: "false"`) or a
`text/event-stream` of progress chunks (when `streaming: "true"`).

**Sync mode (`streaming: "false"`):** the connection is held open until
synthesis completes. Subject to the upstream gateway's ~120 second HTTP
idle cutoff — queries that exceed this return **504 Gateway Timeout**.
Use streaming or async for anything likely to run longer.

**Streaming mode (`streaming: "true"`):** returns SSE. Each event is a
JSON object: `{type, text, sub_type, metadata}`. Heartbeat events with
`metadata.heartbeat == true` fire every 20 seconds to keep proxy idle
timers happy. See the Knowledge Synthesis tag description for the full
wire format.

For long queries (> 60 s) from server-to-server callers or mobile
clients that can't reliably hold SSE connections, prefer
`/kh/chat/async` instead.

post.summary: Submit a synthesis query as a background job
post.description:
Enqueues a synthesis job that runs in a Celery worker and returns a
`job_id` immediately (typically under 3 seconds). Clients poll
`GET /kh/chat/async/{job_id}` until `status` becomes `done`, `failed`,
or `cancelled`.

Because execution is decoupled from the HTTP request, this path has no
practical upper bound on wall-clock — the Redis job state has a 1-hour
TTL which is generous for any realistic synthesis run (typical 90–180 s).

This is the default recommended path for CRM integrations: mobile
clients don't lose state on backgrounding, server-side batch jobs don't
get killed by gateway idle timeouts, and the UI gets a natural
"check progress" affordance.

**KB opt-in.** To include the tenant's knowledge base collections in
the synthesis, supply `session_metadata.available_knowledge_bases` with
a list of Qdrant collection names. Without this field, synthesis
consults only the web (search + scraper) — the "our KB + web" story
works only when the caller names the collections explicitly.

O(log N) with no keyspace scans.

parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of statuses to filter by.
Example: `status=done,running`

parameters.description: Max summaries to return (default 50, max 200)

Verified 2026-09-08: POST https://ingress.ambivo.com/kh/chat answers 404 while POST https://vectordbapi.ambivo.com/kh/chat answers 401 — the route exists on one host and not the other. get.summary: Poll a synthesis job's current state and (when done) its result
get.description:
Single Redis lookup — typically returns in under 100 ms regardless of
whether the job is pending, running, or done. Recommended poll cadence
is every 3–5 seconds; typical synthesis runs complete in 90–180 s.

When `status == done` the response body includes the synthesized
`answer` plus routing metadata, conversation summary, and session info.
When `status` is `failed` or `cancelled` the `error` field is populated.

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: The `job_id` returned by the submit endpoint

200.description: Job state (any status — clients inspect the `status` field)

value.answer: Recent advances in quantum error correction focus on surface codes...

404.description: Job not found or expired (Redis TTL is 1 hour)

post.summary: Cancel a pending or running synthesis job
post.description:
Revokes the Celery task (SIGTERM) if it's currently running, or
removes it from the queue if it hasn't been picked up yet. Transitions
the job state to `cancelled` with `error: "cancelled by user"` and
`completed_at` set to the cancellation time.

**Ownership is enforced server-side:** the authenticated user/tenant
must match the job's owner. Cross-tenant cancellation returns `403`
even with a valid JWT.

**Terminal states cannot be cancelled** — attempting to cancel a job
whose status is already `done`, `failed`, or `cancelled` returns `409`.

403.description:
Authenticated user does not own this job. Enforced against the
`user_id + tenant_id` stored with the job in Redis.

409.description: Job is already in a terminal state (done/failed/cancelled)

get.summary: Poll a research job's status via ambivo_api proxy
get.description:
Thin auth'd proxy to `vectordbapi /pgv/research/{job_id}`. Returns the
upstream body verbatim so chat UIs can rely on the same schema the
`SmartResearchAgent` consumes.

Used by the multi-turn research flow: after `/agent/chat` returns
`status: "action_required"` with `action_required.poll.endpoint`
pointing at this route, the client polls here every ~15 seconds
until `status == "completed"` (or `"failed"`), up to a 20-minute
hard cap.

The frontend only needs the user's ambivo_api JWT — the proxy
forwards it to vectordbapi which enforces ownership (`user_id` +
`tenant_id` claims must match the job's owner).

### Example
```bash
curl "https://ingress.ambivo.com/user/research/status/research_1776129076_6c597c64" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AMBIVO_TOKEN"
```

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: Research job id returned by `SmartResearchAgent` via `action_required.job_id`.

200.description: Job state retrieved (running, completed, or failed — `status` field distinguishes)

stages.description: Map of stage-name to `{status, started_at, completed_at, metrics}` (when `running` / `completed`).

artifacts.description: Present when `status=completed`. S3-presigned URLs for downloadable deliverables.

sources.description: Canonicalized, credibility-checked list of sources actually consulted (see knowledge_synthesis.md).

403.description: Job is not owned by this user/tenant

404.description: Job id unknown or expired (state is cached with a 1-hour TTL upstream)
