post.description:
Cancels a running or queued research job. Proxies to
`vectordbapi POST /pgv/research/{job_id}/cancel`. Ownership is
enforced server-side: the authenticated user+tenant claims must
match the job's owner.

Jobs already in a terminal state (`done` / `failed` / `cancelled`)
return HTTP 409.

### Example
```bash
curl -X POST "https://ingress.ambivo.com/user/research/cancel/research_1776129076_6c597c64" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AMBIVO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{}'
```

schema.description: Empty body accepted. Reserved for future cancellation reason field.

200.description: Cancellation accepted — job state updated to `cancelled`

403.description: Job is not owned by this user/tenant

409.description: Job is already in a terminal state (`done` / `failed` / `cancelled`) and cannot be cancelled

post.summary: Create a CTA, or render a dynamic link from one (optionally shortened)
post.description:
Dispatches on `req_body["action"]`:

- `"add"` (default, if `action` is omitted) — creates a new CTA.
- `"generate_dynamic_link"` — renders a personalized URL from either an
  explicit `cta_link` template OR by deriving a template from an
  existing CTA record (`cta_id`). When `shorten=true`, a `link-redirect`
  CTA is also persisted (or reused, deduped on
  `(tenant_id, final_url)`) and `short_link` / `short_cta_id` are
  returned alongside `url_link`.

Any other `action` value, including a typo or `"update"`, creates a CTA.

### Query-string encoding (`encoding_mode`)
- `x_state` (default): the rendered query string is replaced by one
  parameter, named by `state_param_name` (default `x_state`). Its value is
  base64 of a JSON object holding every query field. `X_type` and `X_id`
  are added when the entity type and id are known.
- `per_field`: each query-string value is base64-encoded on its own.

`generate_dynamic_link` returns `{}` with no `result` when the template
cannot be resolved (unknown `cta_id`, no `cta_link`) or `instance_payload` is empty.

### Template derivation (when `cta_link` is absent)
- `cta_type="widget"`: template is built from `cta.url` plus
  `cta.mapping_dict` — e.g. `cta.url="http://google.com"` with
  `mapping_dict={"email":"lead.email","name":"lead.fullName"}` becomes
  `http://google.com?email={{lead.email}}&name={{lead.fullName}}`.
- Any other `cta_type`: `cta.url` is used verbatim as the template.

### Example
```bash
curl -X POST https://ingress.ambivo.com/cta/manage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AMBIVO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "action": "generate_dynamic_link",
    "cta_id": "63d3a08e84ffa858f320fb2b",
    "instance_payload": {"lead": {"email": "a@b.com", "fullName": "John"}},
    "shorten": true
  }'
```

generate_dynamic_link_from_cta.summary: Derive template from a widget CTA, with short-link

generate_dynamic_link_stateless.summary: Render from an explicit cta_link template (no short-link)

generate_dynamic_link_per_field.summary: Base64-encode each query value on its own

add_cta.summary: Create a CTA (default action when "action" is omitted)

get.summary: List the share links the current user created
get.description:
Scoped to the caller's own links, unlike `/entity/shortcode/share-list`,
which answers "who has THIS entity been shared with".

Dashboard shares live in a separate store and are folded in here, so
asking for `entity_type=dashboard` reads only that store and omitting
`entity_type` reads both.

Items are the stored link records, newest first, up to 100. The code is in
`code`. There is no `url`; the public path is `/entity/shortcode/{code}`.

post.summary: Create a public share link for an entity
post.description:
Mints a short, unguessable code that lets a third party read one record —
or a filtered set — with **no login**. The code IS the capability, so
everything that limits it lives on the link: expiry, an access count, an
optional access code, and revocation.

Two modes:

- **Single entity** — send `entity_id`.
- **Filter** — send `match_filter_dict` to share every record matching it.
  For `file` and `folder`, filter mode is for tenant admins only. Anyone
  else gets `SHARE_FILTER_NOT_ALLOWED`.

Guest accounts cannot share a `file` or `folder` (`GUEST_CANNOT_PUBLISH`).

Works for standard types (`file`, `folder`, `lead`, `contact`, `account`,
`opportunity`, `order`, `invoice`, `product`, `marketing_source`,
`user_task`, `custom_status`, `dashboard`, `questionnaire`,
`installed_base`, `purchase_order`, `work_shift`, `shift_assignment`,
`punch_event`, `attendance_day`, `inventory_item`, `inventory_lot`,
`vendor_price_agreement`, `purchase_requisition`,
`purchase_requisition_line`, `goods_receipt`, `inventory_count_session`)
and for any Custom Module collection, which is read from the separate
custom database. Any other name is looked up as a Custom Module and fails
with `COLLECTION_NOT_FOUND`.

Errors are sent with HTTP 200, `result: 2` and an `error_code`:
`MISSING_ENTITY_TYPE`, `MISSING_ENTITY_REFERENCE`, `INVALID_FILTER`,
`UNSUPPORTED_ENTITY_TYPE`, `COLLECTION_NOT_FOUND`, `COLLECTION_ACCESS_DENIED`,
`SHARE_FILTER_NOT_ALLOWED`, `GUEST_CANNOT_PUBLISH`, `ENTITY_ACCESS_DENIED`,
`ENTITY_ACCESS_CHECK_FAILED`, `ENTITY_VALIDATION_ERROR`, `ENTITY_NOT_FOUND`,
`INVALID_QUESTIONNAIRE_MODE`, `INVALID_ACCESS_CODE`, `INVALID_WHITELIST_IPS`,
`CODE_GENERATION_FAILED`, `INSERT_FAILED`, `SERVER_ERROR`.

entity_type.description: A standard type or a Custom Module collection name.

match_filter_dict.description: Share every record matching this filter instead of one record. For `file` and `folder`, only a tenant admin may use it.

questionnaire_mode.description: `questionnaire` only. `review` is read-only. `collect` turns on the public `/answers`, `/draft` and `/upload` routes for this link.

lock_after_submit.description: `collect` only. After a submit, the link is read-only until the owner unlocks it with bulk-manage `unlock`.

access_code.description: Six alphanumeric characters (A-Z, 0-9), case-insensitive. Omit to leave the link openly accessible to anyone holding the URL.

get.summary: Read a shared entity (public, no authentication)
get.description:
**Public.** No bearer token; the code is the credential.

Every request runs the same gate sequence: not found, revoked, expired,
access count exhausted, access code, IP allow-list, creator access. A
protected link needs `access_code` on the query string.

A failed gate is sent with HTTP 200, `result: 2` and an `error_code`:
`SHORTCODE_NOT_FOUND`, `SHORTCODE_REVOKED`, `SHORTCODE_EXPIRED`,
`MAX_ACCESSES_EXCEEDED`, `ACCESS_CODE_REQUIRED`, `IP_NOT_WHITELISTED`,
`SHARE_REVOKED_*` or `ENTITY_NOT_FOUND`. A wrong access code is HTTP 401
with `ACCESS_CODE_INVALID`.

parameters.name: access_code
parameters.description: Required when the link was created with one.

parameters.name: subfolder_id
parameters.description: Folder shares only — read one subfolder.

200.description: The shared record, or the matching set. A failed gate also returns 200 with `result: 2`.

post.description:
**Public.** Valid only when the link shares a questionnaire created in
**collect mode**.

Responses land in the separate `questionnaire_response` collection and
**never touch the canonical answer collection or its approval pipeline** —
a public respondent cannot write into reviewed data.

Runs the same gate as the public read, then three more: the entity must be
a questionnaire, its mode must be `collect`, and the link must not be
locked.

Evidence files are uploaded first via `/upload`; attach the returned ids to
an answer as `attachment_file_ids`.

Errors are sent with HTTP 200, `result: 2` and an `error_code`. Beyond the
gate codes of the public read: `NOT_A_QUESTIONNAIRE`, `COLLECTION_NOT_ENABLED`
(link not in `collect` mode), `QUESTIONNAIRE_LOCKED`, `RESPONSE_LOCKED`,
`INVALID_BODY`, `MISSING_RESPONDENT`, `NO_ANSWERS`, `INVALID_ANSWER`,
`QUESTION_NOT_IN_QUESTIONNAIRE`, `INVALID_OPTION`, `SIGNATURE_REQUIRED`.

signature.description: Required when the questionnaire or the link requires a signature.

put.summary: Save partial answers for later (public, no authentication)
put.description:
**Public.** Save-for-later on a collect-mode share, so a respondent — or
the author pre-filling — can stop and resume by reopening the same link.

One draft per link, upserted. Deliberately **partial**: the respondent's
name and email are optional, an empty answer set is allowed, and
conditional gating is not applied, because the point is to store exactly
what was typed.

It does **not** count as a submission and never overwrites an
already-submitted response.

Answers whose `question_id` is not in the questionnaire are dropped
without an error.

Errors are sent with HTTP 200, `result: 2` and an `error_code`: the gate codes
of `/answers`, `INVALID_BODY`, or `ALREADY_SUBMITTED`.

post.summary: Upload an evidence file (public, no authentication)
post.description:
**Public**, and the only unauthenticated write that accepts a file — so the
limits are part of the contract rather than an implementation detail:

- **25 MB** per file, **10 files per share link**, and a fixed extension
  allow-list.
- Files are stored **privately in the share owner's tenant**, reachable
  only by presigned URL and never public-read.
- Tracked in `shortcode_upload` with `source=public_shortcode` for the
  per-link cap and later antivirus and review.

Attach the returned `file_id` to an answer as `attachment_file_ids` on the
subsequent submit.

Errors are sent with HTTP 200, `result: 2` and an `error_code`: the gate codes
of `/answers`, `UPLOAD_LIMIT_REACHED`, `NO_FILE`, `EMPTY_FILE`, `FILE_TOO_LARGE`,
`FILE_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`, `OWNER_UNRESOLVED`, `SERVER_ERROR`.

file.description: One file per request. If several are sent under `file`, only the first is stored.

error_code.description: Present with `result: 2` (gate failure, too large, wrong type, or the per-link cap is reached).

delete.description: Only the link's creator or a tenant admin may revoke it.

401.description: Not the creator, and not a tenant admin

get.summary: Who this entity has been shared with
get.description: Tenant-scoped, and creator-scoped for non-admins: a non-admin sees the links they created.

200.description: The links created for that entity

post.summary: Manage an entity's share links — one, several, or all
post.description:
Omitting `codes` applies the action to **every** link for that entity.

Auth mirrors share-list: authenticated, tenant-scoped, creator-scoped for
non-admins.

The actions differ in what survives, which is the whole point of having
both `deactivate` and `delete`:

- **`deactivate`** — links stop working (`SHORTCODE_REVOKED`) but the
  records are **kept**, so the audit trail (recipient, views) survives.
- **`delete`** — removes the link records, their access logs and any
  in-progress drafts, but **keeps submitted responses**: they stay under
  the questionnaire. A purge of the links, not of the answers.
- **`lock` / `unlock`** — re-lock or reopen a lock-after-submit link for
  one more edit.
- **`extend`** — moves expiry to now + `expires_in_hours` (1 hour to 2
  years). Revives an expired link **in place**, so the recipient can use
  the URL they already hold with nothing re-sent. It does not reactivate a
  deactivated link; that stays an explicit choice.
- **`set_access_code` / `clear_access_code`** — adds, replaces or removes
  the code while keeping the URL the recipient already has. Normalised to
  uppercase and validated exactly as on create, so a code accepted here is
  always one the public read will accept.

**Note the hyphen.** This path is hyphenated so the public
`/entity/shortcode/{code}` route, whose code pattern is alphanumeric only,
cannot capture it.

codes.description: Omit or leave empty to apply to ALL links for the entity. Send an array. A string is ignored, so the action runs on every link. `clear_access_code` requires a non-empty array (`CODES_REQUIRED`).

get.summary: Who opened a share link, when, and whether it worked
get.description: Paginated. Failed attempts are recorded too, with their `error_code` — a run of `SHORTCODE_EXPIRED` against one link is a recipient still trying, not an attack, and the two are only distinguishable if both are logged.

parameters.name: success
parameters.description: Filter to successful or failed accesses.

get.summary: Chart config, aggregation and picklists for any entity
get.description:
Three GET actions are spec'd here:

- **`action=picklist`** returns rows for a dropdown. See "Picklists" below.

- **`action=chart_config`** — returns the field catalog (groupable / aggregate /
  date fields), supported time grains, sensible defaults, and one-click
  chart presets for the entity.
- **`action=aggregate`** — runs a Mongo aggregation in one of two modes:
    - **Group-by** mode: pass `group_by_fields` (+ optional `aggregate_field`).
    - **Time-bucket** mode: pass `date_field` + `time_grain` (+ optional
      `aggregate_field`). Mutually exclusive with group-by mode.

Other actions on this endpoint (`get`, `export`, `get_entity_ids`) are
documented in `docs/entity_data.md` and not yet in this spec.

**Picklists.** `action=picklist` takes `match_filter_dict`, `search_text`,
`sort_dict`, `page_num` and `page_size`. A non-admin may send
`tenant_scope=true` to list every record in the tenant. The answer is
`{result: 1, data: {<key>: [...], total_count}, gross_count, msg_list}`.
`data.total_count` is the rows on this page. `gross_count` is every
matching row, counted on page 1 only.

**Inventory and procurement picklists.** For `inventory_item`, `inventory_txn`, `inventory_lot`, `inventory_count_session`, `inventory_count_line`, `inventory_forecast`, `purchase_order`, `purchase_requisition`, `vendor_price_agreement` and `goods_receipt`, the
picklist is read through the entity's own service. The response shape is
the same. The differences:

- The caller needs `R` on the module (`purchase_order` for orders).
  Without it the answer is `result: 2` with the service's
  `NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_<MODULE>` code and the message "You cannot view
  this list."
- `tenant_scope` is ignored. The service decides what the caller sees.
- `page_size` defaults to 1000 and is at most 1000.
- A failed read answers `INVENTORY_READ_FAILED` (inventory types) or
  `PROCUREMENT_READ_FAILED` (procurement types), never an empty list.
- To look up rows by id, send `match_filter_dict={"_id": {"$in": [...]}}`.
  Each id is a bare 24-character hex id or `"ObjectId('<hex id>')"`.
  `id` and `<entity_type>_id` are read as `_id`.

**Filters that are refused.** On GET and POST, a `match_filter_dict` that
contains `$where`, `$function` or `$accumulator` at any depth answers
`result: 2`, `error_code: INVALID_DATA`, message "This filter is not
allowed." `$expr` is allowed.

**Filters about the caller.** A saved filter cannot name the signed-in
user, so `match_filter_dict` takes three keys that are expanded for
whoever is asking (GET and POST, every entity type). Send `true` to
apply one; `false` drops it.

| key | becomes |
|---|---|
| `is_mine` | `userid` is the caller |
| `awaiting_my_approval` | `purchase_requisition` and `purchase_order` only: `approval_status: pending` and the CURRENT step (`seq == current_approval_seq`) is pending and lists the caller in `approver_userids`. Later steps of a chain are stored pending too and do not count. Ignored on other types. |
| `in_my_sites` | `site_code` is one of the sites on the caller's roles (`open_assignment_group_code`). No sites: nothing matches. |

The current-step test is an `$expr`. A caller's own `$expr` is kept and
joined with `$and`. Procurement's role cards are saved filters built on
these keys (Procurement Shape brief, question 30).

Inventory and procurement record types carry `name` and
`<entity_type>_id` on each row. `name` joins these parts with ` · ` and
skips blank ones:

| entity_type | `name` is built from |
|---|---|
| `inventory_item` | product name (or SKU), `site_code`, `location_code`, `bin_code` |
| `inventory_txn` | product name, `txn_type`, `qty`, `uom` |
| `inventory_lot` | `lot_number`, product name, `expiry_date` |
| `inventory_count_session` | name (or code), `count_date` |
| `inventory_count_line` | product name, `location_code`, session name |
| `inventory_forecast` | product name (or SKU), `site_code`, `period_key` |
| `purchase_requisition` | `requisition_number`, `name` |
| `vendor_price_agreement` | `agreement_number` (or `name`), product name (or SKU) |
| `goods_receipt` | `receipt_number`, `po_number`, `receipt_date` |
| `purchase_order` | the order's own `name` |

`<key>` is the entity type (for example `inventory_item`) when
`use_native` is true, the default. It is `values` when `use_native` is
false, and always `values` for `purchase_order`.

**Fixed lists.** These types have no records behind them. They answer
`action=picklist` only, and need no `tenant_scope`. The rows are under
`data.values`, and `data.total_count` equals `gross_count`.

| entity_type | `match_filter_dict` keys | Row fields |
|---|---|---|
| `inventory_uom` | `dimension` (`count`, `weight`, `volume`, `length`) | `code`, `label`, `dimension`, `precision`, `is_pack` |
| `inventory_item_type` | none | `code`, `label`, `description`, `example`, `dimensions` |
| `inventory_txn_type` | `hand_entry` (bool) | `code`, `label`, `description`, `action`, `source_type`, `inbound`, `signed_by_caller`, `reason_required`, `moves_to_another_place` |
| `inventory_txn_source_type` | none | `code`, `label`, `books_owns_it` |
| `inventory_txn_reason` | `txn_action`, `txn_type_code` | `code`, `label`, `is_waste` |
| `site` | `include_inactive` (bool) | `code`, `name`, `is_primary`, `is_active` |

`site` returns inactive sites too, unless `include_inactive` is `false`.
Its `data` also carries `codes_enforced`. It is false when the tenant has
no registered sites, and then any site code is accepted.

Any other action on a fixed list, GET or POST, answers `result: 2` with
`error_code: INVALID_DATA` and the message "This list supports
action=picklist only". `POST` with `action=picklist` answers the same code
with the message "Use GET for this list. It supports action=picklist only".
A fixed list that fails to build answers `result: 2`, `error: server_error`.

**Time-bucket mode notes:**
- Bucket boundaries are tenant-tz aware (`user.timeZone` → `tenant.timeZone` → `UTC`).
- The resolved timezone is echoed back in the response.
- Records where `date_field` is null or non-`date` typed are silently excluded.
- `total_value` / `avg_value` / `max_value` / `min_value` are returned only
  when `aggregate_field` is a real numeric field (not `_count`).

parameters.name: entity_type
parameters.description:
Entity type to operate on. The last six are fixed lists and answer
`action=picklist` only. The listed types are the ones this spec covers.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Which action to perform.

parameters.name: group_by_fields
parameters.description:
JSON-encoded array of field names for group-by mode (e.g. `["stage"]` or `["stage","userid"]`).
Required when `action=aggregate` and `date_field` is not provided.

parameters.name: aggregate_field
parameters.description:
Numeric field to sum/avg/min/max alongside count. Pass `_count` (or omit) for
count-only output. Must be one of the entity's `aggregate_fields` (see chart_config).

parameters.name: date_field
parameters.description:
Date field to bucket on for time-bucket mode. Must be one of the entity's
declared `date_fields` (see chart_config). MUST be paired with `time_grain`.

parameters.name: time_grain
parameters.description: Time grain for bucketing. MUST be paired with `date_field`.

parameters.name: match_filter_dict
parameters.description:
JSON-encoded MongoDB-style filter. On `aggregate` it applies before
aggregation. On a fixed-list picklist only the keys listed above are read.

parameters.name: search_text
parameters.description: `picklist`. Text search over the records.

parameters.name: tenant_scope
parameters.description: `picklist`. `true` lists every record in the tenant, not only the caller's. Ignored for the inventory and procurement types and the fixed lists.

parameters.name: use_native
parameters.description: `picklist`. `false` puts the rows under `data.values`.

parameters.name: sort_dict
parameters.description:
JSON-encoded sort dict. Defaults to `{"count": -1}` for group-by mode and
`{"_id.year": 1, ...}` (chronological) for time-bucket mode.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Rows per page. On `aggregate` it applies after aggregation.

parameters.name: page_num
parameters.description: 1-based page number. On `aggregate` it applies after aggregation.

200.description:
Action-specific response. `chart_config` returns the catalog; `aggregate`
returns the bucketed data array.

value.message: When using time-bucket aggregation, both date_field and time_grain must be provided.
'made_up_field' not a valid date_field for opportunity. Allowed: ['agreement_signed_date','close_date','expected_close_date','last_touchpoint_ts','renewal_date','timestamp']

500.description:
Server error. The handler logs full traceback via `self.logger.exception()`
and returns a generic envelope.

example.message: An error occurred processing the request.

post.summary: Batch retrieval, aggregate report, and user_status_values upsert
post.description:
A `match_filter_dict` that contains `$where`, `$function` or
`$accumulator` at any depth answers `result: 2`, `error_code:
INVALID_DATA`, message "This filter is not allowed." `$expr` is allowed.

POST on `/entity/data` supports three actions. `action` defaults to `upsert`. **Do NOT use this
endpoint for CREATE or DELETE operations** — those have cascading impacts
on related entities (activities, comments, attachments, linked records)
that are handled by the entity-specific endpoints (e.g. `POST
/product/manage_product` with `action=delete`).

**Supported POST actions:**
- `get_entity_ids` — Retrieve a batch of records by explicit id list.
  Requires `entity_ids` (array). Optional: `match_filter_dict`,
  `sort_dict`, `use_native` (default `true`), `export_settings`.
  Tenant scoping is always applied (`tenant_id` from the caller's
  token); non-superadmins cannot override it via `match_filter_dict`.
- `upsert` — Upsert a record. Only supported when
  `entity_type == "user_status_values"`.
- `aggregate_report` — Render an HTML or PDF report combining a
  group-by (or time-bucket) aggregation with an optional tabular
  records section. Optionally uploads to S3 and returns a presigned
  URL ready to drop into an email or share link. Designed for
  workflow automation (Schedule → Entity → Email) but also usable
  interactively. See `EntityDataAggregateReportRequest` /
  `EntityDataAggregateReportSuccess` schemas for the exact shape.

Any other action value returns `error = "unsupported_action"` with a
message that names the supported actions and points at the entity-
specific endpoint for CREATE/DELETE.

entity_type.description:
For `get_entity_ids`, one of the supported entities
(lead, contact, order, account, opportunity, invoice,
product, marketing_source, custom_status, task, folder,
file, plaid_item, bill, payment, vendor). For `upsert`,
must be `user_status_values`.

entity_ids.description: Required for `get_entity_ids`. Rejected (with `invalid_request`) if empty or missing.

match_filter_dict.description: Extra filter applied on top of the id list. `_id` keys are ignored (the entity_ids filter is preserved); `tenant_id` is ignored unless the caller is a superadmin.

use_native.description: When true (default) and the entity supports `to_native_response`, records are serialized in the native response shape under the entity's native response key; otherwise falls back to `toJSON()`.

export_settings.description:
Optional `{"export_to": "csv" | "json"}` — when set, records are
written to file and the response returns `export_url` +
`export_msg` instead of inline values.

payload.description:
Required for `action=upsert` (user_status_values document to
upsert, matched on `{tenant_id, value}`).

POST /entity/data does not support action='delete_many'. Supported POST actions: ['get_entity_ids', 'upsert', 'aggregate_report']. For CREATE or DELETE, use the entity-specific endpoint (e.g. POST /product/manage_product with action='delete').

and removes the team id from `applied_team_ids`. Every current team

get.summary: Read the company's own AI setup (admin)
get.description:
The signed-in admin's own company. No secrets: provider names only, the
server address and request format, and whether a gateway key is stored.

**Auth (every `/user/admin/genai/providers` route):** Bearer JWT of an
admin of the company (`is_tenant_admin`) or Ambivo staff (superadmin).
Anyone else: 403 `NOT_TENANT_ADMIN`. The company is always the caller's
own; no route takes a tenant id. A company that is not fully approved
gets 403 with the sentence "Account Review Pending before this feature
is enabled" as `error_code`.

200.description: The setup, or the error envelope

403.description: Not an admin of this company (`NOT_TENANT_ADMIN`)

put.summary: Save the company's own provider keys or its own AI server (admin)
put.description:
Send exactly one of `providers` or `custom_endpoint`.

The first save creates the company's config set at the Ambivo LLM
gateway (`tenant-<tenant_id>`, bound to the tenant) and mints its
gateway key, which Core stores encrypted. The key's scopes are every
provider this page can set, so a provider added later works with it.
Later saves add or replace only the providers sent and keep the stored
gateway key. A provider sent as `null` is removed; the last one cannot
be (use DELETE). Choosing keys removes a saved server from the config
set, and choosing a server removes saved keys.

Every save clears `last_test`. **Saving does not switch the company
over**; PATCH does that.

`endpoint_url` must be `https://` with a public host (DNS checked) and
no login, `?` or `#` (`GENAI_INVALID_ENDPOINT_URL`); the gateway checks
it again. It is required on the first server save and optional after.

Provider keys and the server token go to the gateway only. Core never
stores, logs or returns them.

Errors: `GENAI_BAD_REQUEST`, `GENAI_INVALID_ENDPOINT_URL`,
`GENAI_ADMIN_NOT_CONFIGURED` (the server has no gateway admin token),
`GENAI_GATEWAY_MANAGED_BY_AMBIVO` (staff set the company up on another
gateway), `GENAI_GATEWAY_REFUSED` (with `data.gateway_detail`),
`GENAI_GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE`, `GENAI_SETUP_BUSY`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

providers.description: Provider name to its key, or `null` to remove that provider.

bearer_token.description: Sent by the gateway as `Authorization: Bearer`. An empty string keeps the saved token; it does not clear it.

default_model.description: The model name the gateway sends when the call names none. Most inference APIs need one; OpenAI's answers 400 without it.

response_map.description: Dotted paths to the reply fields. Keys text, input_tokens, output_tokens, finish_reason.

timeout_seconds.description: Core's gateway client gives up at 90 s.

200.description: The saved setup, or the error envelope

403.description: Not an admin of this company (`NOT_TENANT_ADMIN`)

patch.summary: Switch the company to its own AI, or back to Ambivo's keys (admin)
patch.description:
`{"enabled": true}` sets the company's `genai_via_gateway` to its config
set id and `genai_gateway_url` to the Ambivo gateway. It needs a stored
gateway key (`GENAI_SETUP_MISSING`) and a passing test since the last
save (`GENAI_TEST_NOT_PASSED`). From the next AI call on, the company's
AI uses its own setup and is not billed by Ambivo.

`{"enabled": false}` clears both fields: AI uses Ambivo's keys again.
The setup and the stored key are kept.

These are the only routes a company admin can use to set those two
fields. `update/tenant` still drops them for anyone but staff.

Errors: `GENAI_BAD_REQUEST`, `GENAI_SETUP_MISSING`,
`GENAI_TEST_NOT_PASSED`, `GENAI_GATEWAY_MANAGED_BY_AMBIVO`,
`INTERNAL_ERROR`.

200.description: The setup after the switch, or the error envelope

403.description: Not an admin of this company (`NOT_TENANT_ADMIN`)

delete.summary: Remove the company's own AI setup (admin)
delete.description:
In order: the company switches back to Ambivo's keys; every saved key
or server is removed from the config set at the gateway; the gateway key
is revoked at the gateway and deleted from Core. The empty config set is
kept, so its usage history stays. A later PUT reuses it and mints a new
gateway key.

If a gateway step fails the reply is an error, the company stays on
Ambivo's keys, and the stored key is kept so the DELETE can be retried.

Errors: `GENAI_ADMIN_NOT_CONFIGURED`, `GENAI_GATEWAY_MANAGED_BY_AMBIVO`,
`GENAI_GATEWAY_REFUSED`, `GENAI_GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE`, `GENAI_SETUP_BUSY`,
`INTERNAL_ERROR`.

200.description: The empty setup, or the error envelope

403.description: Not an admin of this company (`NOT_TENANT_ADMIN`)

post.summary: Test the company's saved AI setup with one small completion (admin)
post.description:
No body. Works whether or not the company is switched over. The call
goes exactly as a real one: Core mints a 5-minute `llm_gateway` token
for the signed-in admin and sends the stored gateway key to the gateway.
Not billed by Ambivo. The result is stored as `last_test`, which
PATCH `{"enabled": true}` requires.

Failure codes: `GENAI_SETUP_MISSING` (nothing saved),
`GENAI_TENANT_KEY_FAILED` (the gateway refused the key), `GENAI_GATEWAY_POLICY_REFUSED`
(a guardrail or routing rule refused it), `GENAI_GATEWAY_LIMIT` (usage cap or
monthly budget reached), `GENAI_GATEWAY_BUSY` (429), `GENAI_PROVIDER_ERROR`
(other 4xx), `GENAI_GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE` (unreachable, timeout, 3xx/5xx, or no
provider answered), `GENAI_GATEWAY_NOT_PROVISIONED`,
`GENAI_GATEWAY_NEEDS_USER`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`. `data.gateway_detail` is
the gateway's own reason.

403.description: Not an admin of this company (`NOT_TENANT_ADMIN`)

post.summary: Test one saved provider key at the gateway (admin)
post.description:
No body. The gateway makes a 1-token call with the stored key
(admin API `POST /admin/config-sets/{id}/providers/{provider}/test`).
Does not change `last_test`. A dead key is a result: `result` 1 with
`ok` false, a plain `message` and the gateway's reason (secrets cut
out) in `gateway_detail`.

Errors: `NOT_TENANT_ADMIN` (403), `GENAI_BAD_REQUEST` (provider not
saved for this company), `GENAI_SETUP_MISSING`, `GENAI_ADMIN_NOT_CONFIGURED`,
`GENAI_GATEWAY_REFUSED`, `GENAI_GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE`.

200.description: Test result, or the error envelope

message.description: Empty when ok. A plain sentence when not.

403.description: Not an admin of this company (`NOT_TENANT_ADMIN`)

get.summary: Read the company's AI routing, guardrails and budget (admin)
get.description:
Merges the config set entry (`optimize_routing`), its routing rules, its
guardrails and this month's spend against its budget, from the LLM
gateway admin API. Conversation memory is not part of this reply.
`GENAI_SETUP_MISSING` until the company has saved provider keys or a server.
If only the budget read fails, the reply still succeeds with both
budget fields null. A failed routing or guardrails read fails the call.

200.description: The settings, or the error envelope

403.description: Not an admin of this company (`NOT_TENANT_ADMIN`)

put.description:
Every field is checked in Core first (`GENAI_BAD_REQUEST`, the message
names the setting in plain words). At most 50 rules. Takes the company's
setup lock (`GENAI_SETUP_BUSY`) and is audited on the company's record.
Replies with the full settings.

Core calls only the gateway route whose part changed: the rules
(PUT routing-rules) first, then `optimize_routing` (POST routing). If
the rules saved and the `optimize_routing` call then failed, the error
(`GENAI_GATEWAY_REFUSED` or `GENAI_GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE`) says the rules
were saved and the switch was not, and the rules save is audited.

Errors: `GENAI_BAD_REQUEST`, `GENAI_SETUP_MISSING`, `GENAI_SETUP_BUSY`,
`GENAI_ADMIN_NOT_CONFIGURED`, `GENAI_GATEWAY_MANAGED_BY_AMBIVO` (staff
set the company up on another gateway), `GENAI_GATEWAY_REFUSED` (with
`data.gateway_detail`, secrets removed), `GENAI_GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE`.

200.description: The settings, or the error envelope

403.description: Not an admin of this company (`NOT_TENANT_ADMIN`)

put.description:
The whole set; a field left out is cleared. Checked in Core first
(`GENAI_BAD_REQUEST`). Locked and audited like routing. Replies with
the full settings.

Errors: `GENAI_BAD_REQUEST`, `GENAI_SETUP_MISSING`, `GENAI_SETUP_BUSY`,
`GENAI_ADMIN_NOT_CONFIGURED`, `GENAI_GATEWAY_MANAGED_BY_AMBIVO`,
`GENAI_GATEWAY_REFUSED` (with `data.gateway_detail`, secrets removed),
`GENAI_GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE`.

200.description: The settings, or the error envelope

403.description: Not an admin of this company (`NOT_TENANT_ADMIN`)

put.summary: Set the company's monthly AI budget (admin)
put.description:
`monthly_budget_usd` from 0.01 to 1,000,000,000 (rounded to cents), or
0 or null for no limit (stored as null). Anything between 0 and 0.01,
above 1,000,000,000, or too large to be a number is `GENAI_BAD_REQUEST`.
Locked and audited. Replies with the full settings.

Errors: `GENAI_BAD_REQUEST`, `GENAI_SETUP_MISSING`, `GENAI_SETUP_BUSY`,
`GENAI_ADMIN_NOT_CONFIGURED`, `GENAI_GATEWAY_MANAGED_BY_AMBIVO`,
`GENAI_GATEWAY_REFUSED` (with `data.gateway_detail`, secrets removed),
`GENAI_GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE`.

200.description: The settings, or the error envelope

403.description: Not an admin of this company (`NOT_TENANT_ADMIN`)

post.summary: Test a tenant's LLM gateway setup with one small completion (staff only)
post.description:
Internal secret only (`X-AMBIVO-INTERNAL-SECRET` + `X-AMBIVO-TENANT-ID`,
optional `X-AMBIVO-USER-ID`). A signed-in user's JWT gets 403
`INTERNAL_ONLY`.

Sends one completion to a gateway exactly as a real call does: Core
mints the 5-minute `llm_gateway` token for the acting user (else the
tenant's first admin) and sends the key as `X-Key-Access-Code`. The
tenant does not need to be switched to its own keys. Nothing is billed;
one `genai_call_log` row is written.

`key_access_code` tests a key before it is stored; without it the
tenant's stored key is used. `gateway_url` defaults to the tenant's
`genai_gateway_url`, else `https://llm-gateway.ambivo.com`, and is
checked like a real call (https, public host). Any other `gateway_url`
is accepted only together with `key_access_code`, so a stored key only
ever goes to the tenant's own address or Ambivo's gateway. The reason in
`gateway_detail` has secrets removed.

On failure `gateway_detail` carries the gateway's own reason, for
example "This key_access_code belongs to another tenant".

key_access_code.description: kac_live_... to test; default the tenant's stored key

prompt.default: Reply with the single word: ok

max_tokens.description: Values outside 1-1024 are clamped to that range.

403.description: Called with a JWT (`INTERNAL_ONLY`)

post.summary: One AI completion, on the tenant's keys or Ambivo's
post.description:
The single door for AI calls from outside Core. Routing follows the
tenant's `genai_via_gateway` setting:

- **Empty (default):** Ambivo's provider keys. Token quota is enforced
  first; usage is billed (`tenant_token_billing_events`, `source:
  genai_complete`, with `caller`).
- **Set:** the tenant's own provider keys (or its own inference
  endpoint) through the LLM gateway at the tenant's
  `genai_gateway_url`, using the tenant's gateway key. A missing address
  or key is `GENAI_GATEWAY_NOT_PROVISIONED`. Not billed by Ambivo. A refused key fails the call with
  `GENAI_TENANT_KEY_FAILED`; a guardrail or routing rule refusal is
  `GENAI_GATEWAY_POLICY_REFUSED`; a reached usage cap or monthly budget is
  `GENAI_GATEWAY_LIMIT`. Core sends no model name on this path, so the
  company's default model and routing apply. A gateway that is down,
  times out or answers 3xx/5xx is `GENAI_GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE`; one at its
  rate limit (429) is `GENAI_GATEWAY_BUSY`; another 4xx is
  `GENAI_PROVIDER_ERROR`. Ambivo's keys are never used in its place.
  `update/tenant` sets `genai_via_gateway` and `genai_gateway_url` for
  Ambivo staff (superadmin) only, and drops them from anyone else;
  tenant creation ignores them. A company admin sets them through
  `/user/admin/genai/providers` (PUT, test, then PATCH). The address must be `https://` with a
  public host and no login, `?` or `#`. It is checked on save
  (`INVALID_GENAI_GATEWAY_URL`) and again, with a DNS lookup, before
  each call. A refused address is `GENAI_GATEWAY_NOT_PROVISIONED`.
  Redirects from the gateway are not followed.

**Structured output:** send `output_schema` (JSON Schema). The reply is
parsed (code fences and surrounding prose tolerated) and validated. If it
does not match, the model is asked again once with the errors. Check
`schema_valid`; `usage` covers both attempts. A schema that uses
`pattern` or `patternProperties` anywhere is refused with
`GENAI_BAD_REQUEST` before any provider call. A property may still be
named `pattern`.

**Time limit:** a request, re-ask included, stops after 110 s (before the 120 s load-balancer and proxy limits) with
`GENAI_TIMEOUT`.

**Guests** (`TYPE_GUEST`) are refused this route.

**Dual authentication:** a Bearer JWT, or `X-AMBIVO-INTERNAL-SECRET` +
`X-AMBIVO-TENANT-ID` (+ optional `X-AMBIVO-USER-ID`) for services. The
gateway path never forwards the caller's token: Core mints a 5-minute
token (`typ: llm_gateway`, refused by Core's own routes) for the acting
user, so service callers work too. The acting user must belong to the
tenant, or the call fails with `GENAI_GATEWAY_NEEDS_USER`.

The handler answers HTTP 200 with the standard envelope. The checks in
front of it answer with `result: 2` and a non-200 status: 401
`INVALID_INTERNAL_SECRET`; 400 `MISSING_TENANT_HEADER` or
`UNKNOWN_TENANT`; 500 `NO_ACTING_USER`; and 403 for a tenant that is not
fully approved, whose `error_code` is the sentence "Account Review
Pending before this feature is enabled".

parameters.name: X-AMBIVO-TENANT-ID
parameters.description: Required with `X-AMBIVO-INTERNAL-SECRET`.

parameters.name: X-AMBIVO-USER-ID
parameters.description: Acting user for audit, service path only.

content.description: Text, or a list of `{type:"text", text}` blocks. Blocks of any other type are dropped.

max_tokens.description: Above 16000 is cut to 16000. 0 or missing means 1024.

output_schema.description: JSON Schema the reply must match.

caller.description: Who asked, for usage reports. e.g. `workflow:<workflow_id>:<node_id>`.

messages.content: Invoice INV-7 from Acme Supplies. 2 x Widget at 10.00, 1 x Gadget at 5.50. Total 25.50.

200.description: Completion, or a refusal in the envelope

401.description: Wrong internal secret, or no valid JWT

get.summary: Tenant usage report (with optional shareable HTML artifact)
get.description:
Returns a comprehensive usage report for the caller's tenant: per-month GenAI token usage, record/storage metrics, computed quota limits, and a structured `usage_vs_limits` breakdown. **Tenant-admin or superadmin only** (non-admins get `403`).

**Bank Connections are retired** — the `bank_items` row has been removed from `usage_vs_limits` (replaced by `fin_connections`, Financial Connections). No other row shape changed.

When `generate_report=true`, the endpoint also renders a self-contained HTML report (inline styling + SVG cost-trend/forecast charts, plus the new eSign and PDL enrichment dimensions), uploads it to the temp bucket under `<tenant_id>/usage_report_<timestamp>_<uuid8>.html`, and returns a durable **public** URL as `report_url`. The object is world-readable at an unguessable key and is auto-expired by the bucket lifecycle (~800 days), so the link is good for ~1 year. Default `GET` (no flag) is JSON-only and performs no S3 write. All dollar figures in the report are **shadow / projected**, never invoiced.

parameters.name: generate_report
parameters.description: When `true`, generate + upload the HTML artifact and include `report_url` in the response. When omitted/`false`, return JSON only (no S3 write).

generated_at.description: UTC timestamp the report was generated.

report_url.description: Public URL of the generated HTML report. Present only when `generate_report=true`. Empty string if generation failed (the JSON payload is still returned).

reports.description: One entry for the caller's tenant.

record_metrics.description: Actual record counts per entity type.

quota_limits.description: Computed plan limits. `-1` = unlimited, `-2` = token-metered (managed by TokenQuotaManager).

usage_vs_limits.description: Per-dimension `{usage, limit, label}` map for UI display. The `bank_items` key has been removed; `fin_connections` (Financial Connections) replaces it.

403.description: Caller is not a tenant admin / superadmin.

500.description: Failed to generate the usage report.

post.summary: Create a card payment from a public widget
post.description:
Used by the public appointment widget to take a guest's card payment.
No user login. The `Authorization: Bearer <public_session_id>` header
carries one of the tenant's public session ids.

**On the tenant's connected account.** Send
`on_behalf_of: "for_connect_account"`, or
`action: "create_connect_account_direct_charge"`. The server finds or
creates the Stripe customer on the connected account by email. It then
creates the payment intent there. `payment_method_types` defaults to
`["card"]`.

The payment intent's Stripe metadata carries `site_code` and
`ambivo_source`. `ambivo_source` is `appointment_widget` when
`widget_type` is `appointment`, and otherwise the `widget_type` sent.
Stripe copies this metadata onto the charge. The Stripe Connect webhook
reads it to record the payment in Core and post it to Books. The site's
company (`tenant.site_list[].books_entity_id`) decides which company's
books it lands in. No site means the tenant's default company.

**Without a connected account flag.** The charge is made to the tenant's
own billing customer. Other body fields go to Stripe as sent. The
`site_code` and `ambivo_source` metadata are not set on this path.

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `INVALID_TENANT` | the bearer value is not a public session id of any tenant |
| `TENANT_HAS_NO_CONNECTED_ACCOUNT` | a connected account charge, and the tenant has none |
| `INVALID_CUSTOMER_OR_COULD_NOT_CREATE_CUSTOMER` | no Stripe customer could be found or created |
| `PAYMENT_INTENT_CREATE_FAILED` | Stripe raised an error |
| `TENANT_BILLING_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND` | the tenant has no billing profile |

action.description: `create_connect_account_direct_charge` charges on the connected account, as `on_behalf_of` does.

amount.description: Amount in the smallest currency unit, for example cents.

currency.description: Defaults to the currency of the tenant's Stripe billing customer, then to the tenant's currency.

customer.description: The person paying. Without `address.postal_code` the server answers HTTP 500.

email.description: Used to find the Stripe customer and to send the Stripe receipt.

on_behalf_of.description: Charge on the tenant's connected Stripe account.

payment_method_types.description: Defaults to `["card"]` on a connected account charge.

automatic_payment_methods.description: Passed to Stripe on the tenant's own billing path only. The connected account path does not read it.

application_fee_amount.description: Connected account charges only. Dropped on the other path.

transaction_session_id.description: Stored in the payment intent's Stripe metadata.

is_debug.description: Stripe test mode. Send `false` for a live charge. Any other value, or none, uses test mode.

site_code.description: The site the guest is paying. Kept only if it is a site set up for the tenant, and otherwise ignored. The payment is filed to that site's company.

widget_type.description: Which widget sent the payment. Stored as `ambivo_source` in the Stripe metadata. Cut to 40 characters.

200.description: `result: 1` with the Stripe result in `data`. A failure is also HTTP 200, with `result: 2`, and `error_code` when the server named the cause. Some Stripe failures return only `{result: 2, message: ""}`.

data.description: The Stripe response, including `payment_intent` on success.

get.summary: List all Ambivo platform Stripe products with their prices
get.description:
Returns the full product catalog for the Ambivo **platform** Stripe account, each product with its list of active prices. This is the platform billing account only — it deliberately does **not** include Stripe Connect / connected-account products.

Intended for internal and third-party service consumers, so it is authenticated by the shared internal secret (`X-AMBIVO-INTERNAL-SECRET`) rather than a user JWT: there is no tenant context. When no internal secret is configured on the server, every caller gets 401.

Read-only. Backed by Stripe `Product.list` + `Price.list` (active only, up to 100 each) against the platform secret key.

parameters.name: is_debug
parameters.description: When `true`, reads the Stripe **test-mode** catalog. Omitted or `false` (default) reads the **live** catalog — third-party consumers typically want live production prices.

200.description: Catalog retrieved (`result: 1`). Note: per the platform-wide convention, business-level failures are also returned with HTTP 200 and `result: 2` plus an `error_code`.

has_more.description: Present when Stripe paginated the product list (more than the 100-item page limit exists).

product.description: Stripe product objects, each augmented with a `price` array of its active Stripe price objects.

price.description: Active Stripe price objects for this product.

unit_amount.description: Price amount in the smallest currency unit (e.g. cents).

401.description: Missing or invalid `X-AMBIVO-INTERNAL-SECRET` header, or no internal secret configured on the server.

get.description: Paginated list of commission structures (plans) for the tenant. Access follows the `commission_structure` R privilege. Standard CRM paging via `page_size` / `page_num` / `match_filter_dict` / `sort_dict`.

parameters.name: commission_structure_id
parameters.description: Fetch a single structure by id.

parameters.description: JSON-encoded Mongo filter.

post.description: Create a plan. `commission_type` is one of `straight`, `tiered`, `cumulative_tiered`, `salary_plus` (partial), `gross_margin` (partial). `tiers`/`margin_tiers` are lists of `{threshold,rate}` / `{margin_threshold,rate}`. Requires `commission_structure` C.

patch.description: Update a plan. Body: `{ commission_structure_id, payload:{...} }`. A payload that changes nothing returns a bare `result: 2`. Requires `commission_structure` U.

delete.description: Delete one (`action=delete` + `commission_structure_id`) or many (`action=delete_many` + `commission_structure_ids`). Deleting a structure cascades to its agent assignments. Requires `commission_structure` D.

parameters.name: commission_structure_ids
parameters.description: Stringified id list, e.g. "['a','b']".

get.description: Paginated list of agent→structure assignments (which agent is on which plan, optionally time-boxed). Requires `commission_structure` R.

post.summary: Assign an agent to a commission structure
post.description: Bind an agent (`agent_id` = userid) to a plan (`commission_structure_id`), with optional `effective_date_ts`/`expiry_date_ts` epoch bounds. Requires `commission_structure` C.

patch.description: Body: `{ commission_agent_structure_id, payload:{...} }`. A payload that changes nothing returns a bare `result: 2`. Requires `commission_structure` U.

delete.description: Delete one or many (`action=delete_many` + `commission_agent_structure_ids`). Requires `commission_structure` D.

get.description: Paginated list of booked `commission` records (per order line, per agent). Requires `commission` R.

post.description: Calculate a commission for an order line using the agent's active structure. Persists a `commission` record only when `persist_data` is not "false" AND all of `agent_id`, `sales_order_line_id`, `order_id` are present — otherwise it is a preview. `sale_date` is required for `cumulative_tiered`; `cost_amount` for `gross_margin`. Requires `commission` C.

order_amount.description: Amount the commission is computed on.

sale_date.description: ISO string or epoch; required for cumulative_tiered.

patch.description: Body: `{ commission_id, payload:{...} }`. Supplying `commission_amount` sets `manually_entered=true`. A payload that changes nothing returns a bare `result: 2`. Requires `commission` U.

delete.description: Delete one or many (`action=delete_many` + `commission_ids`). Requires `commission` D.

get.description: Totals each agent's commissions over a date window. The source is the commission splits on order lines (`order_line_list.commissions_list`). Records booked with POST or PATCH `/sales/commission` are not counted. Returns JSON inline by default, or a downloadable file (S3 presigned URL) when `format=csv|xlsx|pdf`. Non-admin callers are pinned to their own commissions (IDOR guard). The date filter defaults to the order line's `fulfillment_date`. Requires `commission` R. Validation errors return 400; other failures return 500.

parameters.name: start_ts
parameters.description: Window start, epoch seconds. Default: end_ts − 90 days.

parameters.name: end_ts
parameters.description: Window end, epoch seconds. Default: now.

parameters.name: agent_id
parameters.description: Restrict to one agent (ignored/overridden to self for non-admins).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Accepted and ignored.

parameters.name: date_field
parameters.description: `fulfillment_date` is the order line date; `timestamp` is the order creation time. Other values return 400 INVALID_DATE_FIELD.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: CSV only. `false` leaves out the per-order-line block.

200.description: Report payload (JSON) or a link to the generated CSV/PDF.

get.description: Export all commission structures for the tenant to a downloadable file (S3 presigned URL). `tiers`/`margin_tiers` are emitted as JSON strings that round-trip on import. Requires `commission_structure` R.

post.description: Bulk create/update commission structures. Body accepts either `rows` (array of objects) or `csv_text` (raw CSV). A row with a valid tenant-owned `commission_structure_id` is updated, else created. Bad rows fail in isolation (max 5000 rows). Requires `commission_structure` C.

get.description: Export all agent→structure assignments, with resolved agent name/email and structure name alongside the raw ids (human-readable + round-trips on import). Requires `commission_structure` R.

post.description: Bulk create/update assignments. Body accepts `rows` or `csv_text`. `agent_id` may be a raw id or resolved from `agent_email`/`agent_name`; `commission_structure_id` from `commission_structure_name`. Supplied ids are validated to belong to the tenant. Bad rows fail in isolation (max 5000 rows). Requires `commission_structure` C.

post.summary: Auto-book commissions from an order's lines (non-destructive)
post.description: Mirror the order's line commission splits (``order_line_list.commissions_list``) into ``commission`` records so the commission-by-agent report reflects all orders. Keyed by (tenant, order, sales_order_line_id, agent). **Non-destructive:** inserts missing rows and refreshes only its own untouched auto-bookings; never overwrites a manually-entered amount, an advanced-status (approved/paid/disputed) commission, or a commission booked by a real user. Idempotent. Callable internally (the ``commission_booking_default`` workflow on ``order.update``) or via user JWT.

post.summary: Reconcile order commissions into QuickBooks vendor bills
post.description: Per-salesperson, create/update/cancel a vendor **Bill** (A/P) for the order's commissions in Ambivo and QuickBooks, dated to the order's fulfillment date. Idempotent by (order, salesperson). No tenant flag gates it. The QuickBooks expense account is found by name in the tenant's own chart; without one, only the Ambivo Bill is written. Callable internally (workflow on `order.update`) or via user JWT. Returns 200 with a per-salesperson summary even for non-QB tenants or zero commissions. `result: 1` can still mean nothing was billed: check `error_code: NO_FULFILLMENT_DATE`, `summary.reason: already_running`, or detail outcomes such as `skipped_pre_golive`. Non-200 only for auth, order-not-found or a server error.

post.summary: Create / update / delete / get installed-base records
post.description: CRUD for the Installed Base entity. Writes stamp the owner and coalesce the FX block. Every row is shared with the team; `payload.access_dict` is not saved. Reporting (grid, charts, aggregate, export) is also available via `/entity/data` with `entity_type=installed_base`. Send dates as epoch seconds. A date that cannot be parsed is saved as 0.

200.description: Success. add/update return {data: InstalledBase}. delete returns {data: [{deleted, installed_base_id}]}, one entry per id. A non-owner gets `deleted: false`. get returns {installed_base:[...], total_count}.

post.summary: Access-scoped text search over installed-base records

200.description: {data:{installed_base:[{id, installed_base_id, name, status, direction, end_date}], total_count}}.

post.description: Idempotent, self-healing date-range scan over installed_base. Per active/ expiring record: fires reminders at each threshold before expiry (default 90/60/30/15 days, deduped), flips active→expiring inside the notice window (opening a renewal task both directions; a renewal opportunity for sold; a draft PurchaseOrder for purchased records flagged requires_purchase_order), and marks lapsed records expired. Internal service-to-service; invoked nightly by celery beat, not the app scheduler.

tenant_id.description: Sweep a single tenant (default all tenants). An unknown id returns result 1 with tenants_processed 0.

dry_run.description: Compute + return counts without writing. Send a JSON boolean. Any non-empty string, even "false", is a dry run.

post.summary: Create / update / delete / get purchase orders
post.description:
Deprecated. Kept for inventory mobile <= 1.1.0 (RETIRE-AFTER-INVENTORY-MOBILE-1.2). Use the verb routes in the procurement spec: `POST /user/purchase_order`, `GET`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /user/purchase_order/{id}`, `GET /user/purchase_order/list` and `GET /user/purchase_order/kanban`.

CRUD for the buy-side PurchaseOrder entity. Reporting via `/entity/data` with `entity_type=purchase_order`. Approval is a separate endpoint. A save cannot set `approved`, `rejected`, `received` or `billed`, and an order that has received goods or has a bill cannot go back to draft (`PURCHASE_ORDER_STAGE_NOT_SETTABLE`). `delete` refuses an order with a bill, received goods or a receipt that is not cancelled (`PURCHASE_ORDER_HAS_BILL_OR_RECEIPTS`). The approval chain is set by the server (`PURCHASE_ORDER_APPROVAL_CHAIN_NOT_SETTABLE`). The full rules are in the procurement spec. On `add`, `data.warnings` (a list of strings) is present only when the company sent differs from the company of the order's site. The order is saved as sent.

200.description: add/update return {data: PurchaseOrder}. delete returns {data: [...]}, one result per id; a non-owner gets `deleted: false`. get and get_entity_ids return {purchase_order:[...], total_count}.

post.summary: Approve or reject a purchase order (single-state gate or multi-approver chain)
post.description:
Deprecated. Kept for inventory mobile <= 1.1.0 (RETIRE-AFTER-INVENTORY-MOBILE-1.2). Use `PATCH /user/purchase_order/{id}/approval`.

Only an order in stage pending_approval can be approved or rejected. Any other stage gets 400 PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_AWAITING_APPROVAL, "This purchase order is not waiting for approval." A repeat Approve on an approved order still returns `already: true`.

Single-state (no approval_steps): transitions approval_status pending → approved/rejected and stage pending_approval → approved/rejected.

Multi-approver (approval_steps present): the caller must be an approver on the CURRENT step (or a tenant admin) — otherwise 400 NOT_AN_APPROVER. Approving advances to the next pending step; the PO is fully approved only once every step approves. Any rejection rejects the whole PO. The response also carries acted_step_seq / next_approval_seq / steps_remaining.

The caller needs the `purchase_order` U module privilege, and must be able to write the record. Tenant admins pass the privilege check.

approve.description: Send `false` to reject. Only false, 0 and "no" reject; any other value, even "reject" or null, approves.

400.description: PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_FOUND_OR_NO_ACCESS, NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_PURCHASE_ORDER (no `purchase_order` U privilege), SELF_APPROVAL_NOT_ALLOWED, PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_AWAITING_APPROVAL, NOT_AN_APPROVER (caller is not an approver on the current step), or PURCHASE_ORDER_NO_PENDING_APPROVAL_STEP.

post.summary: Settle an approved purchase order to a vendor Bill (accounts payable)
post.description:
Deprecated. Kept for inventory mobile <= 1.1.0 (RETIRE-AFTER-INVENTORY-MOBILE-1.2). Use `POST /user/purchase_order/{id}/bill`.

Closes the buy-side renewal loop: turns an approved PurchaseOrder into a vendor Bill that flows through the existing bill / vendor_payment infrastructure ("pay before expiry"). Maps po_line_list → Bill line_list, copies vendor (account_id), total_amount, currency, and needed_by_date → Bill due_date, and stamps meta.purchase_order_id / meta.installed_base_id on the Bill. On success the PO moves to stage `billed` and is stamped with bill_id / bill_number / is_bill_interfaced / bill_interface_ts.

**Gate:** the PO must have cleared approval — stage must be one of `approved`, `ordered`, `received`, `billed`. draft / pending_approval / rejected / cancelled return 400. A blanket PO is never billed.

**Idempotent:** a PO already carrying a live bill returns that bill untouched (`already: true`) and never mints a second payable.

The Bill opens in `stage` (default `draft`). Promoting it to `pending` / `paid` via `/user/bill/manage` is what drives Books/QuickBooks sync — that is deliberately not done here. A bill created here with `stage: paid` is not synced to Books.

stage.description: Initial Bill stage. Send one of the listed values. Any other value becomes draft.

200.description: {data:{purchase_order_id, bill_id, bill: Bill, stage: "billed", created: 1}}; on a re-call, {data:{bill_id, already: true, created: 0}}.

created.description: 1 when a bill was created, 0 when returning an existing one.

already.description: true when the PO was already billed.

raced.description: true when a concurrent create_bill won the race (unique index BillPurchaseOrderUnique) and this call adopted the winner's bill.

400.description: PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_APPROVED (stage has not cleared approval), PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_BILLABLE (rejected/cancelled), BLANKET_PURCHASE_ORDER_IS_NOT_BILLABLE, or PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_FOUND_OR_NO_ACCESS.

post.description: Deprecated. Kept for inventory mobile <= 1.1.0 (RETIRE-AFTER-INVENTORY-MOBILE-1.2). Use `GET /entity/data?entity_type=purchase_order&action=picklist`.

200.description: {data:{purchase_order:[{id, purchase_order_id, name, po_number, stage, approval_status}], total_count}}.

get.description: Returns every board visible to the caller in one list: platform defaults (`tenant_id: "-1"`, `is_default: true`), the tenant's shared boards, and the caller's own private boards. The list rides at the top level of the response (not under `data`).

post.description: Creates a new board owned by the caller's tenant. `visibility: "private"` stamps the caller as `owner_userid`; a user can never create a platform default.

patch.description: Updates a board identified by `dashboard_id` in the body. A platform default is read-only (superadmin only); a private board is editable only by its owner — otherwise the server returns `DASHBOARD_READONLY` / `DASHBOARD_FORBIDDEN`.

200 (error).description: `{result:2, error_code}` — DASHBOARD_NOT_FOUND, DASHBOARD_READONLY, DASHBOARD_FORBIDDEN, INVALID_DASHBOARD_ID, INVALID_VISIBILITY, or MISSING_DASHBOARD_ID.

delete.description: Deletes boards by `dashboard_id` (single) or `dashboard_ids` (JSON array). Each id the caller may not delete is reported inline rather than failing the batch. Defaults and other users' private boards are refused.

parameters.name: dashboard_id
parameters.description: A single board id to delete.

parameters.name: dashboard_ids
parameters.description: JSON array of board ids, e.g. ["id1","id2"].
